meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting October 21, 2013
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 21, 2013 meeting, Durham celebrated national recognition from ICMA, the Public Technology Institute, and Livability's top-100 ranking before holding a contentious public hearing on the draft Durham Traffic Separation Study (TSS). Downtown business leaders, Durham Area Designers, Durham County's Deputy Manager, and neighborhood advocates strongly opposed the study's proposed railroad crossing closures and concrete underpass walls, prompting Council to refer public comments back to staff 5-0 without endorsing specific closures and to request short-term recommendations. Council also approved the consent agenda 6-0 and a pulled liability claims settlement authority item 5-0 after resident Dorothy Crumb used the pull to air grievances over an unrelated cell-tower dispute.

agenda_items.title: Food Day Proclamation, ICMA and PTI National Awards, and Livability Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell proclaimed October 24, 2013 as Food Day, and City Manager Tom Bonfield and Strategic Initiatives Manager Jay Reinstein presented Durham's ICMA Certificate of Excellence and Public Technology Institute Citizen-Engaged Community awards. Mayor Bell noted Durham's #4 national Livability ranking, Council Member Steve Schewel reported results of the five-mile city employee trail challenge, and Council approved a 6-0 routine motion before priority items.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 3-6, 12)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda, covering a DPAC deed of trust release and extension, a utility extension agreement with Helen M. Allison for 7227 Fayetteville Road, a floodplain mapping MOA with NC/FEMA, Southview land purchase for watershed protection and community park development, and designation of an NLC voting delegate. Item 2 was pulled by Dorothy Crumb.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Durham Traffic Separation Study (TSS)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Mark Ahrendsen and Kimley-Horn consultant Matt West presented the two-year draft Traffic Separation Study covering 18 at-grade rail crossings and 12 long-term grade separation or closure recommendations. Ten speakers—including DDI, Durham Area Designers, property owner Doug Osborne, Deputy County Manager Lee Worsley, Gwen Silver, and James Chavis—criticized crossing closures (especially Dillard, Plum, Ramseur, and Blackwell) and massive concrete retaining walls. Council members agreed not to endorse specific closures and referred the comments back to staff while asking for short-term improvements.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Liability Claims Settlement Authority Delegation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Dorothy Crumb pulled Item 2 to protest a two-year dispute before the Development Review Board and Board of Adjustment over a 120-foot concealed cell tower, alleging missing hearing recordings and planning bias. Mayor Bell clarified that her remarks were not relevant to the claims settlement authority resolution, and Council Member Don Moffitt moved approval of the staff recommendation.

votes.item_title: Procedural Motion Following Council Announcements
votes.notes: Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: At the conclusion of ceremonial proclamations, national award presentations, and Council Member Steve Schewel's remarks recognizing city employees who participated in his five-mile challenge run on the American Tobacco Trail, Council took up a routine motion that was moved and seconded prior to priority items. With Howard Clement III absent, the six present members voted 6-0 to approve the motion.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 3-6, 12; excluding pulled Item 2)
votes.notes: Item 2 pulled by resident Dorothy Crumb. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bill Bell read the consent agenda headings, including a DPAC premises release and deed-of-trust extension, a utility extension agreement for 7227 Fayetteville Road, a FEMA/North Carolina floodplain mapping MOA, a Southview watershed and community park land purchase, and designation of a National League of Cities voting delegate. Resident Dorothy Crumb requested that Item 2 (Liability Claims Settlement Authority Delegation) be pulled for discussion. Council approved the remainder of the consent agenda 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 9: Referral of Durham Traffic Separation Study (TSS) Comments Back to Staff
votes.notes: Referred public comments back to staff/study team with request for short-term project recommendations; Howard Clement III absent and Cora Cole-McFadden not present for vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Following an abbreviated presentation of the draft Traffic Separation Study by Transportation Director Mark Ahrendsen and consultant Matt West, ten speakers testified during the public hearing—largely opposing proposed road closures at Dillard, Plum, Ramseur, and Blackwell streets and warning that concrete underpasses and retaining walls would sever downtown neighborhoods and delay county EMS response. In council discussion, Eugene Brown questioned consultant value and expressed skepticism that state or federal rail funds would materialize given falling gas-tax revenues, while Steve Schewel urged entering downtown crossings into the new state freight scoring tier without committing to closures so Durham could pursue funding for rail and pedestrian safety. Don Moffitt and Diane Catotti stressed that the study was only a first step requiring deeper urban-design feasibility studies rather than an endorsement of closures. Mayor Bell described the draft as a 'straw man' to launch debate and moved to refer the comments back to staff with a request for short-term recommendations, passing 5-0.

votes.item_title: Item 2 (Pulled): Liability Claims Settlement Authority Delegation
votes.notes: Pulled by Dorothy Crumb; Howard Clement III absent and Cora Cole-McFadden not present for vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Resident Dorothy Crumb pulled Item 2 from the consent agenda, using her speaking time to criticize the Development Review Board and Board of Adjustment over a two-year dispute involving a 120-foot concealed cell tower, property values, a high-pressure gas line, and missing hearing audio. Mayor Bell interrupted to clarify that Item 2 dealt strictly with delegating liability claims settlement authority and was unrelated to cell towers, though Crumb acknowledged she wanted to place her concern on the record. Council Member Don Moffitt expressed sympathy for Crumb's frustration with cell-tower proceedings before moving approval of the staff resolution. Council approved Item 2 by a 5-0 vote.

disagreements.issue: Durham Traffic Separation Study (TSS) Grade Separations, Street Closures, and State Funding Strategy (Item 9)
disagreements.summary: Public urban-design advocates, county officials, and residents clashed with the draft Traffic Separation Study's crossing closure and concrete grade-separation proposals, while council members differed on the realism of state rail funding versus entering the NCDOT scoring pipeline.
disagreements.side_a_position: Reject proposed crossing closures and concrete retaining-wall grade separations, and question the viability of state rail funding.
side_a_arguments: Durham Area Designers (Dan Jewell, Randy Hester, Eric Hite, Robin Heeks) argued concrete channels and 12-foot retaining walls would recreate a physical barrier through downtown and destroy pedestrian connectivity.
Deputy County Manager Lee Worsley warned Dillard Street closure would harm county operations and EMS response times, while Gwen Silver and James Chavis warned of isolating East Durham.
Council Member Eugene Brown argued state transportation funding is shrinking due to fuel-efficient cars and predicted light rail and grade-separation funds would remain a low-priority footnote.
disagreements.side_b_position: Treat the draft study as an initial engineering 'straw man' and position downtown crossings for state freight-rail scoring without committing to street closures.
side_b_arguments: Future freight and commuter/light rail expansion requires planning now rather than leaving downtown crossings unprotected.

Entering the NCDOT statewide freight tier (40% of state transportation funding) is the only realistic funding stream for the shared rail corridor, while reserving final decisions on closures and urban design for crossing-by-crossing feasibility studies.
disagreements.resolution: Council voted 5-0 to refer public comments back to staff without endorsing long-term closures, requesting short-term safety recommendations.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Opened and presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden while Mayor Bill Bell was en route, the Durham City Council approved priority items including a closed-session consultation on two lawsuits (Triangle Grading and Paving v. City of Durham and Shana Associates LP v. City of Durham) and heard updates from the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority (9.2 million annual passengers) and the Durham Performing Arts Center oversight committee. On the Durham Housing Authority Board appointment—after one of two applicants withdrew—Council suspended the rules (5-0 after Eugene Brown arrived) and voted 4-1 to re-advertise the seat: four of the five members present favored seeking candidates with executive financial experience for a $30-$40 million agency, while one dissenting member (whose name was not announced on the unattributed voice vote) opposed disqualifying the sole applicant over experience/age rather than simply expanding the pool. Council also held a public-hearing preview on the Durham Traffic Separation Study, where Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Eugene Brown questioned endorsing long-term rail grade-separation closures before coordinating with downtown vision planning and clarifying uncertain NCDOT funding formulas. All other procedural votes—including priority items, rule suspension, setting the agenda, and closed session—passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: City Manager & City Attorney Priority Items (Traffic Separation Study & Litigation Closed Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (presentation on Item 9, the Durham Traffic Separation Study, and noting citizen speaker Timothy Ferry would not appear) and the City Attorney's request for closed session on Triangle Grading and Paving v. City of Durham and Shana Associates LP v. City of Durham.

agenda_items.title: Durham Housing Authority (DHA) Board of Commissioners Re-Advertisement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After one of two applicants for the Durham Housing Authority Board withdrew, a Council member moved to re-advertise the seat to attract candidates with experience overseeing a $30-$40 million agency, while a dissenting member opposed rejecting the remaining applicant on those grounds. Once Eugene Brown arrived to establish a five-member quorum, Council unanimously suspended the rules (5-0) and voted 4-1 to re-advertise the position.

agenda_items.title: Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority (RDU) & DPAC Annual Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: RDU leadership reported 9.2 million annual passengers, 400 daily arrivals and departures across nine airlines, Terminal 1 completion, DBE/MBE contractor inclusion, and minimal impact from the federal government shutdown on TSA operations. agenda_items.title: Durham Traffic Separation Study (TSS) Draft Recommendations

disagreements.issue: Re-Advertising Durham Housing Authority Board Seat vs. Evaluating Remaining Applicant
disagreements.summary: Following the withdrawal of one applicant for the Durham Housing Authority Board, Council split 4-1 on whether to re-advertise the seat due to concerns about executive experience.
disagreements.side_a_position: Re-advertise the DHA Board seat to seek candidates with executive management experience
side_a_arguments: The Durham Housing Authority operates as a $30-$40 million-per-year enterprise
Re-advertising allows Council to recruit applicants with experience running an organization of that scale
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose rejecting the sole remaining candidate over perceived age or experience rather than simply enlarging the pool
side_b_arguments: Durham should encourage 'young blood' on boards rather than screening out newer applicants
Expanding the applicant pool is acceptable, but rejecting the candidate on experience grounds is objectionable
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-1 by unattributed voice vote after suspending the rules (5-0) once Eugene Brown arrived.

disagreements.issue: Scope of Council Action on the Draft Durham Traffic Separation Study (TSS)
disagreements.summary: Council members questioned whether a future resolution on the Traffic Separation Study should endorse long-term rail grade-separation projects and street closures or only receive the report and endorse near-term priorities pending downtown planning.
disagreements.side_a_position: Limit formal endorsement to short- and mid-term improvements while treating long-term grade separations conceptually until coordinated with downtown planning and funding
side_a_arguments: Endorsing long-term street closures and pedestrian overpasses before the October 24 Downtown Vision Workshop and Urban Open Space Plan is premature
Grade separations heavily impact the urban environment and require separate public involvement and funding clarity amid shifting NCDOT formulas
disagreements.side_b_position: Endorse a prioritized project list so staff can pursue state and federal rail-corridor funding
side_b_arguments: Merely receiving the report without endorsing a priority list weakens Durham's competitive standing for NCDOT State Tier and federal funding
Endorsing the study's priority list still requires individual Council resolutions and public input before any street is actually closed
disagreements.resolution: Staff agreed to incorporate Council feedback after the October 21 public hearing and refine the proposed resolution language before returning in December.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting October 7, 2013
meetings.executive_summary: With Mayor Bill Bell and Council Member Howard Clement III absent, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presided over the five-member Durham City Council on October 7, 2013. Council issued four October awareness proclamations, referred the Holland Street closing indefinitely back to staff ahead of a community design charrette, and appointed and swore in Susan Austin to the Human Relations Commission. In business items, Council approved the consent agenda 5-0, amended the city's assessment relief policy to grant sewer assessment relief until connection for UDI CDC at 4601 Industry Lane (5-0), and approved the state-contract purchase of 22 police patrol vehicles (5-0) after addressing Victoria Peterson's questions on out-of-state procurement.

agenda_items.title: October Awareness Proclamations and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presented proclamations for National Arts and Humanities Month (with Durham Arts Council and Piedmont Laureate John Claude Bemis), Domestic Violence Awareness Month (Durham Crisis Response Center), Take a Loved One to the Doctor Day (Durham Diabetes Coalition), and Breast Cancer Awareness Month (Dale Mattioli and Sisters Network). Council Member Eugene Brown congratulated his nephew Ruffin Hall on being named Raleigh City Manager.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item: Referral of Street Closing (128 Linear Feet of Holland Street)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin requested that the Holland Street closing public hearing be referred indefinitely back to the administration while staff evaluated alternative options and hosted an on-site design charrette on October 22.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item: Human Relations Commission Appointment (Susan Austin)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted to approve the supplemental appointment of Susan Austin as the Mayor's appointee to the Human Relations Commission, and the City Clerk administered her oath of office.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-3, 6, 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden read the consent agenda, covering minutes, a Triangle Transit Board of Trustees appointment, the June 2013 Procurement Card Performance Audit, the August 2013 bid report, and an interlocal amendment for Durham County convenience center recycling services. Item 5 was pulled by Victoria Peterson.

agenda_items.title: Assessment Relief Policy Amendment and Mini Assessment Roll for Sewer Main on East Cornwallis Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works Director Marvin Williams recommended amending the Assessment Relief Policy to recognize pre-existing utility access as a criterion for relief until tap-on, and granting such relief for UDI Community Development Corporation's parcel at 4601 Industry Lane. Council Member Steve Schewel questioned how frontage fees are calculated and bundled both actions into a single motion.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: State Contract Purchase of 22 Police Patrol Vehicles
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Victoria Peterson pulled Item 5 to question awarding the vehicle contract to a South Carolina dealership rather than an in-state vendor and to ask whether the patrol cars included computers and cages. Budget staff and Fleet Director Joe Clark explained that the city legally tied into a valid North Carolina state contract for police-package Dodge Chargers (upfitted separately) and that Dodge Chargers offered lower lifecycle maintenance and fuel costs than Chevrolet Impalas.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Item: Indefinite Referral of Item 12 (128 Linear Feet of Holland Street Closing) to Administration
votes.notes: Bill Bell and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: As a priority item on behalf of the City Manager, Planning Director Steve Medlin requested that Council refer Item 12—the public hearing on closing 128 linear feet of Holland Street—back to the administration indefinitely rather than to a date certain. Medlin explained that during evaluation it became apparent that alternatives to a full street closure existed, and announced an October 22 on-site design charrette at 6:00 p.m. to gather neighborhood input before returning later in the fall. Council voted 5-0 to refer the item back to administration.

votes.item_title: Supplemental Item: Appointment of Susan Austin to Human Relations Commission
votes.notes: Mayor's appointee sworn in immediately after vote. Bill Bell and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved up a supplemental agenda item appointing Susan Austin as the Mayor's appointee to the Durham Human Relations Commission so she could be sworn in during the meeting. Following a motion and second, the five present council members approved the appointment 5-0. Austin immediately took the oath of office and pledged to learn quickly and work hard on the commission.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1-3, 6, 8; excluding pulled Item 5)
votes.notes: Item 5 pulled by resident Victoria Peterson. Bill Bell and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden read the remaining consent agenda headings, including approval of City Council minutes, a Triangle Transit Board of Trustees appointment, the June 2013 Procurement Card Performance Audit, the August 2013 bid report, and Amendment No. 1 to the interlocal agreement for recycling collection at Durham County convenience centers. Item 5 (state contract purchase of 22 police patrol vehicles) was pulled by resident Victoria Peterson. Council unanimously approved the remaining consent items 5-0.

votes.item_title: Item 11: Assessment Relief Policy Amendment & Sewer Main Assessment Relief for 4601 Industry Lane (East Cornwallis Road)
votes.notes: Bundled policy revision (adding pre-existing utility access as relief criterion) and UDI CDC assessment relief until future connection. Bill Bell and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Public Works Director Marvin Williams presented a two-part recommendation: first, amending the city's Assessment Relief Policy to include pre-existing access to a utility as a criterion for relief with future frontage fees due at prevailing rates upon connection; and second, finding that UDI Community Development Corporation's parcel at 4601 Industry Lane did not benefit from the East Cornwallis Road sewer main and granting relief until connection. Following the public hearing, Council Member Steve Schewel questioned how frontage charges are calculated by linear foot and confirmed with the City Attorney that the policy change had to precede the parcel relief. Schewel bundled both actions into one motion, which passed 5-0.

votes.item_title: Item 5 (Pulled): State Contract Purchase of 22 Police Patrol Vehicles
votes.notes: Pulled by resident Victoria Peterson. Bill Bell and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Resident Victoria Peterson pulled Item 5 to challenge awarding the purchase of 22 police patrol cars to a South Carolina dealership rather than a North Carolina firm and to ask whether the vehicles came equipped with computers and cages. Purchasing staff explained that the city was legally tying into an approved North Carolina state contract awarded to the South Carolina dealer, and Fleet Management Director Joe Clark confirmed the base police-package vehicles excluded computers, cages, and radios (procured separately) for all bidders. Council Member Don Moffitt noted that after the work session he had obtained a detailed lifecycle-cost comparison showing the Dodge Charger cost taxpayers less in maintenance and fuel over its service life than the Chevrolet Impala. Council approved the vehicle purchase 5-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Bill Bell, the Durham City Council addressed downtown public safety following a fatal incident near the Bull, heard Citizens Matters testimony from attorney David Hall alleging racial disparities in policing and proposing Racial Equity Institute training alongside tenant complaints from Timothy Ferry, and received a Durham Public Schools briefing detailing new state academic standards amid a projected $15 million annual state funding shortfall. Council suspended the rules and unanimously approved Item 7, a 10-year lease for the Office of Economic and Workforce Development at 807 East Main Street, while members raised questions about sewer assessment relief on East Cornwallis Road (Item 11) and property-rights/easement implications of closing 128 linear feet of Holland Street for the Hotel Durham development (Item 12). Public Works also presented a well-received update on the Failed and Struggling Developments program, reporting 90 projects across 26 subdivisions completed with minimal city expenditure ($13,000 plus $12,000 recoverable on Dunwoody). All formal votes—including priority items, an excused absence request for October 8 and 10, the Item 7 rule suspension and lease approval, setting the agenda, and closed session—passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: City Manager & City Attorney Priority Items and Downtown Incident Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority request to consider a 10-year OEWD lease at 807 East Main Street (Item 7) and the City Attorney's request for a closed session on Eric Daniel v. City of Durham and Hope Allen v. City of Durham. Council also shared condolences following a fatal incident near the Bull downtown and unanimously approved a member's excused absence request for October 8 and 10.

agenda_items.title: Tenant Lease Complaints & Policing/Racial Equity Institute Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Timothy Ferry urged Council to examine apartment lease enforcement and uncapped rent increases. Attorney David Hall recounted being shot in the back on June 22, criticized Chief Lopez's earlier remarks and traffic-stop racial disparities (>160% higher likelihood of being pulled over), and urged city adoption of Racial Equity Institute Phase 1 training, followed by comments on public-speaker sign-up transparency.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools (DPS) Presentation: New State Standards & Budget Shortfall
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS representatives briefed Council on the rollout of new K-12 state standards requiring constructed-response answers, online testing, and new teacher evaluation metrics while teachers learned and implemented the curriculum simultaneously. Responding to Council questions on General Assembly funding cuts, DPS reported a projected $15 million shortfall for the current fiscal year.

agenda_items.title: Ten-Year Lease for Office of Economic and Workforce Development (807 E. Main St.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed utilizing city-owned properties for neighborhood-based city functions to reduce future rental costs, then suspended the rules and unanimously approved Item 7, the 10-year lease with Edgemont Tenant LLC at 807 East Main Street.

agenda_items.title: East Cornwallis Sewer Assessments & Holland Street Closing (Hotel Durham)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council questioned staff on frontage/tap fee relief rules for the East Cornwallis Road sewer main assessment roll (Item 11). On Item 12 (closing 128 linear feet of Holland Street adjacent to the Hotel Durham site), members probed whether closing the street surrendered public rights, the 10-foot easement, adjacent landowner consent, and how restaurant and hotel jobs were counted for economic development incentives.

agenda_items.title: Report on Failed and Struggling Developments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Development Review Manager Robert Joyner reported that 90 projects across 26 subdivisions (91 total) had been completed under the Failed and Struggling Developments program by matching developers, banks, and surety bonds, costing the city only $13,000 plus roughly $12,000 recoverable via assessments on Dunwoody. Council members commended staff for running a far more proactive program than neighboring municipalities.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda & Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the regular meeting agenda (consent Items 1-6 and 8; GBA public hearings Items 11 and 12) and voted unanimously to convene in closed session.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; Cora Cole-McFadden was noted as arriving late at roll call (00:00:17), while Bill Bell, Diane Catotti, Don Moffitt, Steve Schewel, and Eugene Brown were called.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Granted excused absence for the October 8 regular meeting and October 10 work session.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules for Item 7 (10-Year OEWD Lease at 807 E. Main Street)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended rules to vote immediately on Item 7.

votes.item_title: Approve Item 7: 10-Year Lease for Office of Economic and Workforce Development
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved 10-year lease with Edgemont Tenant LLC at 807 East Main Street for the Office of Economic and Workforce Development.

votes.item_title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda (Consent 1-6, 8; GBA Public Hearings 11-12)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Set consent agenda for Items 1-6 and 8, and GBA public hearings for Items 11 and 12.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to go into closed session for the litigation consultations.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting September 16, 2013
meetings.executive_summary: On September 16, 2013, the six-member Durham City Council (with Howard Clement III absent) issued proclamations for older workers, disability employment, Hispanic Heritage Month, and Equality Week—including a message to Durham's sister city Kostroma, Russia—and saw Mayor Bill Bell receive the Triangle Business Journal's Leadership in Diversity Award. Police Chief Jose Lopez reported a 15-year low in Part 1 crime and CALEA Gold Standard status. In major land-use action, Council unanimously approved (6-0) all components of the 33.4-acre Hendrick Southpoint automotive campus annexation, plan amendment, and rezoning in Kennington Heights after residents praised the buyout as environmental justice for failing septic systems and the developer added seven commitments including a 75-foot southern buffer. Council also approved a pulled $495,000 WIA contract extension with General Management Solutions 6-0 after examining job-placement and local contracting data.

agenda_items.title: Diversity Proclamations, Sister Cities Statement, and Mayor Bell Diversity Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell and Council issued proclamations for Employ Older Workers Week, Disability Employment Awareness Month, Hispanic Heritage Month, and Equality/Diversity Week (noting Pride Week and urging equality in sister city Kostroma, Russia). Former council member Farad Ali presented Mayor Bell with the Triangle Business Journal's inaugural Leader in Diversity Award, and council members promoted community diaper drives, the Bull City Stand Down for veterans, and Project Homeless Connect.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-8, 10-17, 21)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda, covering NCLM voting delegates, July bid report, Equality Week proclamation, special-needs permanent housing funds, CDBG/HOME/ESG grant amendments, Center for Documentary Studies contract, WIA grant ordinance, NCIMED project management contract, Durham Bulls DAP assignment, city auction, Durham Arts Council lease extension, Life & Science rapid-bill development agreement, container rental, municipal software, fixed sewer-only rates, and the Board of Health water fluoridation recommendation. Item 9 was pulled for discussion (after initially being misidentified as Item 8).

agenda_items.title: 2013 Second Quarter Crime Summary Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Jose Lopez reported that Part 1 crime reached a 15-year low in the first half of 2013, with violent crime down 9%, burglaries down 10%, homicide clearance at 66.67%, and CALEA Gold Standard Accreditation recommended. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden asked for youth crime figures, and resident Victoria Peterson urged reporting Part 2 crimes and addressing employment barriers for young African American men.

agenda_items.title: Mini Assessment Roll for Sewer Main on East Cornwallis Road (Continuance)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works Director Marvin Williams requested delaying the public hearing on the East Cornwallis Road sewer main mini assessment roll until the October 7, 2013 council meeting, noting affected property owners had been notified.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation Item: Hendrick Southpoint (BDG-1202 / A12-14 / Z12-25)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented four requests for the 33.373-acre Hendrick Southpoint automotive park (up to 180,000 sq ft commercial) in Kennington Heights, adding seven new developer commitments including a 75-foot southern buffer, no loudspeakers, and an 18-inch stone wall. Neighbor Helen Ellison raised concerns over potential right-of-way taking at Massey Chapel and Fayetteville roads, while Kennington Heights resident Jeanette Wilson presented signatures from 11 families supporting the buyout due to decades of failing septic systems and contaminated well water. Council approved annexation, plan amendment, zoning, utility extension, and Parkwood fire district actions in separate 6-0 votes.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Contract Extension with General Management Solutions, Inc. ($495,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden and Council Member Eugene Brown examined the $495,000 six-month WIA adult/dislocated worker contract extension with General Management Solutions, Inc. OEWD Director Kevin Dick reported that 1,300 clients had been served, 331 placed in jobs earning $26,000 to $70,000 annually with 75-80% retention, and noted that no other Durham or North Carolina private firms bid in 2010; Brown requested that future initial reports include client counts, retention, and cost per job.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1-8, 10-17, 21; excluding pulled Item 9)
votes.notes: Council initially misidentified Item 8 as the pulled item before clarifying at 00:44:43 that Item 9 was pulled. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bill Bell read the consent agenda items covering voting delegates, the July bid report, Equality Week proclamation, permanent housing funding for persons with special needs, CDBG/HOME/ESG grant amendments, a Center for Documentary Studies contract, workforce and telecom/energy grants, the Durham Bulls DAP assignment amendment, city auction, Durham Arts Council lease extension, Museum of Life and Science agreement, municipal software, fixed sewer-only rates, and the Board of Health water fluoridation recommendation. After initially pulling Item 8, council members clarified at 00:44:43 that Item 9 (GMSI contract extension) was the item held for additional information. The rest of the consent agenda passed 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 22: Continuance of Public Hearing on East Cornwallis Road Sewer Main Mini Assessment Roll
votes.notes: Public hearing delayed to October 7, 2013. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Public Works Director Marvin Williams requested that Council postpone the public hearing on the mini assessment roll for the East Cornwallis Road sewer main until the October 7, 2013 City Council meeting, confirming that all affected property owners had been notified of the delay. Mayor Bell invited any public comments on the continuance request, and no one spoke. Council voted 6-0 to continue the hearing to October 7.

votes.item_title: Item 23A: Voluntary Annexation — Hendrick Southpoint (BDG-1202)
votes.notes: Voluntary contiguous annexation of 33.373 acres in Kennington Heights effective September 30, 2013. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bill Bell structured Item 23 into separate votes beginning with the voluntary annexation petition (BDG-1202) to ensure every affected property owner's consent was verified on the record under revised state annexation laws. Planning Director Steve Medlin confirmed that the City Clerk certified all signatures in Attachment 17 and staff re-verified current tax records showing all owners of record had signed. With no public speakers opposing annexation itself, Council closed the annexation hearing and approved the ordinance effective September 30, 2013 by a 6-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Item 23B: Comprehensive Plan Amendment — Hendrick Southpoint (A12-14)
votes.notes: FLUM change on 12.87 acres from Low-Medium Density Residential to Commercial. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff and developer attorney Lewis Cheek presented Plan Amendment A12-14 to change 12.87 acres within the 33.373-acre Kennington Heights site from Low-Medium Density Residential to Commercial, noting stream buffers and lack of water/sewer made residential development infeasible and that the Planning Commission recommended approval 10-2. Nearby landowner Helen Ellison raised concerns about losing frontage on Massey Chapel and Fayetteville roads to a potential turn lane and asked about compensation; Transportation staff and WRS's Stacy Woodhouse explained that Hendrick's pending site plans would likely shift any Massey Chapel widening requirement onto the 751 South project, and any future taking would be compensated. Kennington Heights resident Jeanette Wilson testified that residents had waited 11 years for commercial redevelopment to relieve 40 years of failing septic systems and undrinkable well water, presenting a petition signed by 11 homeowners. Council approved the plan amendment 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 23C: Initial Zoning Map Change — Hendrick Southpoint (Z12-25, Commercial General with Development Plan)
votes.notes: Allows up to 180,000 sq ft of commercial auto campus development. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented Case Z12-25 establishing Commercial General with a Development Plan (up to 180,000 sq ft) as initial zoning for the annexed Kennington Heights site, incorporating seven newly proffered commitments including a 75-foot southern buffer adjacent to Massey Chapel Church. Council Member Diane Catotti reviewed buffer illustrations and received confirmation on the record from WRS's Stacy Woodhouse that the developer intended to close on both Phase 1 and Phase 2 homeowner properties immediately after approval regardless of negotiations over five Southpoint Mall parcels. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden described the approval as an act of environmental justice for Kennington Heights families and held attorney Lewis Cheek accountable to fulfill the buyouts, while Council Member Steve Schewel questioned DOST buffer requests and streetscape visibility. Council approved the zoning change 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 23D: Utility Extension Agreement — Hendrick Southpoint
votes.notes: Extension of city water and sewer service to the Hendrick Southpoint campus. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Following approval of the voluntary annexation, comprehensive plan amendment, and initial CG(D) zoning for Hendrick Southpoint, Council took up the companion Utility Extension Agreement authorizing city water and sewer service to the site. Public Works and Water Management had previously confirmed adequate water and sewer capacity to serve the proposed automotive campus. Without additional debate, Council approved the utility extension agreement 6-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Bill Bell, the Durham City Council approved an excused absence, accepted priority items including a 2:00 p.m. Durham County Board of Health presentation on municipal water fluoridation (Item 21) and a closed-session request, and allowed two residents (Jamie Hahn and Marcia McNally) to address Council regarding the June 3 downtown parking fee increases. During Citizens Matters, MoveOn.org and Working People in Durham presented a 550-signature petition urging expansion of Durham's $11.91/hour living-wage ordinance to all workers, while Council questioned staff on Southside/Rolling Hills contractor hiring benchmarks (5 local hires out of 20 new jobs toward a ~7-job goal). Budget staff delivered the FY 2012-13 fourth-quarter financial report, showing a 13.6% general fund balance with $2.5 million available for carryover reappropriation, narrowed transit deficits ($110,000), a $700,000 solid waste tipping-fee revenue shortfall, and improved parking and ballpark fund balances. Before unanimously setting the agenda and entering closed session, Council members noted the Board of Health's fluoridation presentation was well-documented relative to opponents' handouts and requested follow-up confirmation on exact municipal fluoride concentration levels.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence, City Manager & City Attorney Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved a member's excused absence, accepted the City Manager's priority items scheduling the Board of Health water fluoridation presentation (Item 21) for 2:00 p.m. and noting a citizen speaker's absence (Item 28), and approved the City Attorney's closed-session request under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3).

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Living-Wage Petition, Southside Hiring & Downtown Parking Fees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Advocates with MoveOn.org and Working People in Durham delivered a petition of over 550 signatures asking Council to extend Durham's $11.91/hour living-wage ordinance beyond city contractors to all workers. Council also questioned staff on whether general contractors at Southside/Rolling Hills were meeting local hiring goals (20 new hires, 5 toward the 33% target) and heard Baldwin Building resident Jamie Hahn protest downtown parking fee increases adopted in June 2013.

agenda_items.title: FY 2012-13 Fourth Quarter Financial Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget staff reported ending FY 2012-13 with a 13.6% general fund balance (above 12.09% budgeted) and $2.5 million available for reappropriation, including speed-hump funding. Across enterprise funds, staff reported $4.3 million in water/sewer fund-balance savings, a reduced $110,000 transit deficit, a $700,000 solid waste tipping-fee revenue shortfall, strong stormwater collections, $263,000 lower-than-budgeted parking fund-balance draw, a ballpark surplus, and upcoming five-year planning and fleet right-sizing initiatives.

agenda_items.title: Water Fluoridation Follow-Up & Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After setting the agenda for consent Items 1-17, GBA Item 20, and GBA public hearings Items 22-23, Council noted no action was needed on Item 21 (Board of Health water fluoridation recommendation), contrasted health officials' research with opponents' handouts (including references to a Michigan study), and requested exact fluoridation parts-per-billion/million figures. Council then voted unanimously to set the agenda and enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Approve Excused Absence
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; individual roll-call responses were truncated in the transcript digest except for Bill Bell, Don Moffitt, and excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved excused absence request at the start of the work session.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Items (Item 21 Timing & Item 28 Removal)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Scheduled Item 21 (Board of Health water fluoridation presentation) at 2:00 p.m. and noted Item 28 speaker would not appear.

votes.item_title: City Attorney Priority Item (Closed Session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved request for closed session for attorney-client consultation.

votes.item_title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda (Consent 1-17, GBA 20, GBA Public Hearings 22-23)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Set consent agenda for Items 1 through 17, GBA Item 20, and GBA public hearings for Items 22 and 23.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Convened closed session following agenda setting.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting September 3, 2013
meetings.executive_summary: At its September 3, 2013 meeting, the Durham City Council swore in the Durham Youth Commission, approved 2% salary raises for the City Clerk and City Attorney and an 8.1% raise for City Manager Tom Bonfield (6-0), and ruled the Kent Corner 2 protest petition invalid after signatory withdrawals. Council unanimously approved four water and sewer assessment items, Self-Help's Kent Corner mixed-use/grocery cooperative project (5-0 on zoning with Don Moffitt recused), the 443-acre Del Webb Carolina Arbors annexation and rezoning expansion, and a city water tower annexation. The evening concluded with a lengthy public hearing on Carolina Crossing II (two seven-story medical office buildings at NC 54 and Farrington Road), which Council approved unanimously after the applicant proffered pedestrian crosswalks and signals despite an earlier 8-4 Planning Commission denial recommendation and Falconbridge residents' traffic and height objections.

agenda_items.title: Durham Youth Commission Swearing-In and Constitution Week Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Office of Youth staff introduced members of the 2013-14 Durham Youth Commission, who introduced themselves and took the oath of office from City Clerk Ann Gray. Mayor Bell also presented a Constitution Week proclamation to DAR Regent Fran Ferrell.

agenda_items.title: Performance Evaluations and Salary Increases for Council Appointees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell announced that Council had just completed performance evaluations for its three appointed officers and recommended effective July 1, 2013 salary increases of 2% for the City Clerk, 2% for the City Attorney, and 8.1% for City Manager Tom Bonfield.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items: Agenda Reordering (Item 27) and Kent Corner 2 Protest Petition Ruling (Item 22)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the City Manager's request to hear Item 27 (Del Webb 3 annexation) before Items 23 and 24 for legal sequencing, and approved the City Clerk's ruling that the Kent Corner 2 protest petition was invalid due to signatory withdrawals.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-3, 5-6, 9-15)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda, including minutes, board appointments, street acceptances, CIP budget amendment, mortgage loan servicing extension, Motorola radio system renewal, Carolina Panthers and NRPA parks grants, city code revisions on infrastructure acceptance and reimbursement, and a county interlocal paving agreement.

agenda_items.title: Durham City-County Appearance Commission Appointment (Ballot)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council cast written ballots for the Durham City-County Appearance Commission appointment; at the close of the meeting (`02:42:10`), the City Clerk announced Lowanna Burrows received four votes.

agenda_items.title: Water and Sewer Main Assessment Rolls (Ed Cook Rd, Ardmore Dr, Valley Springs Rd, Andrew Ave/Cortez Dr)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works staff presented four assessment roll items: confirming water main assessments on Ed Cook Road (Item 17) and Ardmore Drive (Item 18); confirming Valley Springs Road water assessments while continuing three objected parcels to October 21 (Item 19); and granting sewer assessment relief until tap-on for 0 Cortez Drive while confirming $2,373.50 for 107 Cortez Drive (Item 20).

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Kent Corner (A12-00017)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Chapel Hill Street Development LLC's (Self-Help) request to change 1.3 acres at Kent and West Chapel Hill streets from Medium Density Residential to Commercial, backed by a 12-0 Planning Commission vote. One supporter praised the project's jobs, retail, and affordable housing potential.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Kent Corner 2 (Z13-00007)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Self-Help's rezoning of 2.7 acres at Kent and West Chapel Hill streets to CG(D) and CI(D) for 50,000 sq ft of commercial space anchored by the Durham Central Market co-op grocery. Seven supporters—including Quality of Life Project, Kent Corner Task Force, DDI, Durham Central Market, and DCLT—praised Self-Help's 40 community meetings; resident Marshall Williams raised concerns about losing the closed West End Community Center youth study space, and Self-Help and Mayor Bell pointed to Lyon Park and Emily K Center programs. Council Member Don Moffitt was excused due to a conflict of interest.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation Item: Del Webb 3 (BDG-1201 / Z12-21A)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Pulte Homes' voluntary annexation and initial Rural Residential zoning for approximately 18 acres as part of the Del Webb 3 expansion, noting net-positive fiscal impact.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Del Webb Carolina Arbors (A12-00011)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Horvath Associates' request to amend 14.3 acres north of US 70 and west of Andrews Chapel Road from Low-Medium Density Residential to Low Density Residential, recommended 12-0 by the Planning Commission.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Del Webb Carolina Arbors (Z12-00022)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the companion rezoning adding ~18 acres to the 420-plus-acre Del Webb age-restricted PDR 3.7 community (capped at 1,314 units). Council Member Steve Schewel questioned fire station land donation progress, HOA enforcement of age restrictions, greenway trail construction versus peripheral easements, and striped bike lanes on the collector street; applicant Ron Horvath also noted 2,500 attendees at the recent open house.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation Item: 2207 Page Road Water Tower
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the voluntary annexation and initial Rural Residential zoning for the City of Durham's proposed water tower site at 2207 Page Road. No public opposition was raised.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Carolina Crossing II (Z12-00004)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a rezoning of 5.033 acres at 5936 Farrington Road from RS-20 to OI(D) for two seven-story medical office buildings—consistent with the comprehensive plan but recommended for denial 8-4 by the Planning Commission. Falconbridge residents opposed traffic impacts at NC 54/Farrington Road and the seven-story height, while Farrington Road Baptist Church Pastor Jason Hughes supported selling the church site. After the applicant proffered crosswalks and pedestrian signals at NC 54/Farrington Road and $1 million in interim lane improvements, council members who had initially leaned against the project voted to approve.

votes.item_title: Salary Increases for Council Appointees (City Clerk 2%, City Attorney 2%, City Manager 8.1%)
votes.notes: Effective July 1, 2013 following closed-session performance evaluations. Howard Clement III not present.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bill Bell announced that Council had just concluded its annual performance evaluations of the City Manager, City Clerk, and City Attorney prior to opening the public meeting. Based on those deliberations, Council agreed to grant salary increases retroactive to July 1, 2013 of 2% for the City Clerk, 2% for the City Attorney, and 8.1% for City Manager Tom Bonfield. No council members raised objections on the floor. Council approved the salary adjustments 6-0.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Item: Move Item 27 (Del Webb 3 Annexation) Before Items 23 and 24
votes.notes: Howard Clement III not present.
votes.discussion_detail: The City Manager requested as a priority item that Council consider Item 27, the consolidated annexation for the Del Webb 3 development, prior to considering Items 23 and 24 for the Del Webb Carolina Arbors plan amendment and rezoning. votes.notes: Protest petition ruled invalid due to withdrawal of signatories. Howard Clement III not present.
votes.discussion_detail: The City Clerk reported as a priority item that the zoning protest petition filed against Item 22 (Kent Corner 2, Z13-00007) had been ruled invalid because property owners had withdrawn their signatures below the statutory threshold. Mayor Bell entertained a motion to accept the City Clerk's priority ruling. Without debate, Council voted 6-0 to accept the determination.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Confirmation of Assessment Roll for Water Main on Ed Cook Road
votes.notes: Howard Clement III not present.
votes.discussion_detail: Public Works Engineering Services staff member Nathan McHenry presented Item 17, recommending confirmation of the assessment roll for completed water main improvements on Ed Cook Road. Mayor Bell opened the public hearing and solicited questions from Council and comments from the audience. With no speakers appearing, Council closed the public hearing and confirmed the assessment roll 6-0.

votes.notes: Howard Clement III not present.
votes.discussion_detail: Nathan McHenry of Public Works Engineering Services presented Item 18, recommending confirmation of the water main improvement assessment roll for Ardmore Drive. Council closed the public hearing and confirmed the Ardmore Drive assessment roll 6-0.

votes.notes: Confirmed Valley Springs Road area rolls except Foster, R&K Real Estate, and Bellis Browning (4723 Rose Rd), which were continued to Oct 21, 2013. Howard Clement III not present.
votes.discussion_detail: Nathan McHenry presented Item 19, noting that John A.T. Foster, R&K Real Estate Group, and Bellis Browning (4723 Rose Road) had objected to their water main assessments in the Valley Springs Road area. Staff recommended confirming the remaining Valley Springs Road area assessment rolls while continuing the public hearing on the three objected properties to the October 21, 2013 Council meeting without further advertising. With no public speakers, Council approved the staff recommendation 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Mini Assessment Roll for Sewer Main on Andrew Avenue and Cortez Drive
votes.notes: Granted relief until tap-on for 0 Cortez Dr heirs properties; confirmed $2,373.50 assessment for 107 Cortez Dr. Howard Clement III not present.
votes.discussion_detail: Public Works staff presented Item 20, a continued mini assessment roll for the sewer main on Andrew Avenue and Cortez Drive. Staff recommended granting relief until tap-on for the William Coakley and Janet Tyndall heirs and R.T. and C.M. No public speakers objected, and Council approved the mini assessment roll 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Comprehensive Plan Amendment — Kent Corner (A12-00017)
votes.notes: Clerk announced 6-0 vote, though City Attorney later stated at 00:58:03 that Don Moffitt was excused from both Kent Corner items due to a conflict of interest. Howard Clement III not present.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff member Aaron Cain presented Case A12-00017, a request by Chapel Hill Street Development LLC (Self-Help) to amend the Future Land Use Map for 1.3 acres at Kent and West Chapel Hill streets from Medium Density Residential to Commercial. Both staff and the Planning Commission (12-0) recommended approval. One supporter spoke briefly, praising Self-Help's plans for jobs, retail, street life, and nearby affordable housing. Council closed the public hearing and approved the plan amendment by a recorded 6-0 tally (before the City Attorney later noted Don Moffitt's recusal from both Kent Corner items).

votes.item_title: Item 22: Zoning Map Change — Kent Corner 2 (Z13-00007)
votes.notes: Don Moffitt excused/abstained due to conflict of interest. Howard Clement III not present.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented Case Z13-00007, rezoning 2.7 acres at Kent and West Chapel Hill streets to CG(D) and CI(D) for 50,000 sq ft of commercial space anchored by the Durham Central Market cooperative grocery store, with extensive buffering, lighting, and height commitments. Nine supporters—representing Self-Help, Quality of Life Project, Kent Corner Task Force, Downtown Durham Inc., West Chapel Hill Merchants Alliance, Durham Central Market, and DCLT—praised the 40 community meetings that produced the plan, while West End resident Marshall Williams opposed the loss of the closed West End Community Center for neighborhood youth study programs. votes.item_title: Item 27: Consolidated Annexation and Initial Zoning — Del Webb 3 (BDG-1201 / Z12-21A)

votes.notes: Expanded PDR 3.7 community to 443 acres with max 1,314 age-restricted units. Howard Clement III not present.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented Case Z12-00022, adding 18 acres to the existing 420-plus-acre Del Webb Carolina Arbors PDR 3.7 development while maintaining a 1,314-unit cap and previously committed roadway improvements. Council Member Steve Schewel questioned an acreage typo in an applicant attachment, progress on donating a fire station site (which Ron Horvath confirmed was 95% complete), enforceability of HOA age restrictions, and the distinction between constructed internal greenway trails versus peripheral trail easements. Transportation staff confirmed striped bike lanes were already constructed along part of the north-south collector street. Mayor Bell noted over 2,500 people attended Del Webb's recent open house before Council approved the rezoning 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 26: Consolidated Annexation — 2207 Page Road Water Tower
votes.notes: Voluntary annexation and Rural Residential zoning for City of Durham water tower site. Howard Clement III not present.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff member Pat Young presented the consolidated annexation item for the proposed City of Durham Water Tower at 2207 Page Road, comprising a voluntary annexation petition and initial Rural Residential zoning (the least intense tier allowing the facility). votes.item_title: Item 25: Zoning Map Change — Carolina Crossing II (Z12-00004)
votes.notes: Rezoning of 5.033 acres at 5936 Farrington Rd from RS-20 to OI(D) for two 7-story medical office buildings; Planning Commission had recommended denial 8-4. Howard Clement III not present.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented Case Z12-00004 to rezone 5.033 acres at 5936 Farrington Road to OI(D) for two seven-story medical office buildings, noting consistency with the comprehensive plan despite an 8-4 Planning Commission denial recommendation. Traffic engineer Earl Lewellen and developer representatives detailed $1 million in interim turn-lane, median, and bike-lane upgrades maintaining Level of Service D until NCDOT's $40 million Farrington flyover is funded after 2023, while Farrington Road Baptist Church Pastor Jason Hughes testified the sale would allow the church to relocate. Falconbridge residents Van Noah, Rosemary Kitchen, and Julia McMillan opposed the seven-story height, 40-fold weekday trip increase over a church, and cut-through traffic. After the applicant agreed on the record to proffer pedestrian crosswalks and signals at NC 54 and Farrington Road, initially skeptical council members (Catotti, Schewel, Moffitt, and Brown) concluded the improvements benefited the intersection in the interim and voted unanimously to approve.

disagreements.issue: Carolina Crossing II Seven-Story Medical Office Rezoning at NC 54 & Farrington Road (Z12-00004)
disagreements.summary: Following an 8-4 Planning Commission denial recommendation and Falconbridge neighborhood opposition to building height and severe congestion at NC 54/Farrington Road, Council debated whether $1 million in interim road improvements and a new pedestrian-crossing proffer justified approving two seven-story medical office buildings.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the rezoning with $1 million in interim roadway improvements and proffered pedestrian crosswalks/signals.
side_a_arguments: City and NCDOT traffic staff verified the developer's interim turn lanes and median improvements would maintain Level of Service D and improve intersection efficiency for a decade or more before NCDOT's $40M flyover is funded.
The applicant's last-minute proffer of crosswalks and pedestrian signals addressed TTA transit rider safety across NC 54.
The site lies in a compact neighborhood tier near a future transit station node.
disagreements.side_b_position: Opposed by Planning Commission (8-4) and Falconbridge residents (Van Noah, Rosemary Kitchen, Julia McMillan) due to traffic congestion, cut-through volume, and seven-story scale.
side_b_arguments: NC 54 and Farrington Road is already one of the region's most congested intersections, and two medical office towers generate roughly 40 times the weekday traffic of the existing church.
Two seven-story buildings are aesthetically out of scale with surrounding one- to three-story structures and will worsen neighborhood cut-through traffic on Hunting Ridge Road.
disagreements.resolution: Approved 6-0 after the applicant proffered pedestrian crosswalk and signal improvements at NC 54 and Farrington Road.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Opened and presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden (with Mayor Bill Bell arriving at 00:21:36), the Durham City Council suspended the rules and unanimously approved an FAA grant offer for RDU Terminal 1 Apron Rehabilitation (Item 8) and accepted a valid protest petition on the Kent Corner II rezoning (Item 22). Council heard five public speakers and conducted an extended review of the proposed deer bow-hunting ordinance (Item 7)—raising questions regarding crossbows, dwelling setback distances, broadheads, and urban archery seasons—before referring the ordinance back to staff and committee to return as a public hearing item. Council also reviewed a $500,000 Southside East CIP amendment (Item 9), a $30,000 contract termination fee (Item 10), utility assessment formulas (Item 19), and a Public Works stream restoration update under the NC Ecosystem Enhancement Program. Contested advisory board ballots were announced at the close of the session—Historic Preservation Commission (Jennifer Mitchell 5 votes, Michael Morris 4 votes) and City-County Appearance Commission (Lou Rose 3 votes, Terry Emerson 2 votes; individual member ballot choices were not read aloud in the transcript)—while all formal Council voice votes passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Deer Bow-Hunting Ordinance Referral

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting August 19, 2013
meetings.executive_summary: On August 19, 2013, with Council Member Eugene Brown excused, the Durham City Council recognized local employers participating in the Durham Youth Work Internship Program and passed the consent agenda 6-0, including the Parks and Recreation Master Plan. Council confirmed a water main assessment on Duffield Road (6-0) and split an East Cornwallis Road sewer assessment item (5-0, Mayor Bell abstaining) to continue UDI Community Development Corporation's waiver request for four weeks. The meeting culminated in an extensive debate over a $1.33 million historic-preservation economic incentive agreement with Concord Hospitality for a 143-room hotel at the former McPherson Hospital (1108 W. Main Street), which passed 5-1 with Howard Clement III voting no over the exclusion of lower-wage hospitality workers from Durham's living-wage standard.

agenda_items.title: Durham Youth Work Internship Program & DollarWise Financial Literacy Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell and Council Members Diane Catotti and Steve Schewel recognized local employers participating in the collaborative Durham Youth Work Internship Program and awarded an Amazon Kindle to student Ronald Bethea Jr. through the DollarWise financial literacy program. Council Member Howard Clement III congratulated Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, Kenneth Spaulding, and Dr. John Lucas on recent awards from the Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-6, 8-9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda, covering HRC and CAC appointments, preliminary assessment rolls, street acceptances, a Joint Disparity Study interlocal amendment with Durham County, Limited Obligation Bonds Series 2013A/B, a Del Webb HOA license agreement, and the Parks and Recreation Master Plan. Council Member Steve Schewel commended Parks and Recreation staff for completing the 170-page master plan in-house with extensive public input.

agenda_items.title: Mini Assessment Roll for Water Main on Duffield Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works staff member Nathan McHenry presented Item 10, finding no qualifying relief criteria for the owner of 1205 Duffield Road and recommending confirmation of the original $2,012.50 water main assessment. No public speakers opposed.

agenda_items.title: Mini Assessment Roll for Sewer Main on East Cornwallis Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell recused himself due to his employment with UDI CDC and turned the chair over to Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden. UDI CDC President Ed Stewart contested the assessment on 4601 Industry Lane citing unreceived P.O. Box mailings, an earlier land swap with city engineers, and pre-existing sewer access. After engineering staff confirmed UDI already had sewer availability at the rear of its site, Council voted to approve Item 11B (confirming 1602 and 1604 East Cornwallis Road) and continue Item 11C (4601 Industry Lane) for four weeks.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development and Historic Property Preservation Agreement: Concord Hospitality (1108 W. Main St.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD Director Kevin Dick presented a $1.33 million eight-year tax-increment-style incentive (paired with a $400,000 county grant) to rehabilitate the historic 1926 McPherson Eye, Ear, Nose and Throat Hospital into a 143-room Residence Inn, projecting a $446,000 net city return over eight years. Trinity Park and Preservation Durham leaders supported the deal, while Council Members Howard Clement III, Cora Cole-McFadden, Steve Schewel, Don Moffitt, and Diane Catotti criticized the fact that half of the 31 hotel jobs paid below Durham's $11.91 living wage and that Durham County earned far higher tax returns per incentive dollar. Council approved the agreement 5-1 with Clement voting no.

votes.item_title: Item 10: Mini Assessment Roll for Water Main on Duffield Road (1205 Duffield Road)
votes.notes: Confirmed original assessment of $2,012.50 against 1205 Duffield Road. Eugene Brown absent (excused).
votes.discussion_detail: Public Works Engineering Services staff member Nathan McHenry reported that the owner of 1205 Duffield Road had objected to the water main assessment during the May 6, 2013 hearing, prompting a staff review. Staff determined that no grounds existed under Council's approved assessment relief criteria and recommended confirming the original assessment of $2,012.50. No council members raised questions and no members of the public spoke during the hearing. Council approved the confirmation 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 11: Mini Assessment Roll for Sewer Main on East Cornwallis Road (Approve 11B; Continue 11C Four Weeks)
votes.notes: Mayor Bill Bell recused due to UDI CDC employment; Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presided. Confirmed 11B (1602 and 1604 E. Cornwallis Rd) and continued 11C (UDI CDC / 4601 Industry Lane) for four weeks. Eugene Brown absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bill Bell recused himself from Item 11 due to his employment with UDI Community Development Corporation, and Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presided. UDI CDC President Ed Stewart urged Council to waive the assessment on 4601 Industry Lane, testifying that UDI had closed the P.O. Box where notices were mailed and was told during an earlier sewer easement land swap that there would be no cost to UDI. Public Works staff confirmed notices were sent to the address of record in tax files, while engineering staff member Robert Joyner testified that UDI's parcel already had sewer availability at the rear and therefore gained no additional benefit from the line built for a failing neighbor septic system. Council Members Don Moffitt, Steve Schewel, and Diane Catotti sought more mapping and legal clarity on relief eligibility, leading Catotti to move approval of Item 11B (1602 and 1604 East Cornwallis Road) while continuing Item 11C (4601 Industry Lane) for four weeks; the motion passed 5-0 with Mayor Bell abstaining.

votes.item_title: Item 12: Economic Development and Historic Property Preservation Agreement — Concord Hospitality (1108 W. Main Street)
votes.notes: $1.33 million over 8 years for 143-room Residence Inn preserving historic McPherson Hospital facade. Eugene Brown absent.
votes.discussion_detail: OEWD Director Kevin Dick presented a proposed $1.33 million eight-year incentive agreement with Concord Hospitality to rehabilitate the vacant 1926 McPherson Hospital at 1108 West Main Street into a 143-room Residence Inn, projecting $1.13M in occupancy/sales taxes and $640k in property taxes for a net $446,000 city gain alongside a $400,000 county preservation grant. Preservation Durham Executive Director Wendy Hillis and Trinity Park representatives supported the incentive as the last chance to save the unprotected landmark, while public speakers Victoria Peterson and Vince Taylor demanded stronger monitoring of local and minority construction hiring. Council Members Howard Clement III and Cora Cole-McFadden objected that only half of the 31 full-time hotel jobs would meet Durham's $11.91 living wage, and Steve Schewel and Don Moffitt criticized the lopsided city-county return ($0.35 net per dollar for Durham vs. $6-$7 for the county). Though Schewel, Moffitt, Catotti, Cole-McFadden, and Bell all expressed reluctance and called for reforming city incentive policy, only Clement voted no, and the agreement passed 5-1.

disagreements.issue: Living Wage Requirements and City-County Cost Sharing in Concord Hospitality Incentive Agreement (Item 12)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 5-1 over whether to approve a $1.33 million historic-preservation incentive for Concord Hospitality's Residence Inn at McPherson Hospital when roughly half of the hotel's permanent positions would pay below Durham's $11.91 living wage.
disagreements.side_a_position: Reluctantly approve the incentive to save the historic McPherson Hospital building, add 143 downtown hotel rooms, and gain net tax revenue.
side_a_arguments: The 1926 McPherson Hospital has no historic protection and would likely deteriorate or be demolished without the incentive.
City policy only mandates living wages for job-creation incentives and city-service contracts, not capital/historic preservation grants, and prior hotel incentives did not impose living wages.

Concord committed to good-faith local hiring via Durham JobLink, competitive benefits, and wage growth above $11.91 over time, though council members urged future policy reform on living wages and county cost-sharing.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose or defer the incentive unless all jobs meet Durham's living-wage standard.
side_b_arguments: Public tax dollars should not subsidize private projects that exclude service workers from a living wage.
Clement urged a two-cycle deferral to ask Concord Hospitality to incorporate living-wage compliance into the agreement.
disagreements.resolution: Incentive agreement approved 5-1 with Howard Clement III voting no.

disagreements.issue: UDI CDC Sewer Assessment Waiver Dispute on East Cornwallis Road (Item 11)
disagreements.summary: UDI Community Development Corporation contested a sewer assessment on 4601 Industry Lane citing P.O. Box notice issues, a prior easement swap, and pre-existing sewer access, prompting Council to defer the parcel.
disagreements.side_a_position: Waive the sewer assessment against 4601 Industry Lane (argued by UDI CDC President Ed Stewart; engineering staff confirmed UDI already had rear sewer access).
side_a_arguments: UDI did not receive mailed hearing notices sent to a closed P.O. Box and had been told an earlier easement land swap carried no cost.
Engineering staff testified that 4601 Industry Lane already had access to an existing sewer outfall and gained no additional benefit.
disagreements.side_b_position: Confirm other assessments (11B) while continuing UDI's parcel (11C) four weeks to clarify maps, easement swap history, and relief eligibility.
side_b_arguments: Council lacked maps and sufficient documentation on the land swap and whether an unconnected parcel with pre-existing availability qualifies for relief until tap-on.
disagreements.resolution: Council voted 5-0 (Mayor Bell recused) to confirm Item 11B and continue Item 11C for four weeks.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Bill Bell, the Durham City Council held its August 8, 2013 work session covering bond financing, parks planning, municipal appointments, and state legislative updates. Council unanimously approved an excused absence for Council Member Eugene Brown for the next two scheduled meetings and moved the Kent Corner comprehensive plan amendment and zoning map change public hearing (Items 13 and 14) to September 3, 2013 because Brown's absence would leave too few members for the supermajority/five-vote threshold. Under suspended rules, Council unanimously approved Item 7, a Parks and Recreation booking agent contract, while Finance Director David Boyd addressed questions on Limited Obligation Bonds Series 2013A and 2013B (Item 6). Council also heard an extended presentation on the Parks and Recreation Master Plan (Item 9), with members pressing staff for clearer park maintenance budget data ahead of the next budget cycle, and received a recap of the North Carolina General Assembly long session covering Jordan Lake rules delays, outdoor dining (HB 192), water utility regionalization (HB 48), and firearms registration (SB 226).

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence Request & City Manager Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Eugene Brown requested an excused absence for the next two scheduled meetings. The City Manager then presented priority items requesting suspension of the rules to vote on Item 7 (Parks and Recreation booking agent contract) and noting a legislative update on the North Carolina General Assembly long session.

agenda_items.title: City Clerk Priority Item: Deferral of Kent Corner Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk and Planning Director Steve Medlin advised Council that with Eugene Brown absent at the next meeting, Council would lack the five or six votes required for the Kent Corner zoning petition (Item 14). Council directed staff to re-advertise and move the public hearing for Items 13 and 14 to September 3, 2013.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review & Immediate Action on Item 7 (Booking Agent Contract)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council read through the consent and public hearing agenda, including Human Relations Commission and Citizens Advisory Committee appointments (Items 1-2), preliminary road assessment rolls (Item 3), a Joint Disparity Study amendment with Durham County (Item 5), Series 2013A/B Limited Obligation Bonds (Item 6), and an East Cornwallis Road sewer main assessment roll (Item 11), from which one member recused due to UDI CDC involvement. Under suspended rules, Council unanimously approved Item 7.

agenda_items.title: Series 2013A and 2013B Limited Obligation Bonds Indenture
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director David Boyd answered Council questions regarding the resolution authorizing Series 2013A and 2013B Limited Obligation Bonds. Boyd explained that amending the existing collateral pool indenture is simpler legally than building a new indenture, and clarified that a reference to former official Nick Tennyson's signature appeared only in an early draft document.

agenda_items.title: Parks and Recreation Master Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the Parks and Recreation Master Plan, prompting extensive Council discussion on parkland acquisition amid county growth and chronic underfunding of park maintenance. Council members, including Diane Catotti, emphasized needing clearer resource data before the next budget cycle rather than relying on ad hoc workarounds such as having Public Works paving trainees practice on park roads.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: RaindownsUS.org
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Anita Woodley representing RaindownsUS.org addressed Council regarding community arts and outreach programming and upcoming local events. Council members thanked her and asked how to stay informed about future events.

agenda_items.title: North Carolina General Assembly Long Session Recap
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff provided a legislative update covering the state budget and tax reform bills, the three-year delay in Jordan Lake rules implementation, House Bill 192 (allowing outdoor dining in central business district NCDOT rights-of-way), House Bill 48 (public utility regionalization), and Senate Bill 226 (firearms registration, which did not pass). Council requested that staff distribute Steve Medlin's planning analysis and Metro Mayors and League recaps to all members.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments, Agenda Setting & Return to Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk announced six-vote appointments to the Human Relations Commission and Citizens Advisory Committee. Council unanimously set the regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1-6, 8, and 9; GBA Public Hearings Items 10-12) before returning to closed session for employee evaluations.
