meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting August 5, 2013
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council (with six members present and Howard Clement III absent) opened with proclamations for the 30th annual National Night Out, the North Carolina Child Response Initiative, and Durham Crime Stoppers, as well as recognition of Youth Summer Service Week and a memorial resolution for former NCCU Chancellor Julius L. Chambers. Council unanimously adopted the consent agenda, then heard testimony from local physicians before passing a resolution (6-0) urging the North Carolina General Assembly and Governor Pat McCrory to expand Medicaid. Council also held public hearings and voted 6-0 to approve a street renaming on Ardmore Drive/Morningside Drive, the Rustic Oaks comprehensive plan amendment and rezoning, and the Del Webb entry monuments comprehensive plan amendment and rezoning.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations and Recognitions: National Night Out, NC Child Response Initiative, Crime Stoppers, Youth Summer Service Week, and Julius L. Chambers Memorial
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented proclamations recognizing the 30th annual National Night Out with Police Chief Jose Lopez and honoring 30 years of Durham Crime Stoppers with board chair Pat Ellis. Representatives from the Center for Child and Family Health thanked the Police Department for nine years of partnership on the North Carolina Child Response Initiative despite recent sequestration grant cuts, and Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden recognized Youth Summer Service Week participants. Council concluded recognitions by voting 6-0 to endorse a memorial resolution for the family of attorney and former NCCU Chancellor Julius L. Chambers.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1-16, 18-21, 23-28)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell read the titles of the consent agenda items, including minutes approval, advisory board and commission appointments, May and June 2013 bid reports, property disposition intent, a training/travel performance audit, HOME Consortium cooperation amendment, grant ordinances, ferric sulfate and Lake Michie property acquisition items, Fleet Maintenance Center roof renovations, stop-loss insurance, Old North Durham Park and American Tobacco Trail contract amendments, electronic recycling, and Bull City Connector agreement with Duke University. Items 31-35 and 39 were reserved on the General Business Agenda.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Urging the North Carolina General Assembly and Governor to Expand Medicaid
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Three Durham physicians—Dr. Gary Greenberg, Dr. Howard Eisenson (Medical Director of Lincoln Community Health Center), and Dr. Mohan Chilukuri—urged Council to pass the resolution, citing the 18% uninsured rate in Durham County and criticizing state leaders for rejecting federal Affordable Care Act funds covering over 500,000 North Carolinians. Council Members Steve Schewel and Eugene Brown spoke strongly in favor of the resolution, calling the state's refusal hostile to residents and thanking organizer Anthony Ross and local health leaders.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Street Renaming (SN1300001) — Ardmore Drive to Morningside Drive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young of the Planning Department presented Case SN1300001 to permanently rename approximately 150 feet of Ardmore Drive to Morningside Drive to provide a consistent street name connecting Woodcroft Subdivision to a new section of Chamberlin Subdivision. Staff reported no public comments at the May 14 public meeting and no objections from the U.S. Postal Service or reviewing agencies. No members of the public spoke at the hearing.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Comprehensive Plan Amendment (A1300003) — Rustic Oaks Subdivision
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented Case A1300003 for Rustic Oaks, LLC to amend the Future Land Use Map for a 0.66-acre parcel at 1819 Rustic Drive from Low Density Residential to Low-Medium Density Residential to allow subdivision into multiple lots. The Planning Commission had recommended approval 11-0 on May 14. During public comment, a speaker performed a satirical song that included a remark about Mexicans, prompting Council Member Steve Schewel to rebuke the remark as inappropriate; the speaker apologized.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change (Z1300006) — Rustic Oaks Subdivision
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented the companion rezoning case Z1300006 to rezone the 0.66-acre parcel at 1819 Rustic Drive from Rural Residential (RR) to Residential Suburban-8 (RS-8) without a development plan, allowing subdivision into approximately three residential building lots. Staff and the Planning Commission (11-0) recommended approval. There were no council questions or public speakers.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Comprehensive Plan Amendment (A1200009) — Del Webb Entry Monuments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented Case A1200009 by Horvath Associates to amend the Future Land Use Map from Low Density Residential to Institutional across three perimeter locations totaling 2.67 acres at the Del Webb Carolina Arbors neighborhood so entryway monuments could be constructed. Staff and the Planning Commission (11-0) recommended approval. Applicant representative Ron Horvath signed up to speak but no questions were raised.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change (Z1200020) — Del Webb Entry Monuments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young presented companion rezoning Case Z1200020 to rezone the 2.67 acres from Planned Density Residential (PDR 3.70) to Office and Institutional with a Development Plan (OI(D)) permitting up to approximately 80 square feet of entryway signage and no buildings or other uses. Council Member Don Moffitt confirmed with staff that the site plan was submitted as the development plan, and no public speakers objected.

agenda_items.title: Scheduling of Special Meeting for Appointee Evaluations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell announced a Thursday special meeting (scheduled for 11:00 a.m., aiming to convene around 11:30 a.m.) to continue performance evaluations for the City Attorney and City Clerk, noting the City Manager's evaluation would be held at the next work session. Council Member Steve Schewel remarked to a visiting family that Council meetings sometimes feature lively debate even though this session was brief, and the meeting adjourned at 7:46 p.m.

votes.item_title: Resolution Honoring the Family of Julius L. Chambers
votes.notes: Council Member Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Following a moment of silent meditation in memory of attorney and former North Carolina Central University Chancellor Julius L. Chambers, Mayor Bill Bell requested Council's endorsement to prepare an official resolution for the Chambers family and enter it into the permanent record. No Council member offered objections or additional debate. The motion was moved, seconded, and approved unanimously 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 39: Resolution Expanding Medicaid in North Carolina
votes.notes: Resolution shared with the Durham delegation of the NC General Assembly. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Three local physicians—Dr. Gary Greenberg, Dr. Howard Eisenson of Lincoln Community Health Center, and Dr. Mohan Chilukuri—spoke in support of the resolution, detailing how rejecting Affordable Care Act Medicaid expansion leaves roughly 500,000 low-income North Carolinians uninsured and strains charity clinics and emergency rooms. Mayor Bell read the resolution noting Durham's status as the City of Medicine, an estimated 18% uninsured rate in Durham County, and projected state savings of $65 million over 10 years. Council Member Steve Schewel strongly endorsed the measure and thanked initiator Anthony Ross and the medical community, while Council Member Eugene Brown characterized the General Assembly's action as exceedingly hostile to citizens. Council passed the resolution 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 31: Street Renaming Case SN1300001 (Ardmore Drive to Morningside Drive)
votes.notes: Renames ~150 feet of Ardmore Drive to Morningside Drive. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning Department staff member Pat Young explained that Case SN1300001 permanently renames approximately 150 feet of Ardmore Drive to Morningside Drive so the roadway connecting Woodcroft Subdivision to a new phase of Chamberlin Subdivision carries a consistent name. Staff reported that a May 14, 2013 public meeting yielded no comments and neither the U.S. Postal Service nor city review agencies identified negative impacts. No Council members asked questions and no members of the public spoke during the hearing, after which Council closed the hearing and approved the renaming 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 32: Comprehensive Plan Amendment Case A1300003 (Rustic Oaks Subdivision)
votes.notes: Amends Future Land Use Map at 1819 Rustic Drive (0.66 acres) from Low Density Residential to Low-Medium Density Residential. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff member Pat Young presented Case A1300003 on behalf of Rustic Oaks, LLC to change the Future Land Use designation of 1819 Rustic Drive from Low Density Residential to Low-Medium Density Residential, noting 11-0 Planning Commission approval on May 14. During public comment, a speaker performing a satirical parody song supporting the item included an ethnic joke about Mexicans. Council Member Steve Schewel immediately objected that remarks targeting ethnic groups were inappropriate even in satire, prompting an apology from the speaker before Mayor Bell accepted the comments and apology into the record. Council closed the public hearing and approved the plan amendment 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 33: Zoning Map Change Case Z1300006 (Rustic Oaks Subdivision)
votes.notes: Companion rezoning from RR to RS-8 without a development plan. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented Case Z1300006 as the companion rezoning to the Rustic Oaks comprehensive plan amendment, changing the 0.66-acre parcel from Rural Residential (RR) to Residential Suburban-8 (RS-8) with no development plan to enable approximately three residential lots. Staff reported that the Planning Commission recommended approval 11-0 on May 14 and found the request consistent with the Unified Development Ordinance. No Council questions or public comments were offered, and Council voted 6-0 to approve the rezoning.

votes.item_title: Item 34: Comprehensive Plan Amendment Case A1200009 (Del Webb Entry Monuments)
votes.notes: Changes 2.67 acres across three perimeter locations from Low Density Residential to Institutional. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented Case A1200009 requested by Horvath Associates to redesignate three perimeter parcels totaling 2.67 acres along the Del Webb Carolina Arbors neighborhood from Low Density Residential to Institutional so large entryway monuments could be permitted. Staff and the Planning Commission (11-0 on May 14) recommended approval. Applicant Ron Horvath was registered to speak but no questions were asked by Council and no opposition spoke, leading to a 6-0 approval.

votes.item_title: Item 35: Zoning Map Change Case Z1200020 (Del Webb Entry Monuments)
votes.notes: Rezones 2.67 acres from PDR 3.70 to OI(D) limiting use to ~80 sq ft signage. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Pat Young presented companion rezoning Case Z1200020 to rezone the 2.67 acres from Planned Density Residential (PDR 3.70) to Office and Institutional with a Development Plan (OI(D)), restricting the sites to approximately 80 square feet of entryway signage with no buildings or other uses allowed. Council Member Don Moffitt asked staff to confirm whether a site plan had been submitted as the development plan, and staff confirmed yes. With no public comments, Council closed the hearing and approved the rezoning 6-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Bill Bell with five Council members present, the Durham City Council reviewed infrastructure contracts, affordable housing and Southside updates, and a detailed presentation on the City Hall Envelope Project. Council unanimously approved an excused absence request for Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, accepted the City Manager's priority item to suspend the rules and vote on Item 22 (Chapel Hill Street Garage concrete repairs with Progressive Contracting Co., Inc. and Walter P. Moore & Associates), and approved two City Attorney closed-session items. During Citizens Matters, speakers addressed rental housing inspection complaints, a stop-work order, and a proposed resolution urging the North Carolina General Assembly and Governor to accept federal funds for Medicaid expansion. Presenters on the City Hall Envelope Project detailed a $6.35M–$6.9M plan to replace failed cementitious panels with a rainscreen system and replace brick-with-brick as required by the Architectural Review Board, while Council questioned Planning basement water intrusion and maintenance priorities before setting the agenda (5-0) and entering closed session.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence, Chapel Hill Street Garage Priority Item (Item 22) & Closed Session Requests

Council then approved the City Manager's priority item requesting suspension of the rules to vote on Item 22 (Chapel Hill Street Garage concrete repairs contract with Progressive Contracting Co. and design amendment with Walter P. Moore & Associates), as well as the City Attorney's request for two closed sessions under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3).

agenda_items.title: Agenda Read-Through & Human Resources Reinsurance Savings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent and public hearing items including city property annexation intent (Item 15), Rebuild Durham Inc. loan modification (Item 17), Durham City-County HOME Consortium amendment (Item 18), Bull City Connector agreement with Duke University (Item 21/28), Old North Durham Park and American Tobacco Trail amendments (Items 25-26), Southside update (Item 29), and Rustic Oaks and Del Webb planning items (Items 32-35). agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Housing Inspections, Permit Stop-Work Order & Medicaid Expansion Resolution

agenda_items.title: City Hall Envelope Project Presentation

Council members, including Diane Catotti, discussed Planning Department basement water issues and potential relocation to the City Hall Annex second floor, as well as distinguishing aesthetic upgrades from needed structural repairs.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting June 17, 2013
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council (six present, Howard Clement III absent) presented proclamations for Parks and Recreation Month, Solid Waste Employees Appreciation Day, Fill the Bus Day, and Olympic Day. Council adopted the FY 2013-2014 Budget and 2014-2019 Capital Improvement Plan via the consent agenda (6-0 overall), though Council Members Steve Schewel and Diane Catotti recorded No votes on Item 5(d), the new monthly solid waste capital recovery fee, and Council subsequently debated how Durham County's potential budget changes on warrant control could impact joint City-County Planning Department funding. Council also unanimously approved street paving on Clover Hill Place, CDBG/HOME Annual Action Plan reconciliations, the sale of 48 Southside lots, an Erwin Road right-of-way closure for Duke University, and municipal election filing fees.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations and Council Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented four proclamations: July as Parks and Recreation Month (to Director Rhonda Parker), June 17 as Solid Waste Employees Appreciation Day (to Director Donald Long), August 3 as Fill the Bus Day (to Crayons2Calculators and Durham Regional Association of Realtors), and June 23 as Olympic Day. Council also recognized the Duke University lacrosse championship, Deputy Manager Wanda Page's appointment to the UNC Board of Visitors, and scheduled July 31 appointee evaluations.

agenda_items.title: City Manager and City Clerk Priority Items (Items 20, 29, and Supplemental Item 38)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield requested referring Item 20 (FY 2014 Planning Department Work Program) back to administration and referring Item 29 (East Cornwallis Road sewer main assessment roll) back for rescheduling in August, which Council approved 6-0. City Clerk D. Ann Gray requested adding Supplemental Item 38 setting filing fees for the November 2013 municipal election, which Council approved 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption Including FY 2013-2014 Budget, FY 2014-2019 CIP, and Monthly Solid Waste Fee (Item 5d)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent items 1 through 27 (excluding referred items 20 and 29, and reserving items 28-32 on General Business), notably including Item 5, the FY 2013-2014 Budget and FY 2014-2019 Capital Improvement Plan. Council Members Steve Schewel and Diane Catotti requested that their votes on Item 5(d)—establishing a monthly rollout solid waste capital recovery fee—be recorded as No because they viewed the flat fee as regressive and preferred funding trucks through property taxes. Council approved the consent package 6-0 with Catotti and Schewel recorded as No on Item 5(d) (4-2).

agenda_items.title: City-County Interlocal Funding Discussion: Warrant Control Program and Planning Department
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following budget adoption, Mayor Bill Bell raised concerns from Durham County Commissioners over the city's decision to end funding for the Sheriff's warrant backlog program and suggested that if the County reduces its share of the joint City-County Planning Department budget, the City could fund long-range planning independently. Council Members Diane Catotti and Steve Schewel stressed that protecting long-range planning—especially affordable housing around future transit—is essential and supported city funding if needed, while Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden noted communication gaps with commissioners and Council Member Eugene Brown urged avoiding a public conflict with County government.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Street Paving on Clover Hill Place (Dunwoody Subdivision)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Robert Joyner of Public Works presented Item 28 under enabling act authority to order street paving on Clover Hill Place in the Dunwoody Subdivision from South Riverdale Drive through the cul-de-sac. No Council members or members of the public offered comments during the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Proposed Amendments to FY 2009-2013 Annual Action Plans (CDBG & HOME)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and Federal Programs Coordinator Wilma Conyers presented formal amendments to the FY 2009-10 through FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plans to reconcile approximately $1,357,071.86 in CDBG funds and $1,699,621 in HOME funds with the city's general ledger and meet HUD expenditure deadlines. No public comments were made at the hearing.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Proposed Sale of 48 Lots in Southside
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Larry Jarvis of the Department of Community Development explained that because some homebuyers in the Southside redevelopment are not low- or moderate-income, the city must disclose terms and sell the 48 lots to homebuilders at appraised fair market value. Staff requested authorization for the sales contracts and conveyance documents. No public speakers appeared.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Street Closing of 109 Linear Feet of Erwin Road (SC1200004)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented Case SC1200004, a request by Duke University to close approximately 109 linear feet by 1.5 feet of Erwin Road right-of-way due to an existing retaining wall encroachment in front of the hospital. All internal departments and utility providers found no issues and no public speakers objected.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item: Ordinance Fixing Filing Fees for Municipal Office Candidates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council took up Supplemental Item 38 added by the City Clerk to establish filing fees for candidates running in the November 2013 Durham municipal election and approved it without debate before adjourning at 7:39 p.m.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Items: Refer Item 20 (FY14 Planning Work Program) and Item 29 (East Cornwallis Sewer Assessment) Back to Administration
votes.notes: Item 29 rescheduled for first meeting in August. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Tom Bonfield requested two priority agenda modifications: referring Item 20, the proposed FY 2014 Planning Department Work Program, back to City Administration, and referring Item 29, the East Cornwallis Road sewer main assessment roll, back to be rescheduled for the first meeting in August. Council moved, seconded, and approved the referrals 6-0 without discussion.

votes.item_title: City Clerk Priority Item: Add Supplemental Item 38 (Municipal Election Filing Fees)
votes.notes: Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: City Clerk D. Ann Gray presented a priority request to add Supplemental Item 38 to the evening's agenda, an ordinance setting candidate filing fees for Durham municipal offices ahead of the November 2013 election. Council moved, seconded, and unanimously approved adding the item 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 28: Resolution Ordering Street Paving on Clover Hill Place (Dunwoody Subdivision)
votes.notes: Enabling act authority inside city limits. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Robert Joyner of Public Works Development Review presented Item 28, recommending adoption of a resolution under enabling act authority to order street paving on Clover Hill Place in the Dunwoody Subdivision from South Riverdale Drive through the cul-de-sac. No Council members asked questions and no members of the public signed up or spoke during the public hearing. Council closed the hearing and approved the resolution 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 30: Approval of Proposed Amendments to FY 2009-2010 through FY 2012-2013 Annual Action Plans
votes.notes: Reconciles CDBG (~$1.36M) and HOME (~$1.70M) grant funds for HUD submission. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and Federal Programs Coordinator Wilma Conyers presented proposed amendments to four fiscal years of Annual Action Plans (FY 2009-10 through FY 2012-13) to reconcile grant funds to the city's general ledger—approximately $1,357,071.86 in CDBG and $1,699,621 in HOME funds—and satisfy HUD timely expenditure guidelines. Staff noted the amendments were advertised in the Herald-Sun and Carolina Times and posted for a 30-day review from May 16 through June 17. With no public comments or council objections, Council closed the hearing and approved the amendments 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 31: Authorization of Sale of 48 Lots in Southside
votes.notes: Authorizes City Manager to execute sales contracts at appraised fair market value. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Larry Jarvis of the Department of Community Development reported that because some homebuyers for homes built on 48 Southside lots will not be low- or moderate-income, the city was required to hold a public hearing disclosing the terms and sell the properties at appraised fair market value. Staff requested authorization to sell the lots at the indicated values and allow the City Manager to execute conveyance contracts with homebuilders. No Council questions or public comments were raised, and Council approved the authorization 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 32: Street Closing Case SC1200004 (109 Linear Feet of Erwin Road)
votes.notes: Requested by Duke University for retaining wall encroachment. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented Case SC1200004, a request by Duke University to close approximately 109 linear feet of Erwin Road by a width of roughly 1.5 feet to resolve an existing retaining wall encroachment in front of the hospital. Internal city departments and service/utility providers reviewed the request and identified no issues, and staff recommended approval. With no questions or public speakers, Council closed the hearing and approved the street closing 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 38: Ordinance Fixing Filing Fees for Municipal Office Candidates
votes.notes: Supplemental item for November 2013 municipal elections. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Following its addition to the agenda as a priority item by City Clerk D. Ann Gray, Council took up Supplemental Item 38, an ordinance setting candidate filing fees for municipal office in the City of Durham for the November 2013 election. No further discussion occurred, and Council approved the ordinance 6-0.

disagreements.issue: Funding Solid Waste Fleet Replacement via Monthly User Fee vs. Property Tax (Item 5d)
disagreements.summary: Council split 4-2 on establishing a monthly solid waste capital recovery fee to pay for sanitation truck fleet replacement, with two members arguing the flat fee is regressive compared to a property tax increase.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the monthly solid waste fee as proposed in the FY 2013-2014 budget to create a dedicated revenue stream for truck fleet replacement.
side_a_arguments: Provides dedicated funding for urgent solid waste truck fleet replacement.
Adopted as part of the balanced FY 2013-2014 budget package.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the flat monthly solid waste user fee and fund needed solid waste vehicles through the property tax instead.
side_b_arguments: A flat monthly fee on households is regressive compared to property taxation.
Both dissenting members supported purchasing the additional solid waste trucks but objected to the fee structure.
disagreements.resolution: Item 5(d) passed 4-2 as part of the Consent Agenda adoption of the FY 2013-2014 Budget, with Diane Catotti and Steve Schewel recorded as voting No.

disagreements.issue: City-County Interlocal Funding for Sheriff's Warrant Control and Joint Planning Department
disagreements.summary: Council members discussed Durham County Commissioners' dissatisfaction over the end of city funding for the warrant backlog program and potential county cuts to the joint City-County Planning Department, weighing independent city planning funding against preserving interlocal cooperation.
disagreements.side_a_position: If Durham County reduces its share of joint Planning Department funding over the warrant program dispute, the City should step in to fund long-range planning independently rather than let planning capacity shrink.
side_a_arguments: The city fulfilled its multi-year commitment to eliminate the warrant backlog and is doing more planning within city jurisdiction.
Under the interlocal structure, a county funding cut triggers a comparable city cut unless addressed, threatening critical long-range planning such as affordable housing around future transit stops.
disagreements.side_b_position: Avoid escalating an interlocal battle with Durham County government and clarify administrative communication regarding agreements.
side_b_arguments: Durham faces sufficient policy challenges from Raleigh and Washington, D.C., and needs City-County unity for all residents.
County Commissioners reportedly felt unaware that the warrant agreement had ended, indicating a need for clearer communication between administrations and elected boards.
disagreements.resolution: Informational discussion only; Item 20 (FY14 Planning Department Work Program) had been referred back to City Administration for revision and return in August.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden in Mayor Bill Bell's absence, the Durham City Council reviewed consent items, environmental and youth-program citizen requests, planning work-program priorities, and emergency sewer repairs. Council unanimously accepted priority items—including an emergency change order for the Ellerbe Creek aerial sewer crossing replacement project (Item 37) and adding John Tarantino to Citizens Matters—as well as closed-session requests for attorney-client consultation and a personnel matter. During Citizens Matters, Blue Hills Environmental Defense League sought city support to phase out perchloroethylene ('perc') at dry-cleaning contamination sites, and Council invited the group to submit a draft resolution directed to NC DENR since the city lacks direct regulatory authority. Council also questioned staff on omitting urban farming (aquaponics and commercial composting) from the Planning Department's FY 2013-14 work program, seasonal Parks and Recreation worker exemptions under the living wage ordinance, and downtown streetlighting options before suspending the rules to unanimously approve Item 37 and setting the regular agenda.

agenda_items.title: Durham Bulls vs. Cuba Announcement, Priority Items & Closed Session Requests
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Eugene Brown announced that the Durham Bulls would host the Cuban National Team on July 23. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (emergency Item 37 Ellerbe Creek aerial sewer crossing change order and adding John Tarantino to Citizens Matters), the City Attorney's closed-session request under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), and a personnel closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6)/(a)(1).

agenda_items.title: Agenda Read-Through
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed the agenda including FY 2012-13 budget ordinance amendments (Item 4), the FY 2013-14 Budget and FY 2014-19 CIP (Item 5), Price Steel Place Housing Inc. loan modification (Item 6), outdoor passenger information AVL and bus refurbishment transit items (Items 26-27), East Cornwallis Road sewer assessment (Item 29), annual action plan amendments (Item 30), public hearing on selling 48 Southside lots (Item 31), and an Erwin Road street closing (Item 32).

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Blue Hills Environmental Defense League (Perc) & Youth Programs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers included Scott Barn (Item 33), Blue Hills Environmental Defense League regarding perchloroethylene ('perc') groundwater contamination (Item 34), Stanback internship program (Item 35), and Campaigning for Change youth basketball/trade summer program seeking funding (Item 36). On Item 34, staff and Council explained the city lacks statutory authority to ban perc directly and suggested the group submit a proposed resolution urging NC DENR to phase out perc.

agenda_items.title: DDI Budget, Downtown Streetlighting, Living Wage Seasonal Exemption & Planning Work Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council questioned staff on a $31,000 administrative reapportionment within Downtown Durham Inc.'s budget (Item 10), connecting Southside subcontractors to the Durham Job and Career Center, downtown streetlighting design options up to $817,000 with Duke Energy and NCDOT, and whether seasonal Parks and Recreation workers receive the city living wage (staff confirmed short-term seasonal positions are exempt). On Item 20, Council questioned Pat Young (Planning) on deferring urban farming follow-ups (aquaponics and commercial composting) due to prioritization and confirmed 0.9 FTE allocated to affordable housing density bonuses and the transit-adjacent housing assessment.

agenda_items.title: Emergency Change Order No. 1: Ellerbe Creek Aerial Sewer Crossing Replacement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management staff presented an emergency change order to replace two failing sewer lines with a single line, build a new junction box, and line adjacent 30-inch sections, funded from existing CIP sewer rehabilitation collection system funds. After a brief exchange on adopting the gender-neutral term 'personhole' in place of 'manhole,' Council suspended the rules and unanimously approved Item 37.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda & Entering Closed Session

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting June 3, 2013
meetings.executive_summary: The marathon June 3, 2013 Durham City Council meeting featured the city's first live E-Town Hall and public hearing on the proposed FY 2013-14 budget, drawing heavy citizen opposition to a proposed $18 solid waste fee and $0.50 bus day-pass increase alongside calls for $750,000 in supportive housing and Ellerbe Creek Trail funding. Council unanimously approved a $400,000 GE Aviation incentive package (7-0), a West Cornwallis Road rezoning (7-0), and the annual Evaluation and Assessment Report (7-0), while referring the Eno Economic Development District plan amendment back to staff (7-0) following intense resident environmental and safety objections. In the night's defining split vote, Council rejected (3-4) the 253-acre 751 South conditional annexation and utility extension agreement—with Brown, Catotti, Moffitt, and Schewel opposing Jordan Lake watershed risks and General Assembly threats, over the yes votes of Mayor Bell, Clement, and Cole-McFadden.

agenda_items.title: Welcome to NCCU Chancellor Debra Saunders-White, Juneteenth Proclamation, and Moral Monday Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council welcomed incoming NCCU Chancellor Dr. Debra Saunders-White and proclaimed June 15, 2013 as North Carolina African American Independence Day (Juneteenth). Council Member Howard Clement III requested adding a resolution to Thursday's work session in support of Rev. William Barber and the Moral Monday movement in Raleigh.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-7, 10-15)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda, including board appointments, the April bid report, a resolution opposing Duke Energy's rate increase, the Next Step Housing/CASA merger, DBAP lighting and seating contracts, solid waste and recycling contracts, parking fee changes, and e-billing vendor selection. Items 8 and 9 were pulled for separate discussion.

agenda_items.title: FY 2013-14 Proposed Budget E-Town Hall and Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: WTVD anchor Anthony Wilson moderated Durham's first interactive budget E-Town Hall, where council members fielded questions on jobs, Ellerbe Creek Trail funding, affordable housing, police/fire pay, solid waste fees vs. property taxes, water rates, and the new police headquarters. In the subsequent public hearing, speakers urged opposing the $18 solid waste fee and $0.50 bus day-pass increase, allocating $750,000 for supportive housing, funding Ellerbe Creek Trail, and preserving housing inspection staff; Schewel advocated a sub-one-cent property tax increase to replace the regressive fees, while Bell defended fee-for-service benchmarking.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Proposed Bus Fare Increases
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell opened the separate public hearing on proposed DATA bus fare increases, folding in all transit comments from the budget hearing. Victoria Peterson urged generating revenue by leasing the empty second floor of Durham Station and charging Greyhound and Megabus rather than raising rider fares.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement: GE Aviation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD Director Kevin Dick presented a $400,000 performance-based incentive (paid over FY16-FY20) for GE Aviation to invest $29 million in new jet-engine manufacturing technology and create 50 jobs averaging $60,000 per year at its Miami Boulevard facility, generating $557,000 in gross new property taxes. Chamber leaders Ted Conner and Casey Steinbacher praised GE's zero-layoff record and high-school aviation academy outreach, while Victoria Peterson urged minority training and certification.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: 800 West Cornwallis Road (A13-02)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented FZH Management's request to change 0.174 acres at 800 West Cornwallis Road from Medium Density Residential to Commercial, supported 13-0 by the Planning Commission. Realtor Kim Griffin explained the lot was needed to expand parking for the Pennies for Change thrift store serving Durham Crisis Response Center.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: 800 West Cornwallis Road (Z13-03)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the companion rezoning of 800 West Cornwallis Road from RS-10 to Commercial General. Council Member Diane Catotti confirmed that a 20-foot opaque buffer would be required along adjacent residential properties.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Eno Economic Development District (A12-00012)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a policy alignment of Durham's Future Land Use Map with Orange County's Eno Economic Development District small area plan near I-85 and US 70. Five nearby residents (Darcy Wilson, Dr. Sarah Glass, Chris Kelsey, Joseph Henderson, and Dr. John Harvick) opposed changing rural residential land to industrial near homes, the Stony Creek wildlife corridor, and winding Old NC 10, and reported never receiving mailed notices. Expressing surprise and concern over notice and cross-county coordination, Council referred the item back to planning staff.

agenda_items.title: 2013 Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented the annual Evaluation and Assessment Report updating Future Land Use Map open-space and agriculture layers, reconciling county-approved Alexander Park, and incorporating a UNC graduate student forecasting report. Council Member Don Moffitt praised the report's quality.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation Item: 751 South
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City staff presented a conditional voluntary annexation (effective June 3, 2023) and utility extension agreement for 253 acres (751 South and Colvard Farms), contingent on the NC General Assembly amending Durham's charter to allow a 10-year annexation deferral and requiring developer widening of NC 751. Six of seven speakers opposed the project over Jordan Lake watershed runoff, traffic, lack of legal authority before charter passage, and legislative coercion. After intense debate, Mayor Bell, Clement, and Cole-McFadden voted yes to secure road widening and charter protection, while Catotti, Moffitt, Brown, and Schewel voted no, defeating the measure 3-4.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Contract Amendment with Community Partnerships, Inc. (WIA Youth Framework)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Victoria Peterson pulled Item 8, questioning why more than half of the $175,000 budget went to staff salaries and requesting data on youth employment and GED outcomes. OEWD Director Kevin Dick explained the framework services for 140 out-of-school youth required a manager and three career counselors and exceeded federal goals; Mayor Bell directed staff to provide public aggregate numbers to Peterson.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Contract Amendment with Achievement Academy of Durham (WIA Youth Program Elements)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 9 to call for clearer public reporting breaking down how many youth in the Achievement Academy program earn GEDs, complete job training, or enter employment, and whether justice-involved youth are served. Mayor Bell asked City Manager Tom Bonfield to follow up with a report.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1-7, 10-15; excluding pulled Items 8 and 9)
votes.notes: Mayor Bell initially mentioned pulling Item 6 (Duke Energy rate increase resolution), then restated the motion excluding only Items 8 and 9.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bill Bell read the consent agenda items, including minutes, appointments to the Cultural Advisory Board, Housing Appeals Board, and Open Space and Trails Commission, the April bid report, a resolution on Duke Energy's proposed electricity rate increases, the Next Step Housing/CASA merger, Durham Bulls Athletic Park lighting and seating contracts, solid waste transport and recycling contracts, parking fee changes, and an electronic billing vendor selection. Although Bell initially remarked on pulling Item 6, the final restated motion excluded only Items 8 and 9 for separate consideration. Council approved the consent agenda 7-0.

votes.item_title: FY 2013-14 Proposed Budget Public Hearing — Acceptance of Comments and Closure
votes.notes: Closed the public hearing and accepted citizen comments ahead of June 6 budget work session.
votes.discussion_detail: Following an hour-long live E-Town Hall moderated by WTVD anchor Anthony Wilson, Council heard 15 public speakers during the formal budget public hearing. Speakers urged Council to reject the proposed $18 annual solid waste fee and the $0.50 bus day-pass increase, allocate $750,000 from dedicated housing funds for supportive housing for chronically homeless residents and veterans, fully budget matching funds for the Ellerbe Creek Trail extension, and retain a housing inspector position. Council closed the public hearing and voted 7-0 to formally accept the public comments into the budget deliberation record.

votes.item_title: Item 25: Close Public Hearing on Proposed Bus Fare Increases
votes.notes: Folded budget hearing bus-fare comments into Item 25 record; deferred staff presentation and decision to June 6 budget work session.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bill Bell opened Item 25, the dedicated public hearing on proposed DATA bus fare increases, explaining that transit fare testimony offered during the earlier budget hearing would be incorporated into this record. Victoria Peterson was the sole additional speaker, recommending that the city generate transit revenue by leasing the vacant second floor of Durham Station to vendors and charging Greyhound and Megabus for terminal access rather than raising fares on low-income riders. Bell noted staff would present the fare analysis at Thursday's work session, and Council voted 7-0 to close the public hearing.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Economic Development Incentive Agreement — GE Aviation
votes.notes: $400,000 performance-based incentive over FY16-FY20 tied to $29M capital investment and 50 jobs averaging $60,000/yr.
votes.discussion_detail: OEWD Director Kevin Dick presented a proposed $400,000 incentive agreement with GE Aviation, paid over five years (FY16-FY20) only after staff verifies a $29 million capital investment and 50 new manufacturing jobs averaging $60,000 annually at its Miami Boulevard plant, yielding an estimated $157,000 net tax gain to the city. Chamber of Commerce leaders Ted Conner and Casey Steinbacher highlighted GE's zero-layoff history in Durham since 1993 and its work with Durham Public Schools on aviation academies, while resident Victoria Peterson urged certification pathways for local African American workers. Council Member Diane Catotti spoke strongly in favor of securing high-wage jobs when 25% of Durham children live in poverty, and Council approved the agreement 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Comprehensive Plan Amendment — 800 West Cornwallis Road (A13-02)
votes.notes: 0.174-acre FLUM amendment from Medium Density Residential to Commercial.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented Case A13-02, a request by FZH Management to amend the Future Land Use Map for a 0.174-acre lot at 800 West Cornwallis Road from Medium Density Residential to Commercial, noting unanimous 13-0 Planning Commission support. Realtor Kim Griffin explained that property owner Fares Hanna purchased the adjacent lot to relieve severe parking shortages at 2715 Durham-Chapel Hill Boulevard, home to the Pennies for Change thrift store supporting the Durham Crisis Response Center. With no public opposition, Council approved the plan amendment 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Zoning Map Change — 800 West Cornwallis Road (Z13-03)
votes.notes: Rezoning of 0.174 acres from RS-10 to Commercial General (CG).
votes.discussion_detail: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented companion zoning case Z13-03 to rezone 0.174 acres at 800 West Cornwallis Road from RS-10 to Commercial General, consistent with the newly amended Future Land Use Map and the Planning Commission's 13-0 recommendation. Council Member Diane Catotti asked staff to verify required buffering along neighboring residential properties, and Medlin confirmed the ordinance mandated a 20-foot opaque buffer along Cornwallis Road. With Kim Griffin waiving additional remarks and no opposition present, Council approved the rezoning 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 22: Referral Back to Planning Staff — Eno Economic Development District Comprehensive Plan Amendment (A12-00012)
votes.notes: Referred indefinitely back to Planning staff for community outreach and re-advertisement.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning staff presented Case A12-00012 to align Durham's Future Land Use Map in the Eno Economic Development District (in Orange County near I-85 and US 70) with Orange County's 2008 small area plan and 2012 FLUM changes anticipating future city water/sewer extension. Five nearby residents—Darcy Wilson, Dr. Sarah Glass, Chris Kelsey, Joseph Henderson, and Dr. John Harvick—strongly opposed industrial land-use designations adjacent to homes, the Stony Creek wildlife corridor, and narrow Old NC 10, and reported that mail notices went to a similarly named street elsewhere in Durham. Expressing concern over the notice discrepancy and lack of clarity on Orange County's public process, Mayor Bell, Steve Schewel, and the City Manager supported Planning Director Steve Medlin's recommendation to refer the case back to staff for community engagement and re-advertisement, which passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 23: 2013 Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR)
votes.notes: Rectified FLUM with Alexander Park county plan amendment, updated conservation easement layers, and adopted policy text updates.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented the annual Evaluation and Assessment Report, which updated the open-space and agriculture layers for permanent conservation easements, rectified the Future Land Use Map to reflect Durham County's Alexander Park plan amendment (Case 1108), and incorporated a land-use forecasting report prepared by UNC graduate volunteers Holly Safi and Daniel Band. Medlin reported a 13-0 Planning Commission endorsement. Council Member Don Moffitt praised the exceptionally high quality of the report and moved approval. With no public speakers, Council approved the EAR 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 24: Consolidated Annexation and Utility Extension Agreement — 751 South
votes.notes: Conditional 10-year annexation (effective June 3, 2023) contingent on NC General Assembly charter amendment; defeated 3-4.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning and Legal staff presented the 253-acre 751 South / Colvard Farms utility extension and conditional 10-year annexation (effective June 3, 2023), made contingent on the General Assembly passing a charter amendment extending Durham's deferral window from 3 to 10 years and requiring the developer to widen NC 751. Six speakers—Helen Fisher, Steve Bocckino, Susan Sewell, Donna Rudolph, Carolyn Aaronson, and Tom Miller—opposed the deal over Jordan Lake watershed runoff, traffic, lack of statutory authority before charter passage, and legislative extortion, while Victoria Peterson urged approval for jobs and tax revenue. Mayor Bill Bell, Howard Clement III, and Cora Cole-McFadden supported the agreement as the best way to secure NC 751 widening and charter protection before expected legislative coercion, whereas Diane Catotti, Don Moffitt, Eugene Brown, and Steve Schewel voted no, citing comprehensive plan violations, the addition of Colvard Farms without updated fiscal analysis, developer absence, and refusal to yield to General Assembly threats. Catotti moved the item with the stated intent to vote no, and it failed 3-4.

votes.item_title: Item 8 (Pulled): Contract Amendment with Community Partnerships, Inc. (WIA Youth Framework Services)
votes.notes: Pulled for public questions by Victoria Peterson; staff directed to provide aggregate outcome data.
votes.discussion_detail: Resident Victoria Peterson questioned Item 8, a $175,000 WIA Youth Framework contract amendment with Community Partnerships, Inc. for July–December 2013, objecting that roughly $140,000 funded staff salaries and benefits while 93 youth remained in-progress without clear job or GED counts. OEWD Director Kevin Dick explained that serving 140 out-of-school youth ages 16–21 required a program manager and three career counselors for intake, case management, GED preparation, and occupational training, and noted the provider helped Durham exceed federal common measures. Mayor Bell directed Dick to provide aggregate public outcome numbers (without youth names) to Peterson, and Council approved the contract amendment 7-0.

votes.item_title: Item 9 (Pulled): Contract Amendment with Achievement Academy of Durham (WIA Youth Program Elements)
votes.notes: Pulled by Victoria Peterson; City Manager asked to provide outcome reporting.
votes.discussion_detail: Victoria Peterson also pulled Item 9, the July–December 2013 WIA Youth Program Element Services contract amendment with Achievement Academy of Durham, requesting itemized public reporting showing how many participating youth were working on GEDs, completing hospital or job training, or placed in employment, and whether youth with criminal records were served. Mayor Bell asked City Manager Tom Bonfield to follow up with Peterson offline to provide the requested reporting. Council then approved the contract amendment 7-0.

disagreements.issue: 751 South Conditional 10-Year Annexation and Water/Sewer Extension Agreement (Item 24)
disagreements.summary: Council split 3-4 on whether to approve water and sewer extension and a conditional 10-year annexation for the 253-acre 751 South / Colvard Farms project under threat of NC General Assembly intervention.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the conditional agreement to lock in NC 751 road widening and secure a 10-year annexation charter amendment.
side_a_arguments: Mayor Bill Bell warned that state legislative leaders had stated in no uncertain terms that the General Assembly would force Durham to extend water and sewer if the city did not reach an agreement.
Without this agreement, Durham could be forced to provide utilities without developer-funded widening of NC 751 and without the 10-year annexation charter change to protect future city budgets.
Cora Cole-McFadden noted she distrusted the players but respected the Mayor's effort to salvage concessions, and Howard Clement III joined in voting yes.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject the utility extension and conditional annexation on planning, environmental, legal, and anti-coercion grounds.
side_b_arguments: Diane Catotti noted the request grew from 167 to 253 acres (adding Colvard Farms) without an updated cost-benefit analysis, criticized the developers' absence, and cited past protest-petition and watershed-boundary maneuvers.
Don Moffitt argued the project undermined the comprehensive plan and drove sprawl toward Chatham County instead of transit-oriented growth near Page Road and I-40.
Eugene Brown and Steve Schewel condemned General Assembly 'extortion' and refusal to negotiate with a 'gun to our heads,' warning of Jordan Lake water-quality risks.
disagreements.resolution: Motion failed 3-4.

disagreements.issue: FY 2013-14 Budget Revenue Strategy: Property Tax vs. Solid Waste Fee and Bus Fare Increases
disagreements.summary: During the budget E-Town Hall and public hearing, council members and residents debated whether to replace the proposed $18 annual solid waste fee and $0.50 bus day-pass hike with a modest property tax increase.
disagreements.side_a_position: Eliminate the solid waste fee and bus day-pass increase and fund them (plus employee pay/trails) with less than a one-cent property tax increase.
side_a_arguments: Council Member Steve Schewel and speakers from People's Alliance, Durham CAN, and People's Durham argued the $18 solid waste fee and $0.50 bus day-pass increase are regressive and disproportionately harm low-income renters and transit-dependent families.

Property taxes are progressive and federally deductible for itemizers, unlike municipal fees, and less than one penny on the tax rate could cover the bus pass, solid waste fee, Ellerbe Creek Trail, and employee pay.
disagreements.side_b_position: Keep property taxes flat and evaluate fee-for-service benchmarking against peer cities.
side_b_arguments: Mayor Bill Bell noted that Council directed the City Manager to propose a balanced budget without a property tax increase and pointed out that peer North Carolina cities fund services through user fees rather than relying solely on property taxes.
Council Member Don Moffitt noted fees charge service users directly while property taxes spread costs across the whole community.
disagreements.resolution: Public hearing closed 7-0; final budget and fee decisions deferred to the June 6 budget work session and subsequent adoption vote.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Preliminary FY 2013-2014 Budget Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Continuing its two-day preliminary FY 2013-2014 budget review on May 30, 2013, the Durham City Council examined departmental proposals from Finance, Risk Management, Public Safety, and Transportation. Finance Director David Boyd reported eliminating one vacant print shop position due to iPad-driven printing reductions, earning $96,000 in electronic payment rebates and 0.62% on a $238 million investment portfolio, consolidating all five Risk Management staff and operating costs into a single Risk Internal Service Fund, and budgeting up to $200,000 in new state transaction fees on 160,000 registered motor vehicles. In the afternoon, Council flagged several items for deeper review, including the $150,000 city share of the Gang Reduction Strategy program, forensic lab accreditation staffing (three mid-year FTEs in a five-year 11-FTE plan), partial-year Gang Assistant District Attorney funding questioned by Diane Catotti, and whether sworn officers are needed in the elementary-school GREAT program flagged by Eugene Brown. Members also reviewed federal MPO funding obligation rules requiring complete right-of-way acquisition and daily bus fare proposals before scheduling a three-hour budget balancing session for the following Thursday; no formal votes were taken.

agenda_items.title: Finance Department & Risk Management Fund Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director David Boyd presented the department's 48-FTE budget, eliminating one vacant print shop position as Council iPad use reduced printing and vehicle deliveries. Boyd detailed accounts payable metrics, $96,000 in e-payment rebates, 62 basis points earned on a $238 million investment portfolio, business license discovery, consolidation of all five Risk Management positions into a single Risk Internal Service Fund, and up to $200,000 in projected state motor vehicle tax/tag transaction fees.

agenda_items.title: Public Safety Flagged Items: Forensics, Gang Programs, Mental Health & School Policing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed public safety budget items including the $150,000 city share for the Gang Reduction Strategy program, three mid-year FTEs toward an 11-FTE police forensics lab expansion and accreditation, cutbacks in 24/7 warrant control and mental health clinician staffing, and Diane Catotti's questions on three-month/50% Gang ADA funding. Council Member Eugene Brown and colleagues also flagged the elementary-school GREAT program to evaluate whether sworn officers are needed versus middle and high school SROs.

agenda_items.title: Capital Project Right-of-Way Acquisition & Federal MPO Funding Rules
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council and staff discussed $75,000 in right-of-way acquisition funding and federal MPO requirements that projects be 95% designed with all property acquired ('shovel ready') before federal funds can be obligated for bidding. Staff cautioned against imposing a hard six-month acquisition deadline that could undermine negotiations.

agenda_items.title: Transit Fares, Parking & Scheduling of Budget Balancing Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council noted that the proposed budget includes daily bus pass fare changes and parking garage rates while the on-street parking meter study had not yet come to Council. Members agreed to hold a three-hour budget balancing session at 10:00 a.m. the following Thursday prior to the regular work session to resolve roughly eight flagged items after Monday's public hearing.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Preliminary FY 2013-2014 Budget Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Opening the first day of its preliminary FY 2013-2014 budget work sessions on May 29, 2013, the Durham City Council reviewed citywide revenue projections, General Services and venue budgets, and Parks and Recreation operations. Staff outlined the item-flagging procedure for new Council Member Don Moffitt and reported that public safety accounts for 48% of the General Fund ($86 million and roughly 1,000 employees) while property taxes supply 54% of revenues amid slow property and sales tax growth and no tax rate increase. Budget staff also explained a forecasting shift to projecting 2% property tax growth on end-of-year estimates rather than adopted budgets. In the afternoon, General Services presented cemetery revenue tracking, new change-order project management metrics, a $500,000 roof/envelope fund, an $11.3 million budget (with the Ballpark Fund dropping from $849,000 to $438,385), and DPAC/Convention Center operating and maintenance arrangements. Parks and Recreation detailed a two-position reduction in force alongside adding one facility maintenance technician for trails and parks, while Council expressed concern over nagging deferred maintenance such as park driveways; no formal votes were taken.

agenda_items.title: Budget Work Session Procedures & General Fund Revenue Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained the two-day budget flagging workflow for Council Member Don Moffitt and noted Water Management part-time staffing changes would be clarified outside the presentation schedule. Budget staff presented General Fund revenue trends—54% from property taxes, 48% of spending dedicated to public safety ($86 million)—and a shift to forecasting 2% property tax growth off end-of-year estimates amid uncertain state vehicle tax changes.

agenda_items.title: General Services Department, Ballpark, Convention Center & DPAC Budget Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services reviewed weekend/holiday burial revenues and an upcoming September cemetery study, new project management metrics tracking change orders, $500,000 for building roof/envelope repairs, and an 80.79% employee survey participation rate. Staff also outlined an $11.3 million budget ($10.9 million General Fund, $438,385 Ballpark Fund), holding the Convention Center transition deficit to $1 million, and DPAC's $40,000/25-year repair-and-replacement schedule.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting May 20, 2013
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council (six present, Howard Clement III absent due to illness) opened with a National Public Works Week proclamation and the Cole-McFadden Diversity Change Agent awards, then unanimously approved the consent agenda and received City Manager Tom Bonfield's proposed $381 million FY 2013-2014 budget presentation. Council approved 6-0 a water extension agreement on East Geer Street after staff addressed annexation questions from Council Member Diane Catotti. Following an extended, contentious public hearing on Item 10—Greenfire Development's request to remove local historic landmark designation from Liberty Warehouses No. 1 and No. 2 to allow a $50 million mixed-use redevelopment by East West Partners—Council voted 6-0 to de-list the property despite unanimous opposition from the Historic Preservation Commission, Planning staff, and the State Historic Preservation Office.

agenda_items.title: National Public Works Week Proclamation and Cole-McFadden Diversity Change Agent Awards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented a proclamation declaring May 19-24, 2013 as National Public Works Week to Public Works Director Marvin Williams. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden then presented the 2013 Cole-McFadden Diversity Change Agent Awards to two co-honorees, Human Resources Manager Ruby Hargrove-Monds and City Hall custodian John Conyers.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Adoption (Items 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent items covering the overtime performance audit, stormwater utility fee audit, High Intensity Drug Trafficking Areas (HIDTA) grant amendment, 2013 street repairs/repaving contract ST-265, residential water meter replacement phase 4 with Vanguard Utility Service, and the Michie Lake Facility Master Plan. Items 6, 9, and 10 were reserved for the General Business Agenda.

agenda_items.title: Presentation of Proposed FY 2013-2014 Budget and FY 2014-2019 Capital Improvement Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield presented the proposed $381 million FY 2013-2014 budget ($170 million General Fund), maintaining the 56.75-cent property tax rate while cutting $1.5 million and 16 positions, funding 2% general and 3-5% public safety pay increases, introducing a $1.50/month solid waste capital recovery fee, expanding DATA transit funding and multi-day pass fares, and allocating $53 million in CIP projects. Bonfield honored absent Council Member Howard Clement III's 30-year anniversary on Council, and Mayor Bell announced two days of budget work sessions on May 29-30.

agenda_items.title: Water Extension Agreement with Urcy Enterprises, LLC (2722 East Geer Street)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Robert Joyner of Public Works Development Review presented a water extension agreement for 2722 East Geer Street due to a documented failed well, noting staff provided requested follow-up explaining why annexation was not pursued for this single lot. Council Member Diane Catotti moved approval, thanking staff for the analysis while urging that future utility extension requests be accompanied by annexation request analyses.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Local Historic Landmark Designation Removal (LD1200003) — Liberty Warehouses No. 1 and No. 2
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented Greenfire Development's application to remove local historic landmark status from Liberty Warehouses No. 1 and No. 2 (611-613 Rigsbee Avenue), noting that Planning staff, the State Historic Preservation Office, and the Historic Preservation Commission recommended denial because the last remaining downtown tobacco auction warehouse retained historic integrity. Thirteen speakers testified: Greenfire's Paul Smith, East West Partners' Roger Perry (proposing a $50M mixed-use workforce housing and commercial project yielding ~$850,000/year in taxes), Preservation Durham leaders Josh Parker and Wendy Hillis (supporting de-listing under a negotiated partial-preservation and memorialization agreement), developers, and business owners urged de-listing, while HPC Chair Heather Wagner and residents John Martin, Peter Katz, and Debbie Pratt opposed de-listing or questioned process transparency and stayed $500/day neglect fines. After extensive council deliberation—including Don Moffitt calling for ordinance changes to assess interest/penalties on repaid tax breaks and Steve Schewel questioning HPC process confidence and securing non-binding commitments from Perry on local retail, workforce rents, and Liberty Arts—Council voted 6-0 to de-list the property.

votes.item_title: Item 6: Water Extension Agreement with Urcy Enterprises, LLC to Serve 2722 East Geer Street
votes.notes: Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Robert Joyner of Public Works Development Review presented the water extension agreement for Urcy Enterprises, LLC at 2722 East Geer Street, explaining the property had a documented failed well and that staff had supplied supplemental information addressing why annexation was not pursued at this time. Council Member Diane Catotti thanked the City Manager and staff for answering her work session inquiry, acknowledged management concerns about inefficiencies on a single lot, and moved approval while reiterating that future utility extension requests should come paired with annexation analyses. The motion was seconded and passed 6-0.

votes.item_title: Item 10: Local Historic Landmark Designation Removal (Case LD1200003) for Liberty Warehouses No. 1 and No. 2
votes.notes: Overruled unanimous denial recommendations from the Historic Preservation Commission, Planning Department, and State Historic Preservation Office. Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning Director Steve Medlin reported that Case LD1200003 sought removal of the 2010 local landmark designation for Liberty Warehouses No. 1 and No. 2 (611 and 613 Rigsbee Avenue) and that Planning staff, the State Historic Preservation Office, and the Historic Preservation Commission all recommended denial. Applicant Paul Smith (Greenfire Development) and prospective buyer Roger Perry (East West Partners) argued the roof-damaged warehouse was economically unviable to preserve intact and unveiled a $50 million mixed-use plan backed by a compromise letter with Preservation Durham (Wendy Hillis and Josh Parker) to integrate the southern brick wall, northeastern facade, signs, and recycled wood. HPC Chair Heather Wagner and residents John Martin, Peter Katz, and Debbie Pratt urged Council to uphold landmark criteria, keep deliberations in public HPC channels, and explain why $500/day demolition-by-neglect fines were halted (which Medlin explained were automatically stayed by the UDO upon application filing). All six present Council members spoke in favor of de-listing to enable downtown redevelopment, though Don Moffitt urged amending the ordinance to add interest and penalties on repaid tax credits and Steve Schewel questioned the community's lack of confidence in the HPC process while obtaining verbal assurances from Perry regarding workforce rents, local retail, and Liberty Arts; Council voted 6-0 to de-list the property.

disagreements.issue: Removal of Local Historic Landmark Designation for Liberty Warehouses No. 1 and No. 2 (Case LD1200003)
disagreements.summary: A sharp policy debate arose over whether City Council should revoke the local historic landmark designation of Liberty Warehouses No. 1 and No. 2 to facilitate a $50 million private redevelopment based on a negotiated developer-Preservation Durham compromise, overriding the Historic Preservation Commission's unanimous denial recommendation.
disagreements.side_a_position: De-list Liberty Warehouse as a local historic landmark to enable East West Partners' $50 million mixed-use redevelopment and Preservation Durham memorialization compromise, while reforming the HPC process separately.
side_a_arguments: Adaptive reuse of the deteriorated 200,000 sq ft warehouse is economically infeasible after years of failed attempts and a 2011 roof collapse.
Preservation Durham negotiated a compromise retaining the southern brick wall, northeastern facade, signs, and old wood, and documenting tobacco auction history.
Redevelopment brings $50M investment, workforce housing, Central Park connectivity, and ~$850,000/year in city real estate and sales taxes.
Landmark designation only delays demolition by one year anyway, and waiting further will not save the building.
disagreements.side_b_position: Deny the de-listing application under UDO Section 3.17 criteria, keep review within public Historic Preservation Commission channels, and maintain enforcement against demolition by neglect.
side_b_arguments: Liberty Warehouse remains Durham's last surviving downtown tobacco auction house and still meets cultural and architectural landmark criteria (unanimous HPC, Planning staff, and SHPO finding).
De-listing based on a developer's redevelopment proposal rather than objective historic merit undermines the entire local landmark program.
Removing landmark status eliminates binding preservation commitments and relies on private negotiations held outside public HPC review.

Critics questioned why $500/day demolition-by-neglect fines against Greenfire were stayed and argued owners should face interest/penalties when repaying tax benefits (a point Moffitt echoed for future ordinance reform).
disagreements.resolution: Council voted 6-0 to de-list Liberty Warehouses No. 1 and No. 2; Don Moffitt requested future ordinance changes to assess interest/penalties on repaid tax credits, and Steve Schewel noted ongoing Planning staff focus groups to rebuild confidence in the HPC process.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Opened by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden before Mayor Bill Bell arrived to preside over the latter half of the session, the Durham City Council addressed Southside environmental remediation, capital project contingencies, and annexation authority. After initially pausing a rules-suspension vote so a member could ask questions, Council discussed ravine soil contamination (PAHs, burnt wood, and lead paint) on the Southside multifamily rental site, heard staff critique NC DENR delays while crediting DENR's Brownfields program for approving a lower-cost cap-and-cover remedy saving roughly $750,000, and suspended the rules to unanimously approve the CDBG contract amendment with McCormack Baron Salazar (Item 3). Council Member Steve Schewel also questioned whether built-in engineering project contingencies encourage full expenditure, prompting staff to note quarterly contingency reporting under Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson. Finally, following discussion of a water/sewer extension for a property with failing well/septic systems, Council suspended the rules and unanimously authorized the Durham legislative delegation to pursue a city charter change extending the annexation effective-date window from three to ten years.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items, Agenda Review & Citizens Matters (Alzheimer's Association)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (Item 3 CDBG amendment, updated Item 7 meter replacement contract with Vanguard Utility Service, and an American Tobacco Trail time-lapse video) and the City Attorney's priority legislative item. Following agenda review—covering audits (Items 1-2), HIDTA grant (Item 4), Lake Michie master plan (Item 8), FY 2013-14 budget presentation (Item 9), and Liberty Warehouses landmark removal (Item 10)—Citizens Matters featured the Alzheimer's Association Eastern NC promoting its September 21 Walk and June 1 charity football game.

agenda_items.title: Engineering Project Contingency Practices & Quarterly Reporting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained that construction contingencies range from 5% to 20% depending on subsurface uncertainty versus vertical construction. Council Member Steve Schewel questioned whether budgeting contingencies encourages departments to spend up to the cap; the City Manager noted Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson was establishing quarterly contingency reporting across Water Management, Public Works, and General Services.

agenda_items.title: Southside Multifamily Rental CDBG Environmental Remediation Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After deferring an earlier vote for questions, Council discussed soil contamination found in a ravine at the Southside multifamily site (asbestos-free soils with polyaromatic hydrocarbons, burnt wood, and lead paint). Staff and members expressed frustration with NC DENR responsiveness that drove up costs before DENR's Brownfields program agreed to cap-and-cover under a parking lot, saving about $750,000; after receiving assurances costs were now known, Council suspended the rules and unanimously approved Item 3.

agenda_items.title: Water/Sewer Extension Annexation Policy & Proposed 10-Year Charter Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed extending water and sewer to an out-of-city property with failing well and septic systems while reserving the city's annexation option under Durham's three-year charter authority. Mayor Bill Bell then circulated a memo proposing a local bill to extend that charter annexation effective-date window from three years to ten years; emphasizing keeping the bill noncontroversial with legislators, Council suspended the rules and unanimously authorized the delegation to pursue the charter change.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the regular meeting agenda with Consent Items 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, and 8, GBA Items 6 and 9, and GBA Public Hearing Item 10 (with Item 3 already approved).
