Items 8, 11, 17, 19, and 21-23 were on General Business.

agenda_items.title: Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC) Operating Agreement Modification and Extension
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield presented modifications and a multi-year extension to the DPAC operating agreement with Durham Performing Arts LLC (Nederlander and Professional Facilities Management), noting that after Mayor Bell and Council Member Don Moffitt raised work-session concerns over a proposed profit incentive at the $2 million level, staff renegotiated an alternate incentive at the $3 million level. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden cited $43.7 million in visitor spending and $4.5 million in tax revenues, and Moffitt, Eugene Brown, and Steve Schewel praised the revised split and PFM/Nederlander partnership before PFM CEO Lynn Singleton addressed Council.

agenda_items.title: Durham Bulls Athletic Park (DBAP) 20-Year Lease and Development Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services Director Joel Wright and Finance Director David Boyd presented a new 20-year lease (effective Jan. 1, 2014, with two 5-year renewal options) and development agreement with the Durham Bulls Baseball Club, shifting day-to-day operating costs and preventive maintenance up to $200,000/year to the club, setting $125,000 base rent plus additional rent, capping city capital improvements at $12 million ($6M deferred maintenance, $6M new improvements) with a minimum $2M club investment, and yielding over $7 million in nominal General Fund savings (~$200,000/year). Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden cited $24.1 million in 2010 visitor spending and $3.3 million projected from the 2014 AAA All-Star Game, and Council Members Don Moffitt, Steve Schewel, and Eugene Brown praised Capitol Broadcasting's partnership; Bulls President Mike Goodman thanked Council.

agenda_items.title: 2013 First Quarter Crime Summary Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Jose Lopez presented the Q1 2013 crime report showing Part 1 crime at a 14-year first-quarter low (down 4%, violent crime down 12%, burglaries down 15% aided by the RAP initiative) and clearance rates above FBI peer averages, while noting an increase in motor vehicle thefts (including scooters and unlocked/running cars). Council Member Steve Schewel raised concerns about 12 firearms violations by 15-year-olds and inadequate state funding for pretrial release programs, Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden inquired about youth tracking under age 16, and Mayor Bell and Council Member Eugene Brown requested breakdowns on key-left-in-car thefts and progress against copper theft.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Confirmation of Assessment Rolls (Donphil Road and Hersey/Percy Street)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Nathan McKinney of Public Works presented assessment rolls for the Donphil Road water main and Hersey/Percy Street sewer main, recommending confirmation of both rolls except for Sasha Delago's objected property on Donphil Road, which staff recommended continuing to the June 17, 2013 meeting. No public comments were offered.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2014 Stormwater Rate Increase
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant Stormwater Director Paul Wiebke presented an ordinance increasing residential stormwater rates by $2.85 to $11.82 per year across tiers effective July 1, 2013, generating over $1 million for capital projects to meet Falls Lake and Jordan Lake Stage 1 nutrient reduction goals. Council Member Steve Schewel asked whether Durham was covering costs given lower rates than peers (Wiebke confirmed 98% billing recovery), and Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden asked about legal advertising in the Carolina Times. No public speakers appeared.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Update on Water and Sewer Connection Charges
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management Director Don Greeley presented updated water and sewer connection fees effective July 1, 2013 to recover city installation costs for new services (misstated by the Mayor initially as Item 23). Council Member Steve Schewel confirmed that the fees cover full costs despite being lower than peer cities, and no public speakers appeared.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Update on Water and Sewer Capital Facilities Fees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Don Greeley presented updated water and sewer capital facilities fees charged to new homes and businesses to fund treatment capacity expansion based on the financial rate model, explaining in response to Steve Schewel that fees are lower than peers like Cary due to differing utility capital needs. Schewel also questioned Public Works Director Marvin Williams on why the out-year stormwater model projected only 2.0% increases, and Williams explained major capital projects would finish in 3-4 years; no public speakers objected.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Convene Closed Session (GS 143-318.11(a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Patrick Baker confirmed no public action was expected following closed session, and Council voted 5-0 to adjourn into closed session for attorney-client consultation in the City Council Conference Room.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Item: Revision to Item 13 (Dunwoody Subdivision Street Completion)
votes.notes: Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Tom Bonfield informed Council that the motion and recommendation for Agenda Item 13 (completion of a street in the Dunwoody Subdivision) had been revised to incorporate the $6,000 increase in the city's contribution discussed at the prior work session. Council moved, seconded, and approved accepting the City Manager's priority item 5-0 without further debate.

votes.item_title: City Attorney Priority Items: Revision to Item 11 Attachment 14 and Addition of Closed Session
votes.notes: Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: City Attorney Patrick Baker notified Council of two priority items: a revision to Attachment 14 (upset bid resolution) on Item 11 for the Durham Bulls Athletic Park lease and development agreement, and a request for a closed session at the conclusion of the meeting for attorney-client consultation under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3). Council approved the City Attorney's priority items 5-0.

votes.item_title: Item 8: Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC) Operating Agreement Modification and Extension
votes.notes: Reflects renegotiated operating profit incentive threshold moved from $2M to $3M. Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Tom Bonfield presented the proposed modification and extension of the DPAC operating agreement with Durham Performing Arts LLC (Nederlander and PFM), explaining that following work-session concerns raised by Mayor Bell and Council Member Don Moffitt regarding an incentive at the $2 million operating profit level, staff renegotiated an alternate incentive threshold at $3 million. Mayor Bell, Don Moffitt, Eugene Brown, and Steve Schewel all commended the renegotiated profit split and the five-year track record of PFM and Nederlander, while Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden highlighted $43.7 million in FY 2011-12 visitor spending and $4.5 million in tax revenues (plus $3 per-ticket revenue). After Cole-McFadden spoke in favor and a final motion and second were made, Council approved the agreement 5-0, and PFM CEO Lynn Singleton thanked Council.

votes.item_title: Item 11: Durham Bulls Athletic Park (DBAP) 20-Year Lease Agreement and Development Agreement
votes.notes: Subject to statutory upset bid process (GS 160A-269) with revised Attachment 14. Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: General Services Director Joel Wright and Finance Director David Boyd presented the new 20-year DBAP lease (effective January 1, 2014, with two 5-year renewal options) and development agreement with the Durham Bulls Baseball Club, noting the Bulls will assume all operating expenses, utilities, and preventive maintenance up to $200,000/year while paying $125,000 base rent plus additional rent, saving the city over $7 million nominally (~$200,000/year) while capping city capital funding at $12 million ($6 million deferred maintenance and $6 million new improvements) alongside a minimum $2 million club investment. Moffitt moved the item, and Council approved it 5-0.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Confirmation of Assessment Rolls (Donphil Road Water Main and Hersey/Percy Street Sewer Main)
votes.notes: Confirms rolls except for Sasha Delago's property on Donphil Road, continued to June 17, 2013. Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Nathan McKinney of Public Works presented Item 19 to confirm assessment rolls for water main improvements on Donphil Road and sewer main improvements on Hersey/Percy Street. Because property owner Sasha Delago objected to the Donphil Road water main assessment, staff recommended confirming both rolls except for the Delago property and continuing the public hearing and objection for that parcel without further advertising to the June 17, 2013 meeting. With no public speakers, Council moved staff's recommendation and approved it 5-0.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Ordinance Amending FY 2014 Stormwater Rate Schedule
votes.notes: Effective July 1, 2013; generates over $1M for Falls Lake and Jordan Lake Stage 1 reduction goals. Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Assistant Stormwater Director Paul Wiebke presented the proposed FY 2014 stormwater rate increase raising residential annual fees by $2.85 to $11.82 across tiers to generate slightly over $1 million for capital projects toward Falls Lake and Jordan Lake Stage 1 nutrient reduction goals. votes.item_title: Item 22: Update on Water and Sewer Connection Charges
votes.notes: Effective July 1, 2013. Diane Catotti (excused) and Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Water Management Director Don Greeley presented an update to the fee schedule for new water and sewer connection charges effective July 1, 2013 to cover city installation costs for new service connections. meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Bill Bell with six members present (as confirmed by six-vote board appointments), the Durham City Council reviewed major venue leases, water and sewer rates, regional partnerships, and subdivision bond disputes. Council unanimously approved an excused absence for Council Member Diane Catotti on May 6 for a Regional Transportation Alliance transit tour, accepted the City Manager's priority items (referring Item 20, the Vermillion zoning map change, back to administration), and approved a closed-session request. Members resolved a Dunwoody Subdivision street completion dispute (Item 13) through an amended compromise resolution to avoid setting a negative precedent on inadequate developer performance bonds, and heard an annual update from Triangle J Council of Governments highlighting an 11-to-1 return on member dues and Eugene Brown's service as board chair. Council also received detailed presentations on a revised Durham Bulls Athletic Park lease and development agreement (lowering base rent from $150,000 to $125,000 and adjusting revenue sharing to 3% over $10.7 million) and proposed FY 2013-14 water and sewer rates supporting an $83 million utility budget while keeping Durham rates below the large-utility state average, before unanimously setting the agenda and entering closed session.

agenda_items.title: Artwork Donation, Catotti Excused Absence & Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council noted the donation of an artwork titled 'The Dream' to the city and unanimously approved Council Member Diane Catotti's excused absence for May 6 to attend a Regional Transportation Alliance transit tour. Council also unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items—including referring Item 20 (Vermillion zoning map change) back to administration—and the City Attorney's closed-session request under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3).

agenda_items.title: Agenda Read-Through & Dunwoody Subdivision Street Completion Compromise (Item 13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During agenda review—covering board appointments (Items 2-4), DPAC operating agreement (Item 8), SAMHSA/Alliance Behavioral Healthcare contract (Item 9), DBAP CIP/lease items (Items 10-11), and USGS streamflow network (Item 12)—Council discussed Item 13 regarding incomplete streets and inadequate developer performance bonds in Dunwoody Subdivision. Council members Steve Schewel and Eugene Brown endorsed an amended compromise resolution drafted with the City Attorney to assist residents without setting an adverse precedent.

agenda_items.title: Triangle J Council of Governments (TJCOG) Member Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: TJCOG presented its annual update, recognizing Durham delegate Eugene Brown as board chair and highlighting HUD preferred sustainability status, MPO/RPO air quality coordination, the North Carolina Next Generation Networks ultra-high-speed broadband initiative with Duke University and Durham, $1.3 million in aging pass-through funds to Durham County, and an 11-to-1 funding leverage on member assessments.

agenda_items.title: Durham Bulls Athletic Park (DBAP) Lease & Development Agreement Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and Durham Bulls representatives presented ballpark capital upgrades (including new video boards) and proposed lease amendments adjusting base rent from $150,000 to $125,000 per year and shifting revenue sharing from 4% over $3.2 million to 3% over $10.7 million. Council members scrutinized contract language, including Section 8.18.2 on ad valorem property taxes and surrounding parking garage revenues.

agenda_items.title: Proposed FY 2013-2014 Water and Sewer Rates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management presented proposed FY 2013-14 water and sewer rates supporting $1.8 billion in pipe infrastructure (80-100 year ductile iron replacements lowering average flow) and an $83 million budget (27% personnel, 31% O&M, 22% CIP, 20% debt service) while holding the dedicated penny flat. Staff noted declining industrial water usage and showed Durham's typical 4,000-gallon bill slipping further below the average of large North Carolina utilities.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Setting, Board Appointments & Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1-7 and 9-14 with Item 13 amended; GBA Items 8, 11, and 17; GBA Public Hearings 19, 21, 22, and 23). The Clerk announced appointments to the Workforce Development Board (five and six votes), Durham Planning Commission (six votes), and City County Appearance Commission (six votes), after which Council voted unanimously to enter closed session.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Bill Bell with six members present (Howard Clement III absent), the April 15, 2013 Regular City Council meeting opened with a moment of silence for the Boston Marathon bombings, the swearing-in of Fire Chief Daniel M. Currie, and proclamations honoring public safety telecommunicators, Earth Day, Smart Start's 20th anniversary, Downtown Durham Inc. leadership, and the Durham YMCA. Council unanimously (6-0) accepted and adopted Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden's supplemental resolution supporting action by the Centers for Disease Control, and passed Item 8 (amending City Code on dangerous weapons) 6-0 following public comment raising Second Amendment concerns. On pulled Item 17 (upset-bid sale of 1111 West Chapel Hill Street / City Tract 1835), Council voted 6-0 to excuse Council Member Don Moffitt due to a conflict of interest and heard 13 speakers debate whether the city should retain the parcel, reserve Council bid approval, or advance Self-Help Credit Union's Kent Corner redevelopment. Council then voted 5-0 (with Moffitt excused) to approve both Item 17 and Item 18, authorizing the City Manager to sign Kent Corners development plan applications as property owner.

agenda_items.title: Boston Marathon Moment of Silence, Fire Chief Swearing-In & Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell led a moment of silent meditation for the Boston Marathon bombings earlier that day before administering the oath of office to new Fire Chief Daniel M. Currie. Council also presented proclamations and recognitions for National Public Safety Telecommunicators, the Durham Earth Day Festival, Smart Start's 20th anniversary, outgoing Downtown Durham Inc. leadership on public-private partnerships (DBAP, DPAC, American Tobacco), and the Durham YMCA.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item Acceptance & Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 6-0 to accept the City Clerk's supplemental priority item (a resolution requested by Cora Cole-McFadden supporting action by the Centers for Disease Control). Council then read the consent agenda, pulling Item 8 (dangerous weapons code amendment) and Item 17 (upset-bid sale of 1111 West Chapel Hill Street) for separate discussion and public comment.

agenda_items.title: Resolution in Support of Action by the Centers for Disease Control (CDC)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden explained that the resolution had been endorsed by the National Black Caucus of Local Elected Officials and the National League of Cities to support CDC action, and moved its adoption. Council approved the resolution 6-0.

agenda_items.title: City Code Amendment Regulating Discharge and Possession of Dangerous Weapons
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson addressed Council raising Second Amendment and self-defense concerns regarding Item 8. After referring her to the City Attorney for statutory details and noting gun-violence concerns, Council voted 6-0 to approve the ordinance amendment.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Sale of 1111 West Chapel Hill Street by Upset Bid (City Tract 1835 / Kent Corner)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 6-0 to excuse Council Member Don Moffitt from Item 17 due to a conflict of interest per City Attorney guidance. Thirteen speakers—limited to two minutes each—presented mixed views, with Kent Corner task force members requesting Option 3 (final Council review of bids rather than City Manager selection) and others urging support for Self-Help Credit Union's neighborhood retail and jobs plan before Council passed the item 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Authorization to Sign Kent Corners Development Plan Applications on Behalf of the City
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Steve Medlin) explained that under the Unified Development Ordinance, all property owners—including the city for the parking lot parcel—must sign development plan applications submitted by Self-Help. After a speaker questioned accepting a site plan prior to property sale closing, Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval and Council passed Item 18 by a 5-0 vote (with Moffitt excused).

votes.notes: Electronic vote opened and closed by City Clerk, passing 6-0; Howard Clement III was absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted resolution supporting action by the Centers for Disease Control, previously endorsed by the National League of Cities.

votes.item_title: Item 8: Amendment to City Code Regulating Discharge and Possession of Dangerous Weapons
votes.notes: Electronic vote opened and closed by City Clerk, passing 6-0; Howard Clement III was absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved City Code amendment regulating discharge and possession of dangerous weapons following public comment.

votes.item_title: Excuse Council Member Don Moffitt from Item 17 Due to Conflict of Interest
votes.notes: Electronic vote opened and closed by City Clerk, passing 6-0; Howard Clement III was absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Formally excused Council Member Don Moffitt from participating in Item 17 due to a conflict of interest identified by the City Attorney.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Proposed Sale of 1111 West Chapel Hill Street by Upset Bid (Parcel ID 114009 / City Tract 1835)
votes.notes: Electronic vote passed 5-0; Don Moffitt was formally excused for conflict of interest and Howard Clement III was absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the upset-bid sale process for 1111 West Chapel Hill Street (City Tract 1835) after hearing 13 public speakers regarding Kent Corner redevelopment and Self-Help Credit Union.

votes.notes: Electronic vote passed 5-0; Don Moffitt was excused for conflict of interest on the Kent Corners property and Howard Clement III was absent.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Bill Bell with five members present (Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden was excused to attend a funeral), the April 4, 2013 City Council work session focused heavily on the Southside neighborhood revitalization package and board review timeliness. Council unanimously approved Cole-McFadden's excused absence, accepted the City Manager's priority items (pulling Items 10-14 for an overview of Southside projects), and approved a closed-session request for *Robinson Taylor v. City of Durham*. Council expressed concern that Historic Preservation Commission deferrals on new construction were delaying quality downtown development and urged advisory boards to act deliberately yet promptly. On Items 10-14, staff detailed Southside homebuyer financing with Duke University incentives ($145,000–$196,000 home prices, 51% low-to-moderate income requirement, and priority for displaced former residents), announced Duke University's voluntary fire-service contribution rising to $400,000 in FY 2013-14, recommended B. Wallace Design & Construction and Andrew Roby General Contractors as builders and D.H. Griffin for site prep, and reviewed Rolling Hills environmental remediation cost overruns with developer McCormack Baron Salazar. Council unanimously set the 40-item regular agenda and entered closed session.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence, HPC Timeliness Discussion & Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously excused Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden's absence due to a funeral. Members then voiced concern over Historic Preservation Commission delays and deferrals on new downtown construction projects, urging advisory commissions to be timely, before approving the City Manager's priority items (pulling Southside Items 10-14) and the City Attorney's closed-session request for *Robinson Taylor v. City of Durham*.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Read-Through & Pulled Consent Questions (Attendance Reports, Weapons Ordinance)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed 40 agenda items including pedal-pub open-container rules (Item 7), dangerous weapons (Item 8), FY 2013-14 budget guidelines (Item 9), Lake Michie land acquisition (Item 16), DNC police equipment donation (Item 26), Orange County solid waste transfer (Item 28), Jordan Lake Partnership contracts (Items 32-33), the 2013 Strategic Plan (Item 34), and Triangle Curling Club rezoning (Items 39-40). agenda_items.title: Proclamations for TRY Prevention, Sexual Assault Awareness Month, and Fair Housing Month

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Opened by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden while Mayor Bill Bell was en route (with Howard Clement III excused absent), the March 21 work session covered affordable housing timelines, consent items, citizen complaints on roadside solicitation, and transit funding. Council received an update that Rolling Hills site preparation was delayed by unforeseen environmental remediation, though 80 of 132 units remained on track for tax-credit compliance, and suspended the rules to approve revisions to the city's right of reentry for Goley Pointe (Item 6) to enable LLC ownership transfer for construction loan closing. Citizens raised residential solicitation concerns, which the City Attorney agreed to research alongside First Amendment constraints. Council also debated Triangle Transit fare-increase scenarios—including charging seniors and students half-fare and raising base fares by 10 to 15 cents to help close a $1.6M–$1.7M FY14 transit funding gap—before unanimously settling the agenda and entering closed session.

agenda_items.title: Rolling Hills Affordable Housing Construction Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Responding to Eugene Brown, City Manager's Office representative Keith Chadwell reported that Rolling Hills site preparation experienced delays due to remediating unforeseen environmental discoveries. Chadwell stated that 80 of the 132 planned units remain on schedule for December completion to maintain tax-credit compliance, while the remaining units may be delayed past December.

agenda_items.title: Priority Item: Revision to City Right of Reentry for Goley Pointe
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested suspending the rules to vote on Item 6, revising the city's right of reentry for Goley Pointe. After Dallas Parks of the Durham Housing Authority explained that combining six DHA lots and five DBI lots into a single LLC was required to close the construction loan and existing restrictions preserved low-income/homeless housing uses, Council suspended the rules and approved the item.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: Mutual/Rockwood Loan Restructuring, SLBE, and Rezoning Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council pulled and questioned several agenda items, including minutes (Item 1), the Randolph Avenue railroad watchmen item (Item 3), the Small Local Business Enterprise ordinance (Item 7), sick-pay conversion (Item 10), and Triangle Curling Club land-use items (Items 18–19). On Item 5 (loan restructuring for Mutual/Rockwood), members examined allowing the developer to retain roughly $10,000 per year in interest while losing under-30% AMI units to preserve project viability.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Roadside Solicitation in Residential Areas
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers Scott Bart and John and Tammy Kobani raised citizen complaints about roadside solicitation, litter, and perceived intrusion near residential homes. The City Attorney noted he was reviewing the solicitation ordinance with staff amid First Amendment limitations and agreed to research whether street-level newspaper sales in residential areas are permissible.

agenda_items.title: FY 2014 Transit Budget Gap and Proposed Fare Increase Scenarios
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and Triangle Transit reviewed FY14 transit budget projections showing a $1.6M–$1.7M shortfall after losing $800,000 in federal Bull City Connector funds and $300,000 in state aid, alongside two-step fare increase options and a scenario charging seniors and youth half-fare. Council members debated ridership elasticity impacts on low-income passengers versus raising base cash fares by 10 cents and whether to authorize TTA public comment forums before the manager's May budget release.

agenda_items.title: Settling the Upcoming Meeting Agenda and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted unanimously by voice vote to settle the upcoming meeting agenda (Consent Items 1, 3–5, and 7–12; GBA Item 2; GBA Public Hearings 16–19). Council then voted unanimously to enter a closed session following a three-minute break.

votes.notes: Mayor Bell arrived shortly after roll call; Howard Clement III excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager requested suspending rules to act on Item 6 ahead of construction loan closing.

votes.item_title: Item 6: Resolution Authorizing Revision to City's Right of Reentry for Goley Pointe
votes.notes: Howard Clement III excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved after DHA confirmed existing restrictions maintain low-income/homeless housing requirements when lots transfer into a single LLC.

votes.item_title: Setting the Meeting Agenda (Consent 1, 3-5, 7-12; GBA 2; Public Hearings 16-19)
votes.notes: Howard Clement III excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Council adopted the consent, GBA, and public hearing lineup as outlined by the City Manager.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Howard Clement III excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted to recess for three minutes and convene in closed session.

disagreements.issue: Proposed Transit Fare Increases and Senior/Student Half-Fare Policy
disagreements.summary: Council members debated whether to consider bus fare increases and charging seniors and youth half-fare to help offset a projected $1.6M–$1.7M FY14 transit deficit.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support testing modest fare increases (such as a 10-cent base fare increase) and gathering public forum feedback to help close the transit budget gap.
side_a_arguments: A 10-cent fare increase would not fill the full $1.3M–$1.6M gap alone, but riders should contribute something rather than placing the entire burden on taxpayers.
A dime increase is unlikely to cause severe ridership losses, and public forums would provide data before May budget decisions.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose raising fares on existing riders and especially oppose charging seniors and students without specific local data.
side_b_arguments: Fare elasticity disproportionately pushes the poorest riders off transit first.
Changing free-fare policies for seniors and youth was not clearly flagged in earlier briefings and lacks specific local ridership impact data.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken; City Manager clarified the discussion was to inform whether TTA should hold public comment forums ahead of May budget recommendations.

meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present under Mayor Bill Bell, the March 4 regular meeting featured proclamations honoring late longtime Duke Power bus driver Horace Calvin Hitchpap and MS Awareness Week, alongside unanimous 7-0 votes accepting the Clerk's priority notice of a valid protest petition on Item 21 (Meadows at Southpoint) and approving Consent Items 1–15. agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented a proclamation honoring the late Horace Calvin Hitchpap ('Seven-Up Baker'), a longtime Duke Power bus driver on the Roxboro Street route, accepted by family members, followed by a proclamation designating March 11–17, 2013 as MS Awareness Week. agenda_items.title: Clerk Priority Item (Item 21 Protest Petition) and Consent Agenda Approval

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change — Meadows at Southpoint

disagreements.issue: Item 21: Meadows at Southpoint Rezoning, Density, and Barbee Road / NC 54 Traffic
disagreements.summary: Council split 5-2 over approving the Meadows at Southpoint rezoning, falling one vote short of the six-vote supermajority required by a valid protest petition.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the rezoning with newly modified roadway timing and $150,000 City of Durham transportation contribution commitments.
side_a_arguments: The applicant met repeatedly with neighbors over nearly a year, reduced density, dropped Tract 3, and made major concessions.
The I-40 corridor location is appropriate for density, and all proffered road improvements are tied prior to the first certificate of occupancy.
Blocking development leaves Barbee Road improvements unfunded because private land and developer contributions are part of fixing the corridor.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the rezoning in deference to impacted neighborhood residents and unresolved traffic and infrastructure concerns.
side_b_arguments: Nearby residents strongly opposed the proposed project and questioned whether future development could offer equal or different protections.

disagreements.resolution: Motion to approve failed 5-2 at 03:10:21 (failing to reach the 6-vote supermajority required by the valid protest petition).

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present under Mayor Bill Bell, the February 18 regular meeting began with 7-0 approval of the City Clerk's protest-petition notices (valid petitions on Items 15 and 16; invalid petition on Item 18) and the consent agenda excluding pulled Item 11. Council unanimously approved the Victoria Praise Fellowship Church rezoning (Item 15, 7-0) following a neighbor agreement on sound orientation, heard contentious buffer and fence disputes on 2125 Guess Road (Item 16), and later passed Item 18 (Southpoint Trails rezoning) by a split 4-3 vote—with Don Moffitt and Steve Schewel explicitly named as voting No (the third No vote and individual Aye breakdown among Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Howard Clement III were not captured in the transcript digest). Council then unanimously adopted the 231-unit Brier Creek Towns rezoning (Item 19, 7-0), the 53-home Montclair consolidated annexation (Item 20, 7-0) despite Schewel's general reservations on density south of I-40, and pulled Consent Item 11 (Riverworks stream restoration, 7-0).

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden (with Diane Catotti and Howard Clement III absent and Mayor Bell reported en route), the February 7 work session approved manager and clerk priority items, including referring Item 10 (Clean Water Management Trust Fund resolution) back to staff and suspending the rules to act on Item 12 (Jordan Lake stormwater policy options). During citizens matters, Open Table Ministry director Carolyn Schult urged Council to repeal roadside panhandling Ordinance 14375, arguing it harms vulnerable unhoused residents without resolving poverty. Council unanimously adopted the color-coded Jordan Lake and statewide stormwater policy positions (Item 12)—favoring having the state resume issuing Jordan buffer impact letters to relieve city staff—and approved a member's excused absences for upcoming PAC meetings. Steve Schewel and a colleague also signaled skepticism toward piecemeal density increases south of I-40 (Items 18 and 20) before Council settled the February 18 agenda.

agenda_items.title: Manager and Clerk Priority Items (Item 10 Referral, Item 12 Rule Suspension, Protest Petitions)

The Clerk also reported valid protest petitions on Items 15 and 16; Council approved all priority items by unanimous voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Request to Repeal Roadside Panhandling Ordinance 14375
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reverend Carolyn Schult, executive director of Open Table Ministry, urged Council to repeal Ordinance 14375 restricting roadside panhandling. While acknowledging safety and litter concerns, Schult argued the ordinance eliminates nearly all viable locations for unhoused residents without cars or internet access and increases trauma and dependence on public agencies.

agenda_items.title: Stormwater Policy Options Update (Jordan Lake Rules and Proposed Statewide Rules)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After suspending the rules to vote at the work session, Council reviewed staff's green/yellow/red matrix staking out Durham's legislative positions on Jordan Lake and statewide stormwater rules. Staff explained that returning Jordan basin buffer-impact letter reviews to the state Division of Water Quality—matching the Neuse River basin—would reduce city staff workload, and Council unanimously adopted the report.

agenda_items.title: Preview of South-of-I-40 Density Requests (Southpoint Trails & Montclair)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Schewel expressed reluctance to approve density increases south of I-40 in Items 18 and 20 without a compelling exception, citing clear community desire to keep development low-density and lack of staff support. Another member concurred on evaluating future land use south of I-40 comprehensively rather than piecemeal while remaining open to hearing the cases.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Bill Bell opened the February 4 regular meeting by delivering his 11th Annual State of the City address alongside a 2012 Year in Review video, emphasizing conservative fiscal management for a manageable $5.2 million budget deficit, neighborhood revitalization, violent-crime reduction (including upcoming public input on East Main Street vs. Fairview Street sites for a new police facility), transit improvements funded by the voter-approved sales tax, and tax-base growth. Following the address, Council approved the consent agenda (6-0) and held the FY 2013–2014 Annual Action Plan Needs Public Hearing (Item 16) for projected CDBG, HOME, and ESG federal funds with no action required. Council voted 6-0 to continue both Meadows at Southpoint items (Items 17 and 18) to March 4 at staff and community request, and unanimously approved the Covington Hall comprehensive plan amendment (Item 19, A1200007) and companion mixed-use rezoning (Item 20, Z1200016) by 6-0 votes.

agenda_items.title: Mayor Bill Bell's 11th Annual State of the City Address and 2012 Year in Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell reviewed 2012 highlights via video—including National Night Out, Project Homeless Connect, MindMixer parks outreach, Hillandale Golf Course renovations, and over 53,000 JobLink visits—and outlined five 2013 priorities. He highlighted a $5.2 million budget deficit, uncertainty in state and federal aid (including $300,000 less state transit funding and city absorption of state/county justice costs), East Main vs. Fairview police facility site selection, and 2014 transit expansions.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval

With no public speakers, Mayor Bell closed the public hearing with no action required.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the January 24 work session approved priority items adding the Clean Water Management Trust Fund to Council's legislative policy agenda, endorsing draft pretrial release bond legislation (G.S. 15A-533) for firearms cases, and accepting a valid protest petition on Meadows at Southpoint (Item 18). Equal Opportunity Director Deborah Giles presented the proposed race- and gender-neutral Small Local Business Enterprise (SLBE) program for construction contracts under $500,000 (Item 15), and staff clarified the $94,000 Housing for New Hope rapid rehousing budget (Item 5) pulled by Cora Cole-McFadden. Mayor Bell also presented six-month magistrate data showing 74 of 209 firearms-related defendants fell under the proposed pretrial bond categories, with eight who would have been held up to three days before court appearance. Council then suspended the rules to appoint Workforce Development Board members (following five-vote ballot tallies), approved closed sessions for Shaner SPE v. City of Durham, Hackney v. City of Durham, and a personnel matter, and settled the February 4 agenda.

agenda_items.title: Legislative Agenda Additions, Pretrial Firearms Bond Draft, and Protest Petition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved manager, attorney, and clerk priority items: confirming addition of the Clean Water Management Trust Fund to the legislative agenda, advancing draft G.S. 15A-533 pretrial firearms bond legislation, noting a second City Council seat could be created on the Workforce Development Board (in which Steve Schewel expressed interest), and recording a valid protest petition on Meadows at Southpoint (Item 18).

agenda_items.title: Consent and Public Hearing Agenda Review (Items 5 and 18 Pulled)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent and public hearing items, with Cora Cole-McFadden pulling Item 5 (Housing for New Hope rapid rehousing) for budget clarity and Mayor Bell pulling Item 18 (Meadows at Southpoint) to question street platting procedures and whether Huntsman Drive would be extended.

agenda_items.title: Presentation: Proposed Small Local Business Enterprise (SLBE) Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Equal Opportunity & Equity Assurance Director Deborah Giles presented the proposed race- and gender-neutral SLBE program modeled on Charlotte's ordinance, targeting construction contracts of $500,000 or less after noting $128.5 million in sub-$500,000 city contracts largely stayed in North Carolina rather than specifically within the Durham MSA. Council members raised questions about contract revocation procedures, Durham resident employment targets, and managerial authority to add service categories.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Item: Housing for New Hope Rapid Rehousing Budget Breakdown
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Responding to Cora Cole-McFadden's inquiry on the $94,000 contract, presenters detailed the administrative allocation ($21,000 in the memo / $15,000 admin plus program management) and $920-per-household direct case management supporting a three-person team assisting with landlord negotiations, budgeting, ready-to-rent classes, move-in logistics, and follow-up.

agenda_items.title: Chief Magistrate Data on Proposed Pretrial Release Bond Firearms Legislation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell shared a spreadsheet compiled from Chief Magistrate Don Paschal covering six months of 2012 firearms-related arrests (~1.2 cases per day), showing 74 individuals met the proposed convicted-felon, pretrial-release, or probation criteria. Of those, 25 received bonds of $100,000 to $6 million, and eight individuals would have remained jailed up to three days until their court appearance under the proposed amendment.

Council also approved closed sessions for Shaner SPE v. City of Durham, Hackney v. City of Durham, and a personnel matter, and settled the February 4 agenda (Consent 1, 3–14; Public Hearings 16–20).

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Legislative Breakfast
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 23, 2013 Special City Council Legislative Breakfast—called to order while Mayor Bill Bell was delayed in traffic and later joined by Bell alongside City Manager Tom Bonfield, city staff, and members of Durham's General Assembly delegation including Senator Floyd McKissick and Representative Larry Hall—Senior Assistant to the City Manager Carmisha Wallace walked legislators through Durham's 2013 local and statewide legislative agenda. City staff and officials presented proposals to allow Durham to negotiate with Durham Public Schools to retain more than the statutory 10% administrative fee for collecting civil penalties (given 19% collection agency costs), increase beer and wine license fees per the League of Municipalities agenda, and fix 2011–2012 annexation referendum anomalies affecting unoccupied rights-of-way and donut holes. The most extensive substantive discussion centered on a proposed statewide amendment to N.C.G.S. 15A-533(f) establishing a rebuttable presumption against magistrate pretrial release for repeat firearm offenders, where visiting legislators and Judge Marcia Morey raised constitutional due process, ambiguity, and misdemeanor-breadth concerns, prompting staff to commit to narrowing the triggering offenses. Additional briefing items covered Division of Water Quality buffer rule implementation timelines, design-build procurement wording, and advocacy support for the Clean Water Management Trust Fund and the Metro Mayors agenda; no formal votes or Council split votes were taken during this informational breakfast.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Delegation Introductions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The meeting was called to order with an initial note that Mayor Bill Bell was delayed in traffic, and attending members of Durham's North Carolina General Assembly delegation—including State Senator Floyd McKissick (noted as a former eight-year City Council member) and Representative Larry Hall (District 29)—introduced themselves. Senior Assistant to the City Manager Carmisha Wallace welcomed the delegation on behalf of City Manager Tom Bonfield and staff, noting the agenda items had been vetted by the administration, City Attorney's office, Council work session, and the Durham Crime Cabinet.

agenda_items.title: Statewide Request: Collection of Civil Penalties with Durham Public Schools
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented draft statewide legislation amending the General Statutes so the City of Durham could negotiate with Durham Public Schools to retain more than the current 10% statutory cap for administering civil penalty collections. Finance Director David Boyd explained that current collection agency contracts cost 19%, so the city sought authority to recover actual collection costs up to a mutually agreed cap with the school district.

agenda_items.title: Beer and Wine License Fee Increase Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented draft legislation and benchmark fee comparisons to raise municipal beer and wine license fees set by state statute, noting the North Carolina League of Municipalities had adopted the proposal on its legislative agenda. Attending legislators cautioned that any fee or tax increase would face a challenging reception in the 2013 General Assembly and asked for comparisons with other North Carolina cities.

agenda_items.title: Annexation Law Cleanup: Unoccupied Rights-of-Way and Donut Holes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Discussion addressed unintended consequences of 2011 and 2012 state annexation legislation requiring referenda even for unoccupied rights-of-way and annexation donut holes, where having zero registered voters results in a 0-0 vote that automatically fails. Staff confirmed Durham was aligned with the League of Municipalities' legislative agenda to correct the donut hole and right-of-way provisions, and also touched on automatic aid agreements with neighboring jurisdictions such as Morrisville.

agenda_items.title: Pretrial Release Proposal for Repeat Firearm Offenses (N.C.G.S. 15A-533)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Mayor Bill Bell's arrival at 00:24:57, staff presented a revised statewide amendment adding subsection (f) to N.C.G.S. 15A-533—modeled on drug trafficking and criminal street gang provisions and omitting an earlier $300,000 bond figure—to create a rebuttable presumption holding repeat firearm offenders for judicial pretrial review. Visiting legislators and Judge Morey questioned constitutional due process implications, the ambiguity of 'reasonable cause to believe' versus conviction, potential inclusion of minor misdemeanors or city ordinance violations, and juvenile disposition limits; staff agreed to narrow the draft specifically to serious triggering offenses.

agenda_items.title: Water Quality Buffer Rules, Design-Build Provisions, and Advocacy Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Participants reviewed Division of Water Quality Section 401 buffer impact certification and whether a one-year or two-year delay was warranted for implementing new development rules, along with technical wording concerns ('without limitation') in design-build permitting legislation. Staff concluded with advocacy items supporting restoration of the Clean Water Management Trust Fund following state budget reductions and endorsing the Metro Mayors agenda before legislators offered brief outlook remarks on the 2013 General Assembly session and adjourned.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven seated Council members participating, the January 22, 2013 Regular City Council Meeting opened with a recognition of students, parents, and leadership from the Raleigh-Durham chapter of the National Black MBA Association's 2012 Leaders of Tomorrow program, followed by unanimous 7-0 approval of the City Clerk's priority items, consent agenda, and a ballot appointment to the Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden pulled three contracts—with Ricks-Howard Builders (Item 7), Biohabitats, Inc. (Item 8), and CDM Smith, Inc. (Item 9)—to press contractors on equal employment opportunity and minority recruitment practices, with Mayor Bell underscoring the Council's expectation of measurable minority hiring results before all three contracts passed 7-0. In public hearings, the Council unanimously (7-0) continued Item 12 (Victorious Praise Fellowship Church zoning map change with a valid protest petition) to by February 18 to allow neighborhood buffer negotiations, and unanimously (7-0) adopted Item 13 (UDO Text Amendment TC120011) establishing a 1,125-foot separation requirement for new state-licensed family care and group homes. The Council also unanimously (7-0) appointed Commissioner Ellen Reckhow to the Triangle Transit Board of Trustees and approved an excused absence for Council Member Eugene Brown; there were no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Silent Meditation, and Recognition of Leaders of Tomorrow Students
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. and led a moment of silent meditation. Council Member Howard Clement III recognized the Raleigh-Durham chapter of the National Black MBA Association's 2012 Leaders of Tomorrow students, their parents, and program director Marion Johnson following their presentation at a recent Rotary Club luncheon.

agenda_items.title: City Clerk Priority Items and Human Relations Commission Swearing-In
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk reported a valid protest petition on Item 12 (Victorious Praise Fellowship Church zoning map change) and a supplemental item requested by Mayor Bill Bell appointing Commissioner Ellen Reckhow to the Triangle Transit Board of Trustees, which the Council approved 7-0. A new appointee was also sworn in to the Human Relations Commission before the Council.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission Ballot
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Council unanimously (7-0) approved the consent agenda covering minutes, street acceptance, Employment and Training 2012–2014 and US EPA 2012–2015 grant project ordinances, and a Mountains-to-Sea Trail lease agreement with the State of North Carolina. Council members also cast paper ballots for Item 2 (Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission appointment), which the Clerk later reported at 01:28:53 passed with 7 votes.

agenda_items.title: Construction Contract with Ricks-Howard Builders for Parks and Recreation Operations Facility
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden to examine workforce diversity, Item 7 concerned a construction contract with Ricks-Howard Builders for the Durham Parks and Recreation operations facility. A company representative explained that entry-level hiring relied on walk-in applications that had not yielded African American applicants and acknowledged needing stronger outreach before Council approved the contract 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Biohabitats, Inc. Feasibility Study for Falls Lake Watershed Algal Turf Scrubber
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant Director of Public Works Paul Wiebke introduced Tim Burkett and Kevin Nunnery of Baltimore-based Biohabitats, Inc. to answer Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden's questions on minority recruitment and workforce composition for the Falls Lake nutrient-removal feasibility study. Following discussion of recruiting technical staff and increasing underrepresented representation, Council approved the contract 7-0.

agenda_items.title: CDM Smith, Inc. Engineering Services for Economic Development District Water and Sewer Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden questioned CDM Smith, Inc. on its workforce statistics and recruitment practices for the Economic Development District water and sewer engineering contract. Mayor Bill Bell seconded Cole-McFadden's emphasis that Durham is eager to see measurable results in minority hiring before the Council approved the contract 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Urban Growth Area (A120010)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Aaron Cain attested that all public hearings were properly advertised and introduced Plan Amendment A120010, removing Urban Growth Area references from the Durham Comprehensive Plan as directed by Council on October 15, 2012. Subsequent discussion of this item and Item 11 occurred within a middle segment truncated in the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Victorious Praise Fellowship Church (Continued)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During the public hearing on the Victorious Praise Fellowship Church rezoning, which carried a valid protest petition, neighbors reported that the church/developers had agreed to add a second-tier buffer near back decks and asked for time to review the revised plans once the HOA president returned from abroad. Council Members Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Don Moffitt supported a continuance so a compromise could potentially lead to withdrawal of the protest petition, voting 7-0 to continue the hearing to by February 18.

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment: Family Care and Group Homes Separation Requirement (TC120011)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented UDO Text Amendment TC120011, initiated by the Joint City-County Planning Committee and recommended 13-0 by the Planning Commission, establishing a 1,125-foot (375-yard) separation requirement for newly established state-licensed family care homes (4–6 residents) and group homes (7–12 residents) while grandfathering existing facilities. East Durham community speakers urged passage to prevent overconcentration of transitional homes in targeted revitalization neighborhoods, and Council adopted the amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item: Triangle Transit Appointment and Eugene Brown Excused Absence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Council voted 7-0 to appoint Commissioner Ellen Reckhow to the Triangle Transit Board of Trustees as the City-County representative through November 30, 2013. Following announcement of the 7-vote ballot result for the Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission, Council voted 7-0 to grant Council Member Eugene Brown an excused absence for Thursday's work session and adjourned at 8:32 p.m.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden—with Mayor Bill Bell noted as on his way and Council Member Diane Catotti having an excused absence—the January 10, 2013 City Council Work Session opened with unopposed voice votes approving an attorney-client closed-session consultation in Hackney v. City of Durham under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and receiving notice of a valid protest petition on Item 12 (Victorious Praise Fellowship Church). During Citizens Matters, Good Neighbors of 751 speakers protested Planning Commission action (TC110007) to eliminate the Development Review Board (DRB) from UDO wireless communication facility approvals, prompting planning staff to explain state statutory limits on discretionary site-plan review and confirm pending South Point Tower Case D12002020 would return to the DRB before the late-February ordinance change. In reviewing the upcoming agenda, Council questioned workforce training grant restrictions under EPA rules, praised the Mountains-to-Sea Trail lease agreement, and moved contract Items 7, 8, and 9 to the General Business Agenda at Cole-McFadden's request to question contractors on equal employment opportunity hiring statistics. The Council then unanimously set the upcoming meeting agenda by voice vote before recessing briefly to await outside counsel; no split or contested votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and City Attorney/Clerk Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order, with roll call noting Mayor Bill Bell was on his way, Council Member Diane Catotti had an excused absence, and Council Members Eugene Brown and Steve Schewel were present. By unanimous voice votes, Council approved the City Attorney's request for attorney-client consultation in Hackney v. City of Durham (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)) and received the City Clerk's notice of a valid protest petition on Item 12 (Victorious Praise Fellowship Church).

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: UDO Wireless Communication Facilities and Elimination of DRB (TC110007)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Representatives of Good Neighbors of 751 objected to Planning Commission Case TC110007 removing the Development Review Board from UDO site-plan review for freestanding concealed wireless towers, warning it would leave approvals to the Planning Director without citizen input and requesting a special use permit requirement or temporary moratorium. Planning staff responded that state law bars unelected boards from discretionary site-plan decisions unless quasi-judicial, confirmed pending Case D12002020 (South Point Tower) would return to the DRB prior to ordinance adoption in late February, and noted alternatives would be presented to the Joint City-County Planning Committee.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Local Economic Development Remarks and Community Tribute
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A second public speaker addressed Durham's economic history, small business owners, and community development funding. Council members also paused to acknowledge the passing and homegoing service of former DPAC usher, educator, and historian James Rogg.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review: Training Grants, Mountains-to-Sea Trail, and Contractor EEO Inquiries
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed upcoming consent and public hearing items, questioning Senior Workforce Development Manager Nicholas McCoy on Item 4 and Item 5 EPA green-jobs training restrictions in Northeast Central Durham, where EPA rules bar on-the-job training wages. Members praised Item 6 (Mountains-to-Sea Trail state lease connecting a 60-mile Durham trail network), while Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden pulled Items 7, 8, and 9 (Ricks-Howard Builders, Biohabitats, and CDM Smith) to the General Business Agenda to scrutinize workforce equal employment opportunity statistics.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda and Recess for Outside Counsel
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council confirmed the upcoming agenda with Items 1 and 3–6 on Consent, Items 2, 7, 8, and 9 on the General Business Agenda, and Items 10–13 as public hearings, approving the agenda unanimously by voice vote. Following the vote, the Council agreed to take a 16-minute recess while waiting for outside legal counsel to arrive for the closed-session briefing.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with six Council members present (Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, newly sworn Ward 3 Council Member Don Moffitt—unanimously elected earlier to succeed departing State Senator Mike Woodard—and Steve Schewel; Howard Clement III absent), the January 7, 2013 Regular City Council Meeting featured a tribute to Woodard and six unanimous 6-0 votes alongside one split 5-1 vote. On the Consent Agenda's statewide legislative proposal to tighten pretrial release/bail bond rules for repeat firearm offenders (referenced by Mayor Bell as Item 11 concerning bail bond pretrial release), the Council split 5-1: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Don Moffitt supported the proposal (Ayes), while Steve Schewel voted Nay, arguing that judges already exercise appropriate discretion, constitutional bail is non-punitive, and the bill would have no impact. All other recorded actions passed 6-0, including referring Street Closure Case SC-1200002 (Newman Street) back to administration, adding Supplemental Item 24, approving Item 22 (floodplain development permit) and Item 23 (major site plan D11-0018) for the McDonald's redevelopment at 1010 N. Miami Boulevard, appointing Diane Catotti (regular) and Steve Schewel (alternate) to the Transportation Advisory Committee, and approving pulled Consent Item 16 after clarifying third-party water sale restrictions in a Chatham County service agreement.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Recognitions, Seating of Don Moffitt, and Farewell Tribute to Mike Woodard
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., Eugene Brown led the Pledge of Allegiance, and roll call confirmed six members present with Howard Clement III absent. Following a presentation by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, Mayor Bell announced that the Council had unanimously elected and sworn in Don Moffitt to the Ward 3 seat vacated by State Senator Mike Woodard, then presented Woodard with a service plaque as Woodard offered farewell remarks to colleagues (noting regret that an absent colleague could not attend).

agenda_items.title: Priority Items: Newman Street Closure Referral (Item 21) and Supplemental Item 24
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested referring Agenda Item 21 (Street Closure Case SC-1200002, Newman Street) back to the administration, which passed 6-0. The City Clerk added Supplemental Item 24 (Transportation Advisory Committee appointments) at Mayor Bell's request, which also passed 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and Debate on Pretrial Release Bail Bond Legislative Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell reviewed consent items including board reappointments, Durham Hosiery Mill loan subordination, NC Urban Progress Zones reauthorization, a wireless water tank license, Falls Lake nutrient study, water infrastructure contracts, and pulled Item 16 (2007 Local Water Supply Plan). Council Member Steve Schewel spoke against the statewide bail bond/pretrial release proposal for repeat weapons offenses—citing judicial discretion, constitutional non-punitive bail principles, and lack of data—while Mayor Bell defended judicial monitoring and data collection, noting Schewel's 'no' vote (referenced as Item 11 concerning bail bond pretrial release) as Diane Catotti moved the consent agenda right before a transcript gap.

agenda_items.title: Floodplain Development Permit: McDonald's Redevelopment (1010 N. Miami Boulevard)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap in the transcript, expert testimony established that proposed sand filters would treat 100% of site runoff, reduce impervious surface near the special flood hazard area, eliminate direct access on Miami Boulevard, and add bicycle facilities and landscaping. Community representatives Vivian McCoy (PAC 1) and Donald Yarborough (Northeast Central Durham Leadership Council) testified to unanimous neighborhood support, and Council approved the permit 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Major Site Plan D11-0018: 1010 N. Miami Boulevard
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Major Site Plan D11-0018 as the companion application to the Item 22 floodplain development permit, confirming it satisfied all technical requirements and had Development Review Board approval. Council unanimously approved the site plan 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item: Transportation Advisory Committee Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk read the supplemental appointment appointing Council Member Diane Catotti as the regular member and Council Member Steve Schewel as the alternate member to the Transportation Advisory Committee. Council approved the appointments 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 16 and Chatham County Third-Party Water Distribution Clarification
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning to Item 16 (pulled earlier from the Consent Agenda), Mayor Bell questioned City Attorney Patrick regarding paragraph 5 of a Chatham County interlocal service agreement. After Patrick clarified that revised language explicitly bars Chatham County from distributing or selling water through third parties without manager approval, Council approved the pulled consent item 6-0 and adjourned at 8:07 p.m.

disagreements.issue: Statewide Bail Bond / Pretrial Release Legislative Proposal for Repeat Firearm Offenses
disagreements.summary: Council divided 5-1 on a proposed statewide general statute amendment restricting magistrate pretrial release for individuals on pretrial release for a weapons offense who are charged with a second weapons offense, with Steve Schewel dissenting on effectiveness and constitutional grounds.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support including the statewide pretrial release amendment in the City's legislative agenda.
side_a_arguments: Judges remain directly involved in setting bond when appropriate under the proposed statewide statutory amendment.
Monitoring individuals on pretrial release for weapons offenses provides critical data on court appearance rates, offense severity, and re-offending currently unavailable to local officials.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the bail bond / pretrial release legislative proposal.
side_b_arguments: Even in revised form, the proposal will not have an impact because judges already take repeat weapons offenses seriously and no data shows they fail to exercise appropriate discretion.
Constitutional principles prohibit punitive bail before guilt or innocence is established, limiting pretrial detention to ensuring court appearance and community safety.
Bail amounts would still ultimately be set despite the procedural delay.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 5-1 on the Consent Agenda (Steve Schewel recorded as voting No; Howard Clement III absent), with the proposal advancing to the Crime Cabinet.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 20, 2012 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the Council unanimously approved an excused absence for Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden for the January 10 work session, heard an inquiry from Council Member Steve Schewel regarding the timeline for a guns-in-parks ordinance, and voted unanimously to enter closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) regarding three Duke lacrosse lawsuits (Evans, McFadden, and Harrington v. City of Durham). In a substantive policy disagreement without a formal vote on the 2013 Long Session Legislative Agenda, Mayor Bill Bell advocated seeking a targeted statewide pretrial release amendment for offenders with prior illegal firearm convictions within five years or pending pretrial release, while Council Member Steve Schewel opposed the draft legislation on grounds of preserving judicial discretion and avoiding unintended expansion by the state legislature. During presentations, staff and consultants briefed the Council on the Durham Police Department Master Facilities Study, comparing a downtown headquarters facility against current $811,000 annual lease costs and evaluating north and south district service centers funded through lease savings. The Council concluded by recording board appointment tallies and unanimously setting the consent and public hearing agenda for the upcoming regular meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Excused Absences
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:00 p.m. and asked the clerk to call the roll. Council unanimously approved an initial excused absence motion and then unanimously granted Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden's request for an excused absence from the January 10, 2013 work session.

agenda_items.title: Council Inquiries, Officer Kelly Stewart Update, and Closed Session Motion (Duke Lacrosse Litigation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Steve Schewel asked the City Attorney when the guns-in-the-park ordinance would return, and the City Attorney anticipated entering it before year-end for the late January or early February cycle. The City Manager reported on the status of Officer Kelly Stewart, and the Council unanimously approved a closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for Evans v. City of Durham, McFadden v. City of Durham, and Harrington v. City of Durham.

agenda_items.title: 2013 Long Session Legislative Agenda — Pretrial Release / Bail Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated a proposed amendment to statewide pretrial release statutes in the 2013 legislative agenda aimed at gun violence and repeat offenders. Council Member Steve Schewel opposed the draft legislation, citing judges' need for discretion and concern over how the General Assembly might alter the bill, whereas Mayor Bill Bell defended the narrowly tailored proposal supported by the Violent Crime Reduction Roundtable; the item was moved to the General Business Agenda for the regular meeting without a work-session vote.

agenda_items.title: Item 18: Durham Police Department Master Facilities Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the Police Department Master Facilities Study, noting that existing leases cost $811,000 annually (projected to reach $958,000 by FY2018) alongside $4.2 million in cumulative maintenance at the 1959 headquarters building and a $5.1 million site appraisal. Consultants recommended two main north and south service centers financed by lease savings, alongside downtown headquarters options near Main or Fayetteville streets funded via installment financing without a referendum, with public input to precede the budget and CIP process.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk announced appointment tallies including five votes for Rod Ali to the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority and five votes each for Willie Kennedy and Dennis Garrett to the Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission. Council then unanimously set the regular meeting agenda comprising Consent Items 1 through 17 and General Business Public Hearings 19 through 23.

disagreements.issue: 2013 Long Session Legislative Agenda — Pretrial Release / Bail Restrictions for Firearm Offenders
disagreements.summary: Mayor Bill Bell and Council Member Steve Schewel differed over whether Durham should seek a state legislative amendment restricting pretrial release for repeat gun offenders.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support requesting a narrow statewide amendment to pretrial release laws targeting repeat firearm offenders.
side_a_arguments: Addresses a perceived revolving-door problem at the jail raised by residents and the Violent Crime Reduction Roundtable.
Narrowly targets individuals already on pretrial release or convicted within five years of an offense involving illegal firearm use, possession, or discharge.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose submitting the draft bail/pretrial release legislation to the General Assembly.
side_b_arguments: Local judges already make sound bail decisions and judicial discretion should be preserved.
Even a narrowly tailored Durham bill could be expanded by state legislators with a different agenda once introduced in the General Assembly.
disagreements.resolution: Discussed at work session without a vote; item moved off consent to the General Business Agenda for consideration at the regular meeting.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 17, 2012 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven seated 2012 members present, the Council held a moment of silence for the victims of the Newtown, Connecticut school tragedy and presented a proclamation honoring La Conexión for winning national recognition from the National Association of Hispanic Publications. Every formal vote passed unanimously 7-0, including the consent agenda covering roadway median solicitation restrictions, the 2012 Analysis of Impediments to Fair Housing updates, a $50,000 Open Streets grant, non-consensual towing fee revisions, and Old North Durham Park infrastructure improvements. Public Works Director Marvin Williams delivered the 2012 Year-End Paving Status Report detailing 588.42 lane miles repaved since 2006 using over $30 million in voter-approved bonds and a dedicated resurfacing fund. Following public hearings, the Council voted 7-0 on each of three Building Improvement Grant completion extensions for Velocity LLC (106 W. Parrish St.), Hutchins Properties LLC (408 W. Geer St.), and Reinvestment Partners (1201 N. Roxboro St.), and heard a briefing from the City Attorney that a 58-page Fourth Circuit opinion had dismissed the vast majority of claims against the city and its officials in the Duke lacrosse lawsuits.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence for Newtown, CT, Roll Call, and La Conexión Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order, led a moment of silence for the families and victims of Newtown, Connecticut, and confirmed via roll call that all seven members—Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Howard Clement III, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard—were present. The Mayor then presented a proclamation honoring La Conexión on its 18th year and its Excellence Gold Award from the National Association of Hispanic Publications.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-5, 8-11)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the consent agenda in a single vote, encompassing minutes, RDU Airport Authority and Human Relations Commission appointments, roadway solicitation and median restrictions, Analysis of Impediments to Fair Housing updates, a $50,000 Open Streets grant, a lease/contract with Youth Education for Savings and Success Inc., non-consensual towing fee schedules under Chapter 50, and Old North Durham Park infrastructure improvements.

agenda_items.title: Item 12: 2012 Year-End Paving Status Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works Director Marvin Williams reported that since 2006 the city had repaved 588.42 lane miles (266.83 centerline miles) funded by three bond issuances totaling over $30 million and established a dedicated annual street resurfacing fund to prevent future backlogs. Council members praised the staff and noted Main Street's repaving and new bike lane.

agenda_items.title: Item 15: Building Improvement Grant Contract Amendment — Velocity LLC (106 W. Parrish St.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic and Workforce Development staff presented an amendment extending Velocity LLC's $75,000 building improvement grant completion deadline from December 19, 2012 to February 18, 2013 after demolition uncovered structural damage from a 1914 fire. With no public speakers, Council closed the public hearing and approved the extension.

agenda_items.title: Item 16: Building Improvement Grant Contract Amendment — Hutchins Properties LLC (408 W. Geer St.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff recommended extending Hutchins Properties LLC's $70,000 building improvement grant completion deadline from December 19, 2012 to June 30, 2013 due to unforeseen storm drainage issues and a redesign for a new anticipated tenant. After holding the public hearing with no speakers, Council unanimously approved the amendment.

agenda_items.title: Item 17: Building Improvement Grant Contract Amendment — Reinvestment Partners (1201 N. Roxboro St.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an amendment extending Reinvestment Partners' $75,000 building improvement grant deadline from December 31, 2012 to March 31, 2013 due to unforeseen foundation remediation needs. Following a public hearing with no public comment, Council approved the extension unanimously.

agenda_items.title: City Attorney Duke Lacrosse Ruling Update and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Attorney reported that the Fourth Circuit issued a 58-page opinion dismissing the vast majority of claims against the city and individual officials/police officers in the Duke lacrosse litigation, leaving one remaining claim for closed-session briefing on Thursday. Mayor Bell also reminded Council of a special Thursday noon meeting to review Ward 3 vacancy applications before adjourning at 7:27 p.m.

votes.notes: Passed 7-0 after public hearing with no speakers.
votes.discussion_detail: Public hearing and approval of completion date extension to February 18, 2013 for $75,000 grant at 106 West Parrish Street.

votes.notes: Passed 7-0 after public hearing with no speakers.
votes.discussion_detail: Public hearing and approval of completion date extension to June 30, 2013 for $70,000 grant at 408 West Geer Street.

votes.notes: Passed 7-0 after public hearing with no speakers.
votes.discussion_detail: Public hearing and approval of completion date extension to March 31, 2013 for $75,000 grant at 1201 North Roxboro Street.
