meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 6, 2012 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell—with Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Steve Schewel present at roll call, Mike Woodard arriving later, and Howard Clement III granted an excused absence—the Council unanimously suspended the rules to approve Item 7, awarding the Durham Fire Station No. 9 construction contract to Orlando Construction alongside an NCDOT street and driveway access permit. Council reviewed the proposed roadway and median solicitation ordinance, which eliminates the $20 registration permit fee in favor of location-based safety enforcement barring solicitation from traffic medians. Following discussion of the supplemental Southside revitalization item (Item 18), Council unanimously suspended the rules and then passed a 5-1 split vote authorizing staff to negotiate with Durham Community Land Trustees (DCLT) before returning a formal business deal to Council; because it was an unrecorded voice/show-of-hands vote following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, the exact identity of the single Nay voter among the six participating members (Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard; Howard Clement III excused absent) was not named in the digest. Council also heard a Kimley-Horn update on the North Carolina Railroad Traffic Separation Study covering 18 at-grade crossings and unanimously adopted the interview and selection schedule to fill the upcoming Ward 3 vacancy.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excused Absence for Howard Clement III, and City Manager Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:04 p.m.; roll call confirmed five members present initially while Mike Woodard was noted as arriving late, and Council unanimously excused Howard Clement III. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items: referring Item 6 (Housing for New Hope rapid rehousing contract) back to staff, requesting rule suspension for Item 7 (Fire Station No. 9), and noting Item 10 (towing presentation) and Item 18 (DCLT Southside selection).

agenda_items.title: Item 7: Durham Fire Station No. 9 Construction Contract and NCDOT Access Permit
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the City Manager's priority request, Council unanimously voted to suspend the rules to take immediate action on Item 7. Council then unanimously approved the Durham Fire Station No. 9 construction contract with Orlando Construction and execution of the NCDOT street and driveway access permit agreement.

agenda_items.title: Item 4: Roadway Solicitation and Median Restriction Ordinance Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained proposed revisions to the roadway solicitation ordinance covering sales, electioneering, and panhandling, prohibiting activity from medians for traffic safety while eliminating the burdensome $20 annual registration fee. Under the revised ordinance, enforcement would be location-based, requiring safety vests and compliance with litter and traffic safety laws.

agenda_items.title: Item 18: Selection of Durham Community Land Trustees for Southside Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a middle section omitted from the transcript digest, staff clarified that Item 18 only authorized staff to begin negotiations with Durham Community Land Trustees (DCLT) for the Southside revitalization project and that any final financing and business deal would return to Council for approval. Council unanimously suspended the rules to vote on the item, then approved the authorization 5-1 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Item 14: NCRR Traffic Separation Study (TSS) Update

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 3, 2012 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell—with Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard present and Howard Clement III absent—the Council opened with proclamations memorializing environmental advocate Hildegard Ryals and recognizing December 15, 2012 as Human Rights and Bill of Rights Day. Every vote recorded in the digest passed unanimously 6-0, starting with motions to open and continue the Meadows at Southpoint comprehensive plan and rezoning hearings (Items 22 and 23) to January 7, 2013 to avoid re-advertising expenses and to acknowledge a valid protest petition on Item 23. Council approved the consent agenda (excluding pulled Items 6 and 14), heard Chief Jose Lopez's 2012 Third Quarter Crime Summary Report highlighting a 43% rise in total calls for service since FY2006-07, and approved a public hearing item establishing a legally defensible 500-foot separation distance. Council also adopted the long-awaited Passenger Vehicle for Hire Ordinance amendments (Item 14) 6-0 to extend operator permits, driver permits, and inspections to shuttles, limousines, and paratransit vehicles while hearing taxi drivers urge stronger late-night enforcement, and passed pulled Item 12 6-0 after public comment on Alston Avenue sidewalk repairs.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Proclamations (Hildegard Ryals; Human Rights and Bill of Rights Day)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. and confirmed six members present (Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard; Howard Clement III absent). Council Member Steve Schewel presented a memorial resolution honoring Hildegard Ryals (accepted by Judy Allen of the Eno River Association), and Mayor Bell proclaimed December 15, 2012 as Human Rights and Bill of Rights Day (accepted by Joan Walsh).

agenda_items.title: Priority Items: Meadows at Southpoint Continuance and Valid Protest Petition (Items 22 and 23)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the petitioner's request, Council Member Mike Woodard moved to open the public hearings on the Meadows at Southpoint comprehensive plan amendment (Item 22) and zoning map change (Item 23) and continue them two cycles to January 7, 2013 to avoid re-advertising costs, which passed 6-0. The City Clerk also certified a valid protest petition on Item 23, which Council accepted 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Items 6 and 14)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the consent agenda in a single 6-0 vote covering board appointments, the October 2012 bid report, FY2013-14 budget schedule, 2013 meeting schedule, radio system upgrades, West Knox Street culvert stabilization, Munis software licensing, Ellerbe Creek sewer crossing contract with Crowder Construction, and the OWASA/Cary-Durham water supply model MOU, while pulling Item 6 (DCLT Southside) and Item 14 (Passenger Vehicle for Hire).

agenda_items.title: Item 19: 2012 Third Quarter Crime Summary Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Jose Lopez presented the third quarter crime summary covering six performance measures, noting that total calls for service rose 43% between FY2006-07 and FY2011-12. He reported the department met its 5.8-minute average Priority 1 response time target and set a FY2012-13 goal to answer at least 57% of Priority 1 calls in under five minutes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Item: Separation Distance Requirement (500-Foot Standard)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle portion omitted from the transcript digest, Council confirmed that a 500-foot separation requirement—roughly one to one-and-a-half typical Durham city blocks—was legally defensible. After closing public comment, Council approved the item 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 14 (Pulled): Amendments to Passenger Vehicle for Hire Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Mark Ahrendsen outlined ordinance revisions extending operator permits ($100 one-time), driver permits ($15 initial, $10 renewal), and inspections equally to shuttles, limousines, sedans, paratransit, and specialty vehicles while retaining color and age rules for taxis and shuttles. Taxi speakers supported parity but Jonathan White and Keith Williams urged stronger 10 p.m. to 2 a.m. enforcement against unpermitted out-of-town operators; Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved adoption, passing 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 12 (Pulled): Sidewalk and Bicycle Corridor Comment (Victoria Peterson) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After closing the earlier agenda gap, speaker Victoria Peterson addressed pulled Item 12, urging the city to repair sidewalks and improve bicycle safety along Alston Avenue. Following the City Manager's acknowledgment, Council approved the item 6-0 and adjourned at 9:28 p.m.

votes.item_title: Open and Defer Items 22 and 23 (Meadows at Southpoint) Two Cycles to January 7, 2013
votes.notes: Moved by Mike Woodard; Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Opened public hearings on petitioner's deferral request to save re-advertising expenses.

votes.item_title: City Clerk Priority Item: Valid Protest Petition on Item 23 (Meadows at Southpoint)
votes.notes: Passed 6-0; Howard Clement III absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the City Clerk's report certifying a valid protest petition on Item 23.

votes.item_title: Public Hearing Item (500-Foot Separation Requirement)
votes.notes: Passed 6-0; exact agenda item number fell inside the truncated middle segment.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted public hearing item incorporating a 500-foot separation standard.

votes.item_title: Item 14: Amendments to Passenger Vehicle for Hire Ordinance
votes.notes: Moved by Cora Cole-McFadden; passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Applied uniform operator/driver permit and inspection standards to all passenger vehicles for hire (15 or fewer passengers) while preserving vehicle age and color standards for taxis and shuttles.

votes.item_title: Item 12 (Pulled): Bicycle/Pedestrian / Sidewalk Item
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved pulled consent item following public comment from Victoria Peterson regarding Alston Avenue sidewalks.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 19, 2012 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell—with Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard present and Howard Clement III excused absent (6-0) for both November 19 and November 20 due to illness—the Council recognized local Boy Scouts and approved the consent agenda 6-0, except for Item 9 (a six-year lease for the Police Domestic Violence Unit on Fayetteville Street), which passed 5-0-1 with Ayes from Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard and an abstention by Mayor Bill Bell. Following public hearings, Council unanimously (6-0) adopted the Swift Avenue Apartment Homes comprehensive plan amendment (Item 21, A1200006) near the proposed 9th Street light rail station and heard the companion rezoning case (Item 22, Z1200018). The meeting featured the Council's first major split deadlock of the year on Item 26: a motion to defer Item 26 without opening its public hearing failed in a 3-3 tie, with Ayes from Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Eugene Brown and Nays from Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard, as members divided over procedural deferral versus addressing annexation, utility extension, and rezoning planning policy. Before adjourning at 9:28 p.m., Council approved pulled Consent Item 12 (bicycle and pedestrian corridor design studies) 6-0 after hearing public comment on Alston Avenue sidewalk repairs.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excused Absence for Howard Clement III, and Boy Scouts Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:05 p.m. with six members present and Howard Clement III absent due to illness. Council voted 6-0 to excuse Howard Clement III for both the November 19 regular meeting and November 20 work session, and Council Member Mike Woodard recognized visiting Boy Scouts working on their Citizenship in the Community merit badge.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-11, 13-17; Item 9 Abstention by Mayor Bell)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the consent agenda (excluding Item 12, pulled by Victoria Peterson) covering surplus equipment donation to Durham Public Schools, automated refuse truck chassis, property exchange, Leigh Farm Park infrastructure, the Police Domestic Violence Unit lease on Fayetteville Street (Item 9), Board of Adjustment report, Bramble Drive/Covey Court sewer rescission, solid waste cart capital project, Hillandale Road landscape agreement, BPAC report, water main reimbursement, and hydrant meter rates. Mayor Bill Bell abstained on Item 9, which passed 5-0-1 while all other consent items passed 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 21: Comprehensive Plan Amendment — Swift Avenue Apartment Homes (A1200006)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Madison Washburn Court LLC's request to move 3.34 acres at 300 Swift Avenue from the Urban Tier to Compact Neighborhood Tier and from Institutional to Design District within a quarter-mile of a proposed 9th Street light rail station (Planning Commission 12-1). Following testimony by applicant representative George Stanziale and closing of the public hearing, Council approved the amendment 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 22: Zoning Map Change — Swift Avenue Apartment Homes (Z1200018)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the companion rezoning case for four stories of residential units over a below-grade podium parking deck, noting Planning Commission approval (10-1) and right-of-way dedication along Hull Avenue. Council members questioned developer representative George Stanziale on affordable units within the ~200-unit proposal, and Watts Hospital-Hillandale Neighborhood Association zoning chair Tom Miller spoke in support before the middle portion of the transcript was truncated.

agenda_items.title: Item 26: Contested Procedural Deferral Motion (3-3 Tie Vote)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a substitute motion failed, a motion to defer Item 26 without opening its public hearing resulted in a 3-3 tie, with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, and Eugene Brown voting Aye and Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard voting Nay. Council debated annexation, utility extension agreements, and planning near I-40/Fayetteville Road as well as statutory public hearing advertising deadlines before accepting the deadlock and moving to the next item.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speaker Victoria Peterson addressed pulled Consent Item 12, praising campus sidewalks while requesting sidewalk repairs and bicycle accommodations along Alston Avenue. Council approved Item 12 by a 6-0 vote and adjourned at 9:28 p.m.

disagreements.issue: Item 26 Deferral vs. Substantive Action on Rezoning and Utility/Annexation Planning Policy
disagreements.summary: Council deadlocked 3-3 on deferring Item 26 without opening the public hearing, pitting members seeking additional time for staff-applicant negotiations against members pressing established planning and utility-extension standards.
disagreements.side_a_position: Defer Item 26 rather than forcing an immediate deadlock or opening the public hearing only to re-advertise.
side_a_arguments: With Council at loggerheads, additional time between meetings could allow the applicant and staff to reach a workable resolution.
Opening a public hearing without continuing to a compliant advertised date would require re-advertising.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose deferral and maintain consistent planning scrutiny over rezoning, annexation, and utility extension agreements.
side_b_arguments: Flagging utility extension agreements, annexation, and rezoning consistency reflects long-standing responsible Joint City-County Planning Committee policy predating the 751 assemblage.
Concerns remained over peripheral growth along Fayetteville Road south of I-40 from Parkwood to the Orange County line.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to defer failed 3-3; with no consensus to open the public hearing or advance an alternative motion, Council acknowledged the deadlock and moved to the next item.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 8, 2012 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell—with Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard present and Howard Clement III excused absent—Council Member Mike Woodard announced his resignation from Ward 3 effective December 31, 2012 following his election to the North Carolina Senate. Council Member Steve Schewel updated the Council on Lincoln Apartments family relocations coordinated through Blessed Durham, Durham DSS, and Housing for New Hope, and during Citizens Matters the Council brokered an agreement for neighborhood residents and church leadership to enter City Attorney-assisted mediation over amplified music noise complaints. agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excused Absence for Howard Clement III, Lincoln Apartments Update, and Mike Woodard Resignation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:05 p.m., confirmed six members present, and Council unanimously excused Howard Clement III for a medical appointment. Steve Schewel reported that Blessed Durham had helped relocate about 30 Lincoln Apartments families while Housing for New Hope would coordinate ongoing relocation for roughly 18+ remaining families, and Mike Woodard announced his Ward 3 resignation effective December 31, 2012.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Citizens Matters (Violent Crime Roundtable and Church Noise Mediation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed Items 1-29 for the November 19 agenda. During Citizens Matters, residents discussed gunfire complaints alongside the Violent Crime Reduction Roundtable and PAC 2 meetings, and homeowners and church representatives debated amplified bass/music levels from New Hope Church, culminating in both sides agreeing publicly to mediation assisted by the City Attorney.

agenda_items.title: Item 20: Bethpage Special Assessment Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle portion omitted from the transcript digest, Bethpage representatives sought Council consensus to meet with the Local Government Commission alongside city staff regarding a special assessment district covering public street infrastructure. Council members inquired about voluntary school impact fees, ordinance vesting, trails, and bicycle striping on Page and Chin Page roads before giving consensus for staff to attend the LGC meeting.

agenda_items.title: Ward 3 Vacancy Procedures, Acceptance of Mike Woodard Resignation, and Setting Regular Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed the Ward 3 replacement timeline—with Diane Catotti cautioning against an extended six-member gap—and suspended the rules to accept Mike Woodard's resignation effective December 31 and adopt the Council Procedures Subcommittee's Section 2.9 vacancy-filling updates (each 6-0). Council also suspended the rules to approve citizen-matters rule updates (6-0) and set the November 19 regular meeting agenda (6-0).

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Council Member Howard Clement III
votes.notes: Voice vote unanimous among the six members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Excused Howard Clement III due to a doctor's appointment.

votes.item_title: Procedural Agenda Order and City Attorney Procedures Subcommittee Request
votes.notes: Voice votes passed unanimously at 00:12:47 and 00:13:19.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved proceeding through agenda review and scheduling the Council Procedures Subcommittee draft at the end of the session.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Accept Resignation of Council Member Mike Woodard
votes.notes: Voice vote unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended rules to vote immediately on accepting Mike Woodard's resignation.

votes.item_title: Accept Resignation of Council Member Mike Woodard (Effective December 31, 2012)
votes.notes: Voice vote unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Formally accepted Ward 3 Council Member Mike Woodard's resignation effective December 31, 2012.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Consider Council Procedures Subcommittee Recommendations (Section 2.9 Filling Vacancies)
votes.notes: Voice vote unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended rules for immediate action on the Ward 3 replacement timeline and Section 2.9 procedure updates.

votes.item_title: Adopt Council Procedures Subcommittee Timeline and Section 2.9 Filling Vacancies Amendments
votes.notes: Voice vote unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the proposed Ward 3 replacement timeline and changes to Section 2.9 of Council procedures.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules and Adopt Citizens Matters Procedural Flexibility Amendments
votes.notes: Both suspension and main motion passed unanimously 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended rules and adopted updated procedural flexibility rules regarding citizen requests.

votes.item_title: Set November 19 Regular Meeting Agenda (Consent 1-17, Public Hearings 21-26)
votes.notes: Voice vote unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the November 19, 2012 regular meeting agenda.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 5, 2012 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell—with Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard present and Howard Clement III granted an excused absence (6-0)—every item passed unanimously 6-0. The Council presented a proclamation honoring the Volunteer Center of Durham and approved the consent agenda covering the JFK Towers multifamily housing resolution, street sweepers, fire pumper trucks, refuse trucks, and North Durham water reclamation improvements. Council adopted amendments to the street vending and special events ordinance (Item 17) removing the requirement for right-of-way vendors to relocate 60 feet every 15 minutes while adding driveway and restaurant setbacks, and confirmed water and sewer assessment rolls (Item 24) while continuing contested parcels to December 17. Following public hearings, Council unanimously approved the Palladian Multifamily rezoning (Item 25, Z1200010) over tenant opposition after securing commitments for Leigh Farm Road bike-lane evaluation and a $30,000 Durham Public Schools contribution, along with UDO text amendments for downtown signs and murals (TC1200003), West Point at 751 roofing materials (Z1200011), Future Land Use Map evaluation procedures (TC1200004), and downtown outdoor recreation (TC1100014).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excused Absence for Howard Clement III, and Volunteer Center Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m. with six members present and voted 6-0 to excuse Howard Clement III. Mayor Bell presented a proclamation recognizing the Volunteer Center of Durham and highlighted youth volunteer service totaling nearly 40,000 hours alongside city neighborhood revitalization efforts.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-16, 19-20)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved the consent agenda covering board appointments, the September 2012 bid report, FY2012-13 budget and grant ordinance amendments, a resolution approving the JFK Towers multifamily housing facility, purchases of Tymco street sweepers, Sutphen fire pumpers, and automated refuse truck bodies, a Budo Karate dojo lease, a sanitary sewer evaluation contract with Bionomic Services, and a North Durham pretreatment contract amendment with Dellinger Inc.

agenda_items.title: Item 17: City Code Amendment — Street Vending and Special Events Permits
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning supervisor Grace Smith presented code amendments for right-of-way vendors selling First Amendment or food items, repealing the unenforceable rule to move 60 feet every 15 minutes while requiring 20-foot separation from driveways and 50-foot separation from restaurant entrances and outdoor dining. Following public comment by Becky Cassio, Council adopted the ordinance 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 24: Confirmation of Assessment Rolls (Loftin Dr., Angier Ave./Cortez Dr., East Cornwallis Rd.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works Director Marvin Williams presented assessment rolls for water and sewer mains on Loftin Drive, Angier Avenue, Cortez Drive, and East Cornwallis Road. Council voted 6-0 to confirm the uncontested assessments while continuing hearings on objected parcels (Cokely/Tyndale heirs, Painter heirs, and Jerome Ramsey) to December 17, 2012.

agenda_items.title: Item 25: Zoning Map Change — Palladian Multifamily (Z1200010)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Z1200010 on 29.558 acres along Leigh Farm Road to remove a prohibition on multifamily development within the Office Institutional development plan. Despite opposition from Palladian II corporate tenant Wes Enik, Council approved the rezoning 6-0 after the applicant proffered committed elements to evaluate/stripe a Leigh Farm Road bike lane and pay $30,000 to Durham Public Schools prior to site plan approval, prompting discussion on whether developer payments reach charter schools.

agenda_items.title: Item 26: UDO Text Amendment — Downtown Signs and General Sign Standards (TC1200003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Michael Stock presented TC1200003 adding sign flexibility in design districts, expanding historic markers, and creating public art placard and mural sign categories (Planning Commission 11-0). With no public speakers, Council adopted the text amendment 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 27: Zoning Map Change — West Point at 751 Revisions (Z1200011)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Z1200011 modifying Z08-31 design commitments to allow asphalt shingles as a roofing material (Planning Commission 13-0), with applicant representative George Stanziale responding to Diane Catotti's inquiry. Council approved the revision 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 28: UDO Text Amendment — Evaluation and Assessment Report / FLUM Procedural Changes (TC1200004)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented TC1200004 updating UDO sections 2.1, 2.2, 3.2, and 3.4 regarding agricultural easements on the Future Land Use Map and annual Evaluation and Assessment Report components (Planning Commission 12-1; County Commissioners 5-0). Council approved the amendment 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 32: UDO Text Amendment — Outdoor Recreation and Activity in Downtown Design Districts (TC1100014)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Michael Stock presented DDI Inc.'s text amendment expanding outdoor recreation and activity standards in the core and support-1 downtown design districts with screening, size, and amplified music limits (Planning Commission 13-0). Council approved the amendment 6-0 and adjourned at 8:00 p.m. after Mayor Bell urged residents to vote the next day.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Council Member Howard Clement III
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved excused absence request for Howard Clement III.

votes.item_title: Item 17: City Code Amendment — Street Vending and Special Events Permits
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Updated right-of-way vending rules, removing the 60-foot/15-minute movement rule and adding 20-foot driveway and 50-foot restaurant separation requirements.

votes.item_title: Item 24: Confirmation of Assessment Rolls (Continuing Objected Parcels to December 17, 2012)
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Confirmed Loftin Dr., Angier Ave./Cortez Dr., and East Cornwallis Rd. rolls except for contested parcels continued to December 17.

votes.item_title: Item 25: Zoning Map Change — Palladian Multifamily (Z1200010)
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved revised OI(D) plan permitting multifamily housing with two added committed elements (Leigh Farm Road bike lane study/striping and $30,000 DPS payment).

votes.item_title: Item 26: UDO Text Amendment — Downtown Signs and General Sign Standards (TC1200003)
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted UDO sign regulation revisions for design districts, historic markers, public art placards, and murals.

votes.item_title: Item 27: Zoning Map Change — West Point at 751 Revisions (Z1200011)
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Modified Z08-31 design commitments to permit asphalt shingles as a roofing option.

votes.item_title: Item 28: UDO Text Amendment — Evaluation and Assessment Report / FLUM Procedural Changes (TC1200004)
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted UDO procedural updates for agricultural easements on the Future Land Use Map and annual Evaluation and Assessment Reports.

votes.item_title: Item 32: UDO Text Amendment — Outdoor Recreation and Activity in Downtown Design Districts (TC1100014)
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved DDI Inc. text amendment expanding outdoor recreation and activity standards in downtown core and support-1 areas.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 18, 2012 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven seated 2012 members present, Council Member Steve Schewel opened by recognizing city heavy-equipment operator Eric Taylor, a Second Chance Program graduate repairing potholes on Carolina Avenue while studying engineering at NC State. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority agenda adjustments—including presentations on Chartwell Properties' 9th Street infrastructure deal points, street vending, and citywide permitting, referring Item 18 (bicycle/pedestrian studies) back to staff, and adding UDO outdoor recreation Item 32. During Citizens Matters, Amy McMahon raised safety and 911 response concerns along the American Tobacco Trail near mile marker 1.25, and staff later presented on ABC/beer-wine permit coordination, street vending impacts on private commercial ingress/egress and unimproved right-of-way, and an Office of Economic and Workforce Development profile of Durham's unemployed highlighting youth literacy gaps (2nd- to 4th-grade reading levels) and job linkage at Duke Cancer Center's expansion. The Council concluded by unanimously (7-0) setting the November 5 regular meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Employee Recognition, and Priority Agenda Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:05 p.m. with all seven seated members present. Council Member Steve Schewel commended Public Works employee Eric Taylor, a Second Chance Program graduate now operating heavy equipment, and Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items covering Items 15, 17, 18 (referred back), 22 (1:45 p.m. time certain), and 32.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Citizens Matters (American Tobacco Trail Safety), and ABC Permitting Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed Consent and Public Hearing items for November 5, noting JFK Towers (Item 8) was not a Durham Housing Authority project. During Citizens Matters, Amy McMahon criticized limited police visibility and 911 response on the American Tobacco Trail near mile marker 1.25, another resident spoke on Rolling Hills housing and light rail, and staff outlined coordination between police, PACs, fire/zoning, and the Durham County ABC Board on alcohol permitting.

agenda_items.title: Item 17: Street Vending and Special Events Permits Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a middle section omitted from the transcript digest, a business representative and Council discussed concerns that loosened right-of-way vending rules could encourage pushcarts and roadside vendors near commercial driveways and unimproved rights-of-way (citing Guess Road/North Pointe Drive and Ninth Street). Staff clarified that the citywide code would prohibit selling on unimproved right-of-way.

agenda_items.title: Item 23: Profile of the Unemployed in Durham (Office of Economic and Workforce Development)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD presented workforce data on ~768 registered participants (averaging 480 annually) alongside roughly 11,000 unemployment insurance claimants, noting efforts to place residents in the 2,400 jobs associated with Duke Cancer Center's expansion via the Northgate JobLink center. Staff highlighted that 99% of youth served are dropouts—some reading at 2nd- to 4th-grade levels—while workers aged 50-59 represent a major impacted demographic.

agenda_items.title: Set November 5 Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the November 5 regular meeting agenda comprising Consent Items 1-16 and 19-20, General Business Item 17 (street vending), and Public Hearings 24-28 and 32 before adjourning.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Items (Items 15, 17, 18 Referred Back, 22 Time Certain, Supplemental Item 32)
votes.notes: Voice vote unanimous with all seven members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved priority schedule changes including referring Item 18 back to staff and adding Item 32 as a supplemental public hearing.

votes.item_title: Set November 5 Regular Meeting Agenda (Consent 1-16 & 19-20, GBA 17, Public Hearings 24-28 & 32)
votes.notes: Voice vote unanimous with all seven members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the agenda for the November 5, 2012 regular City Council meeting.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 15, 2012 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell—with Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Howard Clement III, and Steve Schewel present and Mike Woodard excused absent—all recorded votes passed unanimously 6-0. The Council recognized Master Police Officer Dwayne Burroughs for his counterterrorism work with the Raleigh-Durham Joint Terrorism Task Force investigating the Triangle Terror Group, earning national awards from the FBI, IACP, and the U.S. Attorney General. Members also discussed the Lincoln Apartments relocation crisis, with Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden urging workforce development and job-training support for affected tenants, and approved procedural priority items shifting planning/inspections fee amendments (Item 8) to a public hearing and adopting an ordinance (rather than a resolution) modifying Chapter 70 for annexation and utility extension coordination (Item 19). Following public hearings, Council voted 6-0 to approve an old school building historic landmark designation and approved the Duraleigh Investments comprehensive plan amendment (Item 17, A1100013) and rezoning (Item 19, Z1100028) for 25.19 acres at NC 55 and Riddle Road, while Mayor Bell directed staff to examine whether voluntary developer school contributions to Durham Public Schools are subsequently shared with charter schools.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Recognition of Master Police Officer Dwayne Burroughs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. with six members present (Mike Woodard previously excused). Council honored Master Police Officer Dwayne Burroughs and the Durham Police Department for a four-year Joint Terrorism Task Force investigation into the Daniel Patrick Boyd Triangle Terror Group, recognized with the FBI Director's Award, IACP Award, and U.S. Attorney General's Award.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements: American Tobacco Trail Run and Lincoln Apartments Relocation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Steve Schewel recapped a six-mile American Tobacco Trail run with 30 participants, after which Mayor Bell and Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden addressed the Lincoln Apartments situation, affirming active city staff engagement and calling for workforce development and job training alongside housing assistance. Council then unanimously approved priority motions moving Item 8 (planning/inspections fee amendments) to public hearing and converting Item 19's Chapter 70 annexation/utility coordination action from a resolution to an ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Historic Landmark Designation (Old School Building / Self-Help Affiliate)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle segment omitted from the digest, Council clarified that the applicant was a Self-Help affiliate rather than generic Self-Help and heard public comment from Victoria Peterson regarding ex-offenders (prompting a reminder of speaker-relevance bylaws). Council approved the landmark designation 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 17: Comprehensive Plan Amendment — Duraleigh Investments (A1100013)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented A1100013 at the southeast corner of NC 55 and Riddle Road in the suburban tier, redesignating ~23 acres from Industrial to Medium Density Residential (6-12 units/acre) and 0.71 acres to Commercial (Planning Commission 11-0). After confirming no Chamber objections and hearing from applicant representative Don D'Ambrosio, Council approved the amendment 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 19: Zoning Map Change — Duraleigh Investments (Z1100028) and Charter School Funding Inquiry
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented companion rezoning Z1100028 for 25.19 acres from IL(D) to RS-M(D) with 60% max impervious surface and 10 feet of Riddle Road bike-lane right-of-way (Planning Commission 11-0). Don D'Ambrosio explained the remaining partner could not make Steve Schewel's suggested $30,000 school donation; Council approved the rezoning 6-0, and Mayor Bell asked staff to investigate whether developer school proffers to DPS flow to charter schools.

votes.notes: Passed 6-0 (Mike Woodard excused absent).
votes.discussion_detail: Moved Item 8 to the public hearing portion of the agenda pursuant to N.C.G.S. 160A-364.

votes.item_title: City Attorney Priority Item: Amend Item 19 Motion (Chapter 70 Annexation/Utility Coordination) from Resolution to Ordinance
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Corrected the motion text for Chapter 70 modifications from adopting a resolution to adopting an ordinance.

votes.item_title: Public Hearing: Historic Landmark Designation (Old School Building)
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved historic landmark designation following clarification of the Self-Help affiliate applicant.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Comprehensive Plan Amendment — Duraleigh Investments (A1100013)
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Redesignated ~23 acres from Industrial to Medium Density Residential and 0.71 acres to Commercial at NC 55 and Riddle Road.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Zoning Map Change — Duraleigh Investments (Z1100028)
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Rezoned 25.19 acres at NC 55 and Riddle Road from IL(D) to RS-M(D) with impervious surface limits and Riddle Road right-of-way dedication.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, the Durham City Council reviewed consent and public hearing items, heard citizen comments, and debated an outdoor dining code amendment. During Citizens Matters, representatives of People of Faith Against the Death Penalty and local clergy urged Council to adopt a resolution calling on North Carolina to repeal the death penalty, building on Durham's 1999 moratorium resolution. Council spent substantial time debating Supplemental Item 22 on outdoor dining permits, examining whether bars and nightclubs should be included alongside restaurants, ADA six-foot sidewalk clearance requirements, and police noise and permit revocation enforcement, before deciding to carry the item over with direction for staff revisions. Council also suspended the rules and unanimously approved by voice vote the Ellerbe Creek Bank Stabilization Project Phase 1 construction contract (Item 12), approved Mike Woodard's excused absence for the October 15 meeting, set the upcoming regular meeting agenda, and entered closed session for economic development discussions.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items, Citizen Matter Addition, and Excused Absence Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden added Mr. Tarantino to Citizens Matters for three minutes. City Manager Thomas Bonfield requested staff updates after Citizens Matters on the American Tobacco Trail and Lincoln Apartments, rule suspension to vote on Item 12 (Ellerbe Creek Bank Stabilization Phase 1), and pulling Items 19 and 22 for presentation. Councilmember Mike Woodard requested and received an excused absence for the October 15 Council meeting to attend National League of Cities business.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and Item 12 (Ellerbe Creek Bank Stabilization Project Phase 1)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent items including August 2012 bid reports, Community Development contractor lists and mortgage servicing contract extensions, Cultural Master Plan grant amendments, Planning and Inspections fee amendments, Police reimbursement grants, a water/sewer reimbursement agreement with Pulte Home Corp. (Item 10), and Water Management projects. Council voted to suspend the rules on Item 12 (Ellerbe Creek Bank Stabilization Phase 1 construction contract), briefly held it for a question, and formally approved the contract by unanimous voice vote at the end of the meeting.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Housing Comments and Death Penalty Repeal Resolution Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ralph McKinney addressed neighborhood housing rehabilitation and urged solutions without racial division. Speakers representing People of Faith Against the Death Penalty (PFADP) and local faith leaders asked Council to adopt a resolution calling on North Carolina to repeal the death penalty, citing Durham's 1999 moratorium resolution and recent unanimous repeal resolutions in Chapel Hill and Carrboro.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item 22: City Code Amendment for Outdoor Dining Permits
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council and staff debated a proposed outdoor dining ordinance limited to restaurants on city-maintained sidewalks with at least six feet of unobstructed ADA pedestrian clearance. Staff and Police Chief Lopez had raised concerns regarding bars and nightclubs, while council discussion centered on defining bars/nightclubs/private clubs under ABC rules, strengthening noise and permit revocation enforcement under Section 54-141, and supporting downtown vibrancy. disagreements.side_a_position: Limit initial ordinance to restaurants to mitigate noise, late-night rowdy behavior, and enforcement concerns.
side_a_arguments: Police Chief Lopez and City Manager Bonfield expressed concern over late-night noise and public safety issues outside bars and nightclubs.

disagreements.side_b_position: Include bars and nightclubs in the outdoor dining ordinance while strengthening permit revocation and enforcement tools.

Approved items included minutes, Historic Preservation Commission appointment, July 2012 bid report, the first amendment to the Durham Athletic Park assignment agreement with the Durham Bulls, a Community Development grant with Bull City Urban Market LLC, City Hall Annex exterior envelope renovations, ACS software service agreement, Southeast Pressure Zone tank design contract, and a Water Reclamation Facility Master Plan amendment with Hazen and Sawyer.

agenda_items.title: Five-Year Update to Multi-Jurisdictional Hazard Mitigation Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mark Shell of Durham County Emergency Management presented the five-year update to the Hazard Mitigation Plan for Council adoption. Steve Schewel asked about catastrophic risks including the Shearon Harris nuclear facility; no public speakers testified at the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Economic Development Incentive Agreement with Hawthorne Durham LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff proposed a $1 million incentive payable over seven years for a redevelopment project inside the Urban Growth Area projected to create roughly 690 total jobs (307 permanent and 320 construction) and incorporate Durham Workforce Plan JobLink hiring. Five public speakers testified (including supporters citing job creation and Victoria Peterson). After the public hearing closed and the item was moved and seconded, an unidentified councilmember stated opposition to the incentive and to amending economic development policy outside community development target areas; the final vote is not captured in the truncated transcript digest.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Outcome not recorded in truncated transcript digest

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Alexander Park Development (Z110022)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Applicant representative Patrick Byker sought rezoning for up to 285 townhomes on roughly 50 acres south of Alexander Drive near RTP (Planning Commission recommended 13-0; protest petition ruled invalid). Neighbors questioned a discrepancy over a 12-inch water main extension on Page Road/Smallwood Drive and potential wetlands. In response to Mike Woodard's question regarding an estimated 31-student DPS impact, the applicant proffered a one-time $15,000 donation to Durham Public Schools prior to first certificate of occupancy, and Woodard moved approval with that added commitment.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Old Chapel Hill Road Residential (Z1200008)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the Old Chapel Hill Road residential rezoning (recommended 12-1 by the Planning Commission in July 2012), and applicant representative Mr. Eaton briefly addressed Council with no opposition. Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden noted for the record that Ms. Wallace had worked on her daughter's home and stated it had no effect on her vote.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: Renaissance at Four Seasons (Z110031)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Pat Young) presented Z110031 to incorporate the clubhouse into the commercial design zone, and speaker Horvath briefly explained the amendment with no public opposition.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened and chaired the work session (with Mayor Bill Bell joining later), which featured employee training recognitions, major project reviews, and an update on American Tobacco Trail safety. Council recognized 16 Public Works, Water Management, and Transportation employees completing heavy equipment operator training and heard Citizens Matters addressing public safety, balanced budgets, and local copper theft. Staff presented the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority annual report, explained a one-year stopgap amendment with the Durham Bulls for Durham Athletic Park operations (Item 6), and detailed Hawthorne Durham LLC's revised 330-unit mixed-use redevelopment proposal with 15% affordable housing (Item 21). Police Chief Jose Lopez briefed Council on a recent youth incident on the American Tobacco Trail and ongoing enforcement, while Council voted unanimously by voice vote to accept priority items, set the regular meeting agenda, and enter closed session on Sevier Construction Company v. City of Durham.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items and Heavy Equipment Operator Training Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the City Manager's priority items (revisions to Item 8 City Hall Annex renovations, RDU report, and DPAC report) and the City Attorney's closed session request on Sevier Construction Company v. City of Durham. Manager Bonfield, Marvin Williams, and Tom Ayres then recognized 16 employees from Public Works, Water Management, and Transportation who completed Heavy Equipment Operator Classes 9 and 10.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Public Safety, Budgets, and Copper Theft
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizens addressed public safety, local and federal balanced budgets, and a recent copper theft causing $10,000-$15,000 in property damage for roughly $100 worth of copper.

agenda_items.title: Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority (RDU) Annual Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: RDU representatives reported airline market-share changes (with Delta now the largest carrier, followed by Southwest, US Airways at 17%, United, and JetBlue at 5%), answered questions on tracking MWBE vendor participation and dollar totals, and discussed how video conferencing and remote interviewing affect business air travel.

agenda_items.title: Durham Athletic Park First Amendment with Durham Bulls Baseball Club
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD staff Joy Guy-Michael and Kevin Dick described the proposed one-year stopgap amendment with the Durham Bulls Baseball Club to evaluate long-term Durham Athletic Park operating costs and marketability. Council members asked about pricing authority and whether trained volunteers could manage the protective field tarp.

agenda_items.title: Hawthorne Durham LLC Economic Development Incentive Proposal Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained that Hawthorne Durham LLC scaled its proposal back from 365 to 330 residential units (plus over 100,000 square feet of retail) to avoid a nine-month rezoning and NCDOT traffic study that could jeopardize retail pre-commitments. The proposal maintained a 15% affordable housing commitment, and Council questioned whether additional subsidies could further reduce rents.

agenda_items.title: American Tobacco Trail Safety Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Jose Lopez briefed Council on a Tuesday incident involving a runner and youths ages 12 to 16 on the American Tobacco Trail, noting he met personally with victims and emphasizing arrest and prosecution alongside social-service interventions. A council member suggested officers cycling the trail engage youth groups informally, and Mike Woodard noted he would miss the September 4 public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council set the consent agenda (Items 1-17) and General Business public hearings (Items 20-30) and voted unanimously to enter closed session on Sevier Construction Company v. City of Durham.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: With six council members present and Diane Catotti excused 6-0, Mayor Bill Bell presided over a meeting focused on crime statistics, fair housing impediments, and Democratic National Convention security funding. Police Chief Jose Lopez presented the 2012 First and Second Quarter Crime Summary Report, reporting full sworn staffing and an improved Priority 1 average response time of 5 minutes 35 seconds, while Eugene Brown urged action against homicides in African-American neighborhoods and Mike Woodard promoted BPAC's upcoming American Tobacco Trail safety forum. Council voted 6-0 to approve the consent agenda (excluding pulled Item 6) and 6-0 to approve water/sewer mini-assessment rolls (Item 11). On Item 13 (the Draft 2012 Analysis of Impediments to Fair Housing Choice), following public testimony emphasizing transit-oriented zoning and affordable housing dispersion, Howard Clement III initially questioned voting on a draft before staff incorporated public comments, but Council voted 6-0 to approve submission to HUD taking those comments into account. Council also voted 6-0 to adopt the pulled $333,000 Democratic National Convention grant project ordinance (Item 6) after Victoria Peterson questioned officer deployment.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Diane Catotti and Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 6-0 to excuse Diane Catotti's absence. Mayor Bell presented a Life Insurance Awareness Month proclamation to Dell Mattioli, and Howard Clement III and colleagues recognized Anne Gray.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-3, 5, 7, 9; Item 6 Pulled)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the consent agenda 6-0 excluding Item 6 (which was pulled for public discussion). Approved items included minutes, street acceptances, an FAA taxiway and airfield lighting grant at RDU, an EPA diesel reduction grant, a 2012-2013 warrant control interlocal agreement, and the Raleigh Road/US 70 Phase 2 construction contract.

agenda_items.title: 2012 First and Second Quarter Crime Summary Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Jose Lopez reviewed six performance measures, highlighting full sworn staffing (33 BLET #34 graduates and 20 new recruits), a 5 minute 35 second average Priority 1 response time (beating the 6-minute target), and 57.27% of Priority 1 calls answered under 5 minutes. Mike Woodard invited residents to BPAC's special meeting on American Tobacco Trail safety and Citizen Observer Patrols, while Eugene Brown voiced urgent concern over ongoing homicides in Durham's African-American community.

agenda_items.title: Mini-Assessment Rolls (Brightwood Lane, Rogers Road, and Green Lane Drive)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering Services staff reported that properties on Brightwood Lane, Rogers Road, and Green Lane Drive had not yet benefited from water and sewer main construction, with frontage charges due upon future connection. No members of the public spoke.

agenda_items.title: Draft 2012 Analysis of Impediments to Fair Housing Choice
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In the public hearing, speakers urged using UDO zoning and transit-corridor planning to expand affordable housing rather than re-creating segregated neighborhoods, while Jackie Wagstaff criticized concentrated subsidized and privatized housing. Howard Clement III questioned approving a draft prior to hearing staff's follow-up on public testimony, but staff and Mike Woodard clarified the document was the analysis (not yet the implementation plan) and public comments would be incorporated into the HUD submission.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 6: 2012 Democratic National Convention Grant Project Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speaker Victoria Peterson questioned discrepancies between $413,000 and $333,000 figures and opposed sending 89 Durham police officers to Charlotte for the DNC. Mayor Bell and staff noted that federal security grant dollars funded mutual-aid convention protection across cities including Raleigh and Greensboro.

votes.discussion_detail: Excused Diane Catotti from the August 20 regular meeting.

votes.notes: Electronic vote among 6 members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved consent items 1-3, 5, 7, and 9 after pulling Item 6.

votes.notes: Electronic vote among 6 members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Found listed properties had not benefited from main construction at this time, with frontage charges due upon future connection.

votes.notes: Electronic vote among 6 members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved submission of the 2012 Analysis of Impediments to HUD incorporating public hearing comments.

votes.item_title: Approve Item 6: 2012 Democratic National Convention Grant Project Ordinance
votes.notes: Electronic vote among 6 members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved federal grant project ordinance for DNC mutual-aid police deployment.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presided over the City Council work session featuring neighborhood safety concerns, agenda referrals, and an extended deliberation on accepting a federal SAFER firefighter hiring grant. Pastors and congregants from Mount Vernon Baptist Church and a neighboring Spanish-speaking church urged Council to restrict a nearby retail tobacco shop selling drug paraphernalia, scales, and synthetic urine next to their church and children, prompting City Attorney and Planning staff to evaluate regulatory options. On Supplemental Item 21 (the 2011 SAFER Hiring Program grant for 15 firefighters), Fire Department staff outlined three-year grant coverage and future Station 17 staffing, while Mayor Bell questioned long-term budget affordability—estimated at $755,000 annually by FY 2016—and expected attrition before City Manager Bonfield confirmed inclusion in the multi-year financial plan. Council unanimously waived the rules by voice vote to approve the SAFER grant ordinance, referred Item 4 (Durham Bulls DAP amendment) and Items 14-16 (NCCU UC-2 zoning items) back to administration, set the regular meeting agenda, and entered closed session for litigation consultation including Sevier Construction Company v. City of Durham.

agenda_items.title: City Manager and City Attorney Priority Items and Agenda Referrals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bonfield referred Item 4 (Durham Athletic Park amendment) and Items 14-16 (NCCU UC-2 zoning and plan amendments, due to advertising glitches) back to administration, noted a supplemental memo on Item 8 (University Drive culvert replacement), and added Citizen Matter Item 20 (Carl Kenney), Supplemental Item 21 (SAFER grant), and a Water Management video preview. City Attorney added two closed sessions under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3), including Sevier Construction Company v. City of Durham.

agenda_items.title: Mount Vernon Baptist Church Complaint on Adjacent Tobacco Shop and Carl Kenney Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Leaders from Mount Vernon Baptist Church and an adjacent Spanish-language congregation asked Council for an ordinance to stop a nearby tobacco shop from selling synthetic urine, home drug tests, drug paraphernalia, and scales, and exposing children to secondhand smoke. City Attorney Baker and Planning staff explained the parcel is zoned for retail and agreed to examine regulatory possibilities. Later, Carl Kenney addressed family structure, public policy, and economic struggles facing young Black men.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item 21: 2011 SAFER Hiring Program Grant Project Ordinance (15 Firefighters)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Fire Department staff presented deployment maps showing gaps in 'two-in/two-out' coverage and proposed accepting the three-year federal SAFER grant to hire 15 firefighters who could eventually staff Fire Station 17. Mayor Bell probed whether the department would have sought 15 positions without the grant, questioned projected attrition, and asked how the City would absorb roughly $755,000 per year by FY 2016; another member urged active recruitment of women and minorities. City Manager Bonfield confirmed the long-term cost would be integrated into the multi-year financial plan, and Council waived the rules to approve the grant.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council set the consent agenda (Items 1-3, 5-7, and 9), General Business Item 10 (Crime Report), and General Business public hearings (Items 11 and 13), noting Item 21 had been acted upon under waived rules. Council then voted unanimously to enter closed session.

votes.notes: Voice vote following rule waiver; Mayor Bell questioned long-term FY16 budget impacts before voting in favor.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven seated council members present, Mayor Bill Bell presided over a meeting highlighted by national performance management honors and unanimous 7-0 approval of the 21c Durham LLC downtown hotel and museum incentive package. Council recognized Durham's ICMA Certificate of Distinction Award (one of 15 jurisdictions nationwide and the only recipient in North Carolina), proclaimed the 29th Annual National Night Out, and referred Item 30 (the Hazard Mitigation Plan update) back to the City Manager 7-0. Council approved 7-0 a broad consent agenda covering board appointments, classification and compensation plan recommendations, Bull City Connector agreements with Duke University, rollout cart contracts, and infrastructure completion for the failed Stonybrook development. After hearing strong support from 11 public speakers, Council voted 7-0 (moved by Cora Cole-McFadden) to approve the 21c Durham LLC economic incentive contract ($5.7 million nominal / $2.8 million present value over 20 years, requiring a policy exception below the $45 million threshold), and voted 7-0 to adopt the Snow Hill/Little School B initial zoning map change (Z1200006A).

agenda_items.title: Coca-Cola Contest, ICMA Performance Distinction Award, and National Night Out Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell recognized Durham Coca-Cola Bottling Co. CEO Hagar for a Sprite community contest award, congratulated staff (Bertha Johnson, Jay Reinstein, Jermaine Brewington, Kerry Goode, Wanda Page, and Thomas Bonfield) on Durham receiving the ICMA Center for Performance Measurement Certificate of Distinction, and proclaimed August 7, 2012 as the 29th Annual National Night Out.

agenda_items.title: Priority Referral: Hazard Mitigation Plan Update (Item 30)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bonfield requested that Item 30 (Hazard Mitigation Plan Update public hearing) be referred back to the City Manager's office.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved the consent agenda 7-0, including board and commission appointments, Workforce Development Board term limit modifications, next-generation 911 hosted communications, 2012-2015 temporary staffing and consultant contracts, compensation and classification plan recommendations, Stonybrook failed development infrastructure completion, Otto Container rollout carts, Duke University Bull City Connector transit agreement, and parking gate access equipment.

agenda_items.title: General Business Public Hearing Item 31
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council closed the public hearing on Item 31 without opposition and approved the item 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Economic Incentive Contract with 21c Durham LLC (Hill Building)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD Director Kevin Dick presented the proposed 20-year economic incentive contract ($5.7 million total / $2.8 million present value) funded from project-generated sales, occupancy, and property taxes for 21c's boutique hotel and contemporary art museum in the Hill Building, requiring a policy exception for falling below the $45 million investment threshold. Eleven public speakers—including Downtown Durham Inc., arts leaders, and Chuck Watts—strongly backed the project, alongside supportive remarks from Mayor Bell, Mike Woodard, Steve Schewel, and Cora Cole-McFadden, who moved approval.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented initial city zoning for a 115.39-acre site north of Snow Hill Road and south of Little River Reservoir (annexed effective June 30, 2012), translating county Rural Residential, Little River A, and Falls-Jordan B districts to equivalent city designations. meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its July 19, 2012 Work Session to preview consent and public-hearing items, process urgent board appointments, and review economic development incentives for the proposed downtown 21c hotel. Council unanimously suspended the rules and approved Item 29, the interlocal agreement for Phase 7 of the Triangle Area Water Supply Monitoring Project, as well as Workforce Development Board appointments (Items 3 and 8). On Homeless Services Advisory Committee appointments, Mike Woodard initially moved to bundle two appointments, prompting an unnamed councilmember to voice support for Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden's opposition and Vote No; Mayor Bill Bell had Woodard split the motion, after which the nonprofit-slot reappointment of Chris Toole passed unanimously by voice vote while the corporate-sector/Duke-slot appointment passed by voice vote with at least one dissenting Nay (individual voter names were not recorded in the work-session voice vote). Council also questioned staff on the $3.7 million 20-year net fiscal impact, 6% discount rate, and city-county revenue sharing for the 21c Durham LLC downtown hotel incentive prior to entering closed session on economic development.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Items 20 and 29)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield requested referring Item 20 (asset forfeiture and controlled substance funds) back to administration and suspending the rules to vote today on Item 29 (interlocal agreement for the Triangle Area Water Supply Monitoring Project). Council unanimously approved the priority items by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Homeless Services Advisory Committee Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Mike Woodard moved to suspend the rules and appoint nominees to the nonprofit and corporate-sector/Duke slots on the Homeless Services Advisory Committee. When an unnamed councilmember objected to bundling both nominees and voiced support for Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden's opposition, Mayor Bill Bell asked Woodard to split the motion into separate votes; the nonprofit reappointment of Chris Toole passed unanimously by voice vote, while the corporate-sector appointment passed by voice vote over at least one No vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Rules suspended unanimously; Nonprofit slot Passed (Voice, Unanimous); Corporate slot Passed (Voice, with Nay vote(s))

agenda_items.title: Consent and Public Hearing Agenda Review (Items 6-33)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell read through departmental, consent, and public-hearing items including board appointments, Workforce Development grant ordinances, Next Generation 911 communications, Compensation and Classification Plan recommendations, watershed monitoring, Auto-Container Management LLC, and a parking gate access contract (Item 28, where a councilmember noted a form contract was attached instead of the final contract). Public hearing items previewed included the Hazard Mitigation Plan, 300 East Main Street LLC building improvement grant amendment, 21c Durham LLC economic incentive, and Snow Hill Middle School zoning (Z1100006A).

agenda_items.title: Interlocal Agreement for Triangle Area Water Supply Monitoring Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the manager's priority request, Council moved to suspend the rules to take immediate action on Item 29, the Triangle Area Water Supply Monitoring Project interlocal agreement. After suspending the rules, Council approved the agreement unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Information Portion (Citizen Speakers)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council heard public comment from five registered speakers: Ralph McKinney, Vivian McCoy, James Chavis Sr., John Tarantino, and Donald Bender. Topics included 911 police backup dispatch protocols and community concerns.

agenda_items.title: Transit Amenities / Boarding Locations Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff responded to councilmember questions on bid re-evaluation and confirmed that transit stop improvements under the Auto-Container Management LLC contract would be determined with Triangle Transit (TTA) at major boarding locations such as Duke Hospital, Durham Regional, NCCU, Durham Tech, South Square, and the Village.

agenda_items.title: Economic Incentive Contract with 21c Durham LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained corrections to the 21c Durham LLC incentive analysis showing a $3.7 million positive net financial impact over 20 years using a 6% discount rate and semi-annual payments, as well as a performance carryover balance applying to sales tax rather than property tax. Councilmembers discussed downtown Convention Center hotel demand, Greenfire's other properties and leverage, and Durham County receiving greater incremental tax revenue while the City funds the bulk of the incentive.

agenda_items.title: Workforce Development Board Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because the Workforce Development Board was scheduled to meet the following week, Council suspended the rules and voted immediately on Items 3 and 8 (including the Mayor's reappointment nominee). Both the rule suspension and the appointments passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Regular Meeting Agenda Setting and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the consent and general-business public hearing agenda for the upcoming regular meeting and discussed Friday agenda packet timing and saving large PDFs such as the gang report in iBooks. Council then voted to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) regarding business location and expansion.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: During its June 7, 2012 Work Session, the Durham City Council reviewed a 50-item agenda spanning the FY 2012-13 budget pull items (shuttle and dedicated housing fund matrix), four Southside East and West revitalization agreements, Better Bus Service final plans, and upcoming zoning cases. Council approved the City Manager's priority schedule requests and set the regular meeting consent and public hearing agenda unanimously by voice vote. Two substantive policy reviews dominated the later portion of the session: (1) community development staff detailed a proposed loan restructuring and stricter compliance monitoring plan for Rebuild Durham's affordable rental portfolio, and (2) councilmembers challenged Water Management staff over Contract SR-54 utility easement mowing (Item 39), questioning why staff recommended paying $200,000 more to the second-lowest bidder after lowest bidder TruGreen's references were deemed unverified.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items and Budget Pull Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield outlined priority items including suspending rules on Item 16 (Historic Preservation Fund grant), a 1:30 PM presentation on Item 37 (Designing Better Bus Service), deferred Item 39 (SR-54 utility easement mowing), a closed session on economic development, and prioritizing budget pull items (shuttle and housing fund matrix) and four Southside items. Council approved the manager's priorities and related procedural items unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Full Work Session Agenda Read-Through
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell read through 50 items covering board appointments, Durham One Call and cell phone audits, FY 2012-13 Budget & CIP, gang reduction interlocal agreement, Southside East/West contracts with Community Self-Help and McCormick Baron Salazar, Workforce Investment Act and Downtown Durham Inc. contracts, City-County property tax collection, Gillig bus and shelter contracts, water meter upgrades, voluntary annexations, Leesville Road and Del Webb zoning cases, and citizen matters (Michael Owens and Ralph McKinney).

agenda_items.title: Rebuild Durham Affordable Housing Portfolio Restructuring and Monitoring
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed past noncompliance in the Rebuild Durham portfolio and outlined a proposal with the City Attorney's Office to defer city loans until property sale, restructure first mortgages (leaving the city in second position on most properties and first on one), and enforce stricter compliance monitoring. A Rebuild Durham representative presented portfolio alternatives including second-mortgage reserve adjustments, CDFI refinancing, and rent subsidies for very low-income tenants; staff agreed to return with a formal restructuring item.

agenda_items.title: Contract SR-54 Utility Easement Maintenance (Mowing and Hand Cutting)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management staff reiterated its recommendation to award the 200-mile easement mowing contract to the second-lowest bidder because lowest bidder TruGreen's references could not be verified as comparable utility-easement bush-hogging work. TruGreen representatives Dominique and Justin Martin cited large-scale easement work at Fort Hood, Gwinnett County, and Quantico, prompting councilmembers to instruct senior staff to personally contact the references and justify the $200,000 price premium before final Council action.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Deferred pending senior staff reference verification

agenda_items.title: Set Regular Meeting Agenda (Consent and Public Hearings)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the upcoming regular meeting agenda with consent items 2-4, 6-15, and 17-42, General Business Agenda Item 5 (Human Relations Commission), and GBA public hearings 43-48, then adjourned.

votes.notes: Voice vote in work session; individual names not recorded.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved City Manager Tom Bonfield's priority items and sequencing for budget pull items and Southside agreements.

votes.notes: Voice vote; passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Procedural motion following city attorney/clerk priority check.

votes.notes: Voice vote; passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Set the agenda for the June 18 regular City Council meeting.

disagreements.issue: Contract SR-54 Utility Easement Mowing Bid Award ($200,000 Price Differential)
disagreements.summary: Water Management staff recommended bypassing lowest bidder TruGreen for the second-lowest bidder due to unverified easement-mowing references, while councilmembers questioned paying $200,000 more without senior staff personally verifying TruGreen's additional references.
disagreements.side_a_position: Award Contract SR-54 to the second-lowest bidder because TruGreen's submitted references have not been verified as comparable utility-easement maintenance.
side_a_arguments: The 200-mile contract crosses thousands of residential backyards requiring specialized bush-hogging and hand-cutting.
Initial reference checks showed no easement maintenance, and staff had not yet reached follow-up contacts by phone.
disagreements.side_b_position: Require senior staff (Mr. Greeley or department leadership) to personally verify TruGreen's references and provide definitive justification before spending $200,000 extra.
side_b_arguments: TruGreen representatives cited comparable right-of-way and utility easement mowing at Fort Hood, Gwinnett County, and Quantico Marine Base.
Council expects a definitive justification if the city is asked to pay $200,000 more for the second-lowest bidder.
disagreements.resolution: Staff agreed to personally follow up on the references and report back with a definitive recommendation before the Council votes at the regular meeting.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: All seven seated members of the Durham City Council—including Council Member Howard Clement III returning from medical absence—met on June 4, 2012, passing every recorded action unanimously (7-0). Council recognized the Toyama, Japan Sister Cities youth choir delegation, approved the Consent Agenda (including cemetery rates, HHW facility design, NCIMED streetscape sidewalk contract ST-259, closed landfill maintenance, and water/sewer connection fee updates), and confirmed Harvard Avenue special assessment rolls after a public hearing. Council also held the public hearing on the proposed FY 2012-13 Budget and FY 2013-18 CIP (featuring a 1-cent tax rate increase for housing and a 7-cent tax rate increase for the Downtown Business Improvement District), approved the Live Well North Durham zoning map change (Item 29) 7-0 despite a valid protest petition requiring a six-vote supermajority, approved Southside West architecture/engineering Contract Amendment 2 (Item 33), and awarded the FY 2012-13 employee medical and dental benefits contract to Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Carolina (Item 34).

agenda_items.title: Toyama Sister Cities Youth Delegation Proclamation and Council Member Clement Welcome
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Mike Woodard introduced the sixth Durham youth delegation and choir traveling to Toyama, Japan, and Mayor Bill Bell presented a proclamation to delegation representative Olivia Marks. Council Member Howard Clement III thanked residents and Alpha Phi Alpha fraternity brothers upon his return to Council.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items (Item 34 Benefits Amendment, Item 26 Housing Code Corrections, Item 29 Protest Petition)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager noted an amended recommendation for Item 34 (medical/dental benefits), the Assistant City Attorney noted corrections to Item 26 (housing code), and the City Clerk reported a valid protest petition filed against Item 29 (Live Well North Durham zoning map change). Council approved each priority report 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Minutes, Reappointments, Infrastructure & Utility Fees)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered consent items including board reappointments, FY 2012-13 cemetery rates, easement sales to MRK Properties LLC, HHW drop-off facility design, AMEC atmospheric deposition monitoring, NCIMED streetscape sidewalk contract ST-259, closed landfill maintenance, and water/sewer engineering connection fee changes. Council Member Howard Clement III inquired about the Zhuzhou, China sister city formalization before Council passed the Consent Agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater Manager Ed Venable presented the continued confirmation of Harvard Avenue assessment rolls for curb, gutter, paving, and water/sewer laterals, noting property owners have until June 19 to submit extended payment plan applications.
