meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Proposed Fiscal Year 2012-2013 Budget
meetings.executive_summary: On Day 2 of its FY 2012-13 Budget Workshops (May 31, 2012), the Durham City Council reviewed departmental budget presentations without taking formal votes. Director Kevin Dick presented the Office of Economic and Workforce Development budget, highlighting 17 FTEs, $400,000 in on-the-job training grants, a SAMHSA youth outreach partnership, major downtown projects (21c and Chesterfield), and the $1.9 million Downtown Revitalization and Parrish Street resource allocation. Later in the session, Council heard budget updates from the Fire Department (recognizing its Golden Globe budget presentation award and bilingual/diversity firefighter agility testing), Emergency Communications (911 CAD and EMD reaccreditation), Emergency Management (realigning 3 FTEs with EMS and FEMA approval of the Hazard Mitigation Plan), and Fleet Maintenance (exploring county fleet management). Council concluded by scheduling June 7 budget flag-item reviews (shuttle and dedicated housing) and requesting audited financial statements for a prospective private vendor prior to voting.

agenda_items.title: Office of Economic and Workforce Development (OEWD) Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Director Kevin Dick presented OEWD's Workforce and Economic Development divisions, noting 17 FTEs, a SAMHSA/Durham Center youth employment coordinator position, an ~80% program completion rate, and $400,000 in on-the-job training grants. He also reviewed major confidential and public development deals (21c and Chesterfield) and a $1.9 million Downtown Revitalization and Parrish Street fund consisting of $1.25 million in existing obligations and $622,000 in operating, lease, and Business Improvement District event costs.

agenda_items.title: Fire Department and Emergency Communications (911) Budget Presentations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Fire leadership discussed holding pre-qualification agility tests in January and April to expand and diversify firefighter recruitment, and Chief Bruce Pagan and Deputy Chief Curia were recognized with the Budget Office's Golden Globe award for best budget presentation. Emergency Communications highlighted rising CAD maintenance costs and its third Emergency Medical Dispatch reaccreditation.

agenda_items.title: Durham City-County Emergency Management Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emergency Management reported a reduction from 42 to 39 FTEs by defunding three positions in realignment with EMS, a 1.9% resource allocation increase driven by fuel and county pay-for-performance costs, and city cost-sharing for emergency management coordinators and administrative staff. Staff also noted FEMA and NCEM approval of the City-County Hazard Mitigation Plan on March 5.

agenda_items.title: Fleet Maintenance Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Fleet Maintenance presented slight operating and personnel increases for technician training and tools, county radio-support revenues, and openness to managing Durham County's vehicle fleet. Staff highlighted recognition as the 37th green fleet in North America via diesel retrofits and hybrid/electric vehicles and welcomed new director Joe Clark starting June 4.

agenda_items.title: June 7 Budget Wrap-Up Schedule and Vendor Financial Due Diligence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council and City Manager Tom Bonfield arranged the June 7 schedule to begin at 10:00 AM with budget flag items (shuttle and dedicated housing) followed immediately by the 53-item work session (including Southside East/West and Better Bus Service). A councilmember requested that the City Manager obtain audited financial statements from a private vendor for review prior to any vote before the session adjourned.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Proposed Fiscal Year 2012-2013 Budget
meetings.executive_summary: On Day 1 of its FY 2012-13 Budget Workshops (May 30, 2012), the Durham City Council adjusted its daily schedule around an 11:00 AM memorial service and reviewed revenue projections, affordable housing funding, and Neighborhood Improvement Services operations without taking formal votes. Budget Director Bertha Johnson reported lower-than-projected real property tax growth (1.87% certified vs. 2.87% projected), a $134.8 million estimated property tax levy (allocating 1 cent to dedicated housing and 3.23 cents to transit), and a 5.3% sales tax growth projection complicated by nonprofit refunds and multi-month state reporting lags. In the afternoon, Council examined the $56 million Dedicated Housing Fund plan—including tax-credit rental partnerships with the Durham Housing Authority, 45 inventory properties in Northeast and Southwest Central Durham, and the Southside West architectural design amendment—and reviewed Neighborhood Improvement Services' $3.4 million budget, IMPACT team blight remediation, and Golden Belt office lease.

agenda_items.title: Budget Workshop Opening and Schedule Adjustments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell convened the special budget session at 9:00 AM and turned proceedings over to City Manager Tom Bonfield. Council adjusted the schedule to suspend at 11:00 AM for a memorial service, work through lunch upon returning at 12:30 PM, and fix the Dedicated Housing Fund discussion for 1:30–2:00 PM.

agenda_items.title: FY 2012-13 Revenue Update (Property Tax, Sales Tax, and Penny Allocation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson reported certified real property tax growth of 1.87% (below the 2.87% retreat estimate) and a drop in public utility property valuation, producing an estimated $134.8 million levy with 1 cent ($2.375 million) dedicated to housing and 3.23 cents to transit. She noted FY 2012-13 sales tax growth is projected at 5.3% (+$1.8 million general fund) despite large local nonprofit refunds and state reporting delays through January, while hotel occupancy tax (+3.4%) and business licenses (+2.4%) showed modest growth.

agenda_items.title: Community Development and $56 Million Dedicated Housing Fund Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Councilmembers and staff discussed leveraging low-income rental tax credits with nonprofits and the Durham Housing Authority, land swaps, and prioritizing infrastructure-ready areas. Members questioned how many second-mortgage homebuyer loans are covered within the $56 million plan (45 inventory houses across NECD and SWCD) and reviewed the Southside West architectural/engineering contract amendment ahead of the June 4 Council meeting.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Improvement Services (NIS) Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: NIS presented its $3.4 million General Fund budget (41 FTEs plus 4 grant-funded FTEs), projecting 5,000 designated-area housing inspections, 800 illegal dump cleanups and 400–450 compliance remediations by the 8-FTE IMPACT team, and $200,000 annual rent for its Golden Belt community space. Councilmembers also raised concerns about long-term vacant HOA homes deteriorating and updates on the Neighborhood Vitality Index and employee diversity training.

meetings.title: FY'12-'13 Proposed Budget segment from ep. 139 of City Hall This Week
meetings.executive_summary: This segment from Episode 139 of City Hall This Week summarizes City Manager Tom Bonfield's proposed $372 million FY 2012-13 budget, which was presented to the Durham City Council on May 21, 2012. Highlights include a $176.6 million general fund, a property tax increase costing $15 annually on a $150,000 home dedicated to affordable housing, water/sewer and stormwater rate adjustments, $400,000 for neighborhood commercial revitalization, and a seven-cent tax rate for the Downtown Durham Business Improvement District. No formal motions or Council votes occur during this informational news segment, which notes a June 4 public hearing and June 18 final approval date.

agenda_items.title: Proposed $372 Million FY 2012-13 Budget and General Fund Public Safety Allocation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The segment introduces City Manager Tom Bonfield's proposed $372 million FY 2012-13 spending plan presented to the City Council on May 21, representing a $10 million overall increase from the prior year alongside a smaller $176.6 million general fund for core services. More than $80 million—or 45% of the general fund—is allocated to public safety across the police, fire, emergency communications, and emergency management departments.

agenda_items.title: Dedicated Property Tax Increase for Affordable Housing Initiatives
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The proposal includes a property tax increase that raises annual property taxes for the owner of a $150,000 home by $15.00 to establish a dedicated funding source for affordable housing initiatives. Remarks in the segment emphasize that dependable, affordable, quality housing stock is essential to thriving, livable neighborhoods across Durham.

agenda_items.title: Water, Sewer, and Stormwater Rate Adjustments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The proposed budget recommends average rate increases of about $1.26 per month for water and sewer charges and $5.40 per year for stormwater rates. Water and sewer revenues support operational and maintenance needs, while stormwater fee increases fund major capital projects required under the Falls Lake and Jordan Lake rules.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Commercial Revitalization, Downtown BID, and Adoption Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The proposed budget allocates an additional $400,000 for neighborhood commercial revitalization in targeted areas, building on $386,000 committed the prior year to two East Durham projects projected to leverage over $12 million in private investment and create 200 temporary and 38 full-time jobs. It also launches the Downtown Durham Business Improvement District with a seven-cent tax rate per $100 of assessed value for enhanced downtown services, with a public hearing scheduled for June 4 and final Council approval set for June 18.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 24, 2012 City Council Work Session, Council excused Diane Catotti (with Howard Clement III also absent) and approved City Manager priority items unanimously by voice vote before reviewing a 32-item agenda. Council Member Mike Woodard recognized Sister Cities of Durham for establishing a new sister city relationship with Zhuzhou, China, and citizen speakers presented a draft resolution opposing corporate personhood in campaign finance. Finance Director David Boyd delivered the Third Quarter Financial Report (noting balanced general fund projections despite fuel pressures and $93,000 lower DPAC ticket facility fee projections), and Assistant NIS Director Rick Hester presented overhauled Minimum Housing Code standards and a Chapter 26 porch-furniture prohibition. Council concluded by announcing 5-vote board and commission balloting results, passing a suspended-rule resolution, setting the June 4 regular agenda, and entering closed session on economic development.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Absence Excusal, and City Manager Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:04 PM, and Council unanimously excused Council Member Diane Catotti by voice vote (Howard Clement III was also absent). City Manager Tom Bonfield presented priority items scheduling the Workforce Development Board annual report (Item 21) and a presentation on Minimum Housing Code and trash/undergrowth ordinances (Item 26), which Council accepted unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Read-Through and Sister Cities (Zhuzhou, China) Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read through consent, presentation, and public hearing items (including water/sewer connection fees, pulled at Item 20; FY 2012-13 Budget & CIP public hearing; stormwater performance standards; and Live Well North Durham zoning). Council Member Mike Woodard recognized Sister Cities of Durham for establishing a new sister city in Zhuzhou, China, and discussed an upcoming Chinese delegation visit and potential Chinese garden at Duke Gardens.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters (Corporate Personhood Resolution, Public Comments)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Harry White and supporters presented a draft resolution opposing corporate personhood and Citizens United campaign spending (citing 145+ U.S. municipalities and several North Carolina local governments), which a councilmember asked to defer until Council could read the text. Ralph McKinney and John Tarantino also addressed the Council.

agenda_items.title: Third Quarter Financial Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director David Boyd reported that the General Fund is tracking close to budget (operating savings offsetting personnel overages), water and sewer are performing well, and transit and solid waste face fuel cost pressures. He noted DPAC ticket facility fees are projected $93,000 below budget (potentially offset by higher operating profit share) and cited regional forecasts projecting strong growth in the Triangle and Asheville.

agenda_items.title: Modifications to Minimum Housing Code and Chapter 26 Trash/Undergrowth Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant NIS Director Rick Hester and staff walked Council through a reorganization of the Minimum Housing Code (overhauling Sec. 10-234 Standards of Fitness and updating Housing Appeals Board and civil penalty provisions) and a Chapter 26 amendment barring interior upholstered furniture on porches and yards exposed to the elements (excluding refuse set out for collection).

agenda_items.title: Suspended-Rule Resolution, Board Balloting, Agenda Setting, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council suspended the rules and adopted a resolution unanimously by voice vote, then announced 5-vote ballot appointments across the Environmental Affairs Board, Open Space & Trails Commission, Planning Commission, Board of Adjustment, Cultural Advisory Board, and Human Relations Commission. Council set the June 4 regular meeting agenda (consent 1-18, 20-22; GBA public hearings 23-29) and entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4).

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: With six councilmembers present (Howard Clement III absent), the Durham City Council passed all recorded motions 6-0 at its May 21, 2012 Regular Meeting. Council opened with a proclamation for the Walk a Mile with a Child / Let's Move Durham Day event at Solite Park, approved City Manager priority deferrals to June 4 for Southside West architecture Contract Amendment 2 (Item 6) and employee medical/dental plans (Item 11), and adopted the Consent Agenda (including CASA supportive affordable housing funds, Housing Authority multifamily revenue bonds, Price-Steele Place loan commitment, repaving contract amendments, and transit grants). Council heard discussion on Beer and Wine Privilege License compliance (Item 8) and formally received City Manager Tom Bonfield's proposed FY 2012-13 Budget (praised by Mayor Bell and councilmembers for avoiding a general fund tax hike while funding Better Bus Service and a 1-cent housing tax). Finally, Council confirmed Green Lane Drive and Hillsborough Road sewer assessment rolls while continuing the Harrison property objections to August 6, and adopted an 8.5% average residential stormwater fee increase effective July 1, 2012 (6-0).

agenda_items.title: Walk a Mile with a Child / Let's Move Durham Day Proclamation & Public Works Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented a proclamation designating Let's Move Durham Day and the Walk a Mile with a Child event at Solite Park on June 2, 2012 to Linda Bunch Gunn (NCIMED), Dr. Sheila Allison, and Henry Lancaster to combat childhood obesity. Public Works Week and a city hall/operations staff job-swap initiative were also recognized.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Deferrals for Items 6 and 11)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield requested deferring Item 6 (Southside West architectural/engineering Contract Amendment 2) and the medical/dental plan portion of Item 11 (FY 2012-13 Benefits Recommendations) to June 4, 2012 while acting on the remaining benefit components. Council approved the priority items 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Housing Bonds, CASA & Price-Steele Funds, Repaving, Transit Grants)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council adopted the Consent Agenda 6-0, approving minutes, the FY 13 Planning work program, CASA permanent supportive affordable housing funds, Housing Authority multifamily revenue bonds, a conditional loan to Development Ventures Inc. for Price-Steele Place, Westry Street parcel donations, the 2012 Activate Youth Grant, repaving amendments (ST-250 through ST-253 and ST-234), yard waste facility contract amendment, and New Freedom and NCDOT transportation planning grant ordinances.

agenda_items.title: Beer and Wine Privilege License Issuance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director David Boyd introduced the annual business privilege license request for beer and wine retailers. A BP retailer representative outlined employee restricted-product compliance training, and discussion addressed ABC permit enforcement against noncompliant retailers before the middle of the transcript was truncated.

agenda_items.title: Receipt of City Manager's Proposed FY 2012-13 Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield concluded his proposed FY 2012-13 budget presentation (noting new City Facebook and Twitter feeds). Mayor Bell and Councilmembers Catotti, Cole-McFadden, Woodard, and Schewel praised the proposal for holding the general fund tax rate flat, funding the Better Bus System, leveraging debt refinancing, and proposing a modest 1-cent housing tax (~$20/year on a $150,000 home), voting 6-0 to receive the presentation.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Confirmation of Assessment Rolls for Green Lane Drive and Hillsborough Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater Manager Ed Venable recommended confirming the sewer main assessment rolls for Green Lane Drive and Hillsborough Road while excluding the properties of objectors Karen M. Harrison and D. Bryan Harrison and continuing their hearing to August 6, 2012. With no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and approved the recommendation 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2013 Stormwater Rate Increase
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an ordinance revising stormwater rates effective July 1, 2012, increasing residential stormwater fees by an average of 8.5%. With no public speakers, Council closed the public hearing and adopted the rate ordinance 6-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened the May 10, 2012 City Council Work Session while Mayor Bill Bell was en route (Mayor Bell presided by the end of the session, with Howard Clement III absent). Council reviewed a 31-item agenda—including Housing Authority multifamily revenue bonds, Southside West engineering (Item 6, pulled), employee benefits (Item 11, pulled), and the failed Dunwoody subdivision (Item 13, pulled)—and heard citizen complaints over a six-year water billing dispute and neighborhood noise ordinance readings near the American Tobacco Trail. Later, Council discussed public outreach on Falls Lake and Jordan Lake rules, heard a Triangle Regional Film Commission pitch to convert the Duke Diet and Fitness Center gym into a 10,000-square-foot film studio, and took up Supplemental Item 31 (FY 2012-13 CDBG/HOME/ESG Annual Action Plan) following Durham County Commissioners' request to fund Operation Breakthrough. Citing Operation Breakthrough's 33/100 score, a unanimous 13-0 Citizens Advisory Committee rejection, and prior audit findings on CDBG scoring accountability, Council unanimously suspended the rules and approved the original staff/CAC recommendation without Operation Breakthrough, then set the May 21 regular agenda before closed session.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Items 6, 11, 21, 26, and Supplemental Item 31)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield requested rule suspension to vote today on Item 6 (Southside West architectural/engineering amendment) and Supplemental Item 31 (FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan), noted presentations for Items 11 and 21, and reported citizen George Bridges (Item 26) would not appear. Council approved the manager's priority items unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Work Session Agenda Read-Through (Housing Bonds, Pulled Items 6, 11, 13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Councilmembers noted that the Housing Authority assumes no financial risk on Item 5 (multifamily housing revenue bonds) while earning a ~$100,000 fee plus annual monitoring fees with no impact on city debt ratings. Councilmembers pulled Item 6 (Southside West architectural amendment), Item 11 (2012-13 benefits recommendations), and Item 13 (Dunwoody failed subdivision update) for discussion.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters: Water Billing Dispute and Noise Ordinance Measurement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Otto Latenzak contested six years of elevated water bills prior to a meter replacement, while City Manager Tom Bonfield stated the tested meter was accurate and the resident had declined a $450 sewer-side credit offer. Staff also explained calibrated decibel meter testing along the edge of the American Tobacco Trail regarding a church noise complaint (Item 27).

agenda_items.title: Falls Lake / Jordan Lake Outreach and Triangle Regional Film Commission Studio Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Councilmembers discussed summer community outreach on Falls Lake and Jordan Lake rules and urged displaying implementation costs alongside conservation efforts. A Triangle Regional Film Commission representative then pitched converting the Duke Diet and Fitness Center gym into a 10,000 sq ft production studio (and pool into an underwater tank) for local economic development and student training.

agenda_items.title: Approval of FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan (CDBG, HOME, ESG Funds)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reconsidering Item 31 after the Board of County Commissioners requested funding for Operation Breakthrough's weatherization program, Council examined why Operation Breakthrough scored 33/100 and received a unanimous 13-0 denial from the Citizens Advisory Committee. Eugene Brown and other members emphasized HUD oversight and a prior city audit requiring strict adherence to application scores, leading Council to suspend the rules and approve the original staff/CAC Annual Action Plan unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Set May 21 Regular Meeting Agenda and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the May 21 Regular City Council Meeting agenda (Consent items 1-5, 7, 9-10, 12-19; GBA items 6, 8, 11; GBA public hearings 23-24) before moving to closed session.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Items
votes.notes: Voice vote; passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted City Manager Tom Bonfield's priority items for the May 10 work session.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules on Supplemental Item 31 (FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan)
votes.notes: Voice vote; passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended rules to vote immediately on the FY 2012-13 CDBG/HOME/ESG Annual Action Plan ahead of the HUD submission deadline.

votes.item_title: Supplemental Item 31: Approve Original Recommendation for FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan (CDBG, HOME, ESG)
votes.notes: Voice vote; passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the original staff and Citizens Advisory Committee recommendation for the FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan without awarding CDBG funds to Operation Breakthrough.

votes.item_title: Set May 21 Regular Meeting Agenda (Consent 1-5, 7, 9-10, 12-19; GBA 6, 8, 11; Public Hearings 23-24)
votes.notes: Voice vote; passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Set the agenda for the May 21, 2012 Regular City Council Meeting.

disagreements.issue: Operation Breakthrough CDBG Funding Exclusion in FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan
disagreements.summary: Following Durham County's request to fund Operation Breakthrough's senior weatherization program ($75,000), councilmembers debated whether past scoring history justified reconsideration before uniting behind the Citizens Advisory Committee's 13-0 denial and competitive scoring audit rules.
disagreements.side_a_position: Uphold the original Annual Action Plan recommendation denying CDBG funding based on the 33/100 application score and unanimous CAC vote.
side_a_arguments: The 13-member Citizens Advisory Committee voted unanimously against funding Operation Breakthrough.
Awarding $75,000 to an application scoring 33/100 over higher-scoring rejected applicants would undermine HUD compliance and repeat deficiencies flagged in a prior city CDBG performance audit.
disagreements.side_b_position: Clarify how Operation Breakthrough applied and scored in prior years (e.g., non-construction vs. construction grant) before finalizing rejection.
side_b_arguments: Operation Breakthrough's director stated they applied as a non-construction grant and could not provide construction-grant documentation.
Reviewing past-year applications and scores could clarify the discrepancy without immediately committing $75,000.
disagreements.resolution: Council suspended the rules and voted unanimously by voice vote to approve the original staff/CAC Annual Action Plan without adding Operation Breakthrough.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: With six members present (Howard Clement III absent due to health), the Durham City Council passed all votes 6-0 at its May 7, 2012 Regular Meeting. Council opened with proclamations for Drinking Water Month (including statewide-winning student water conservation posters), Crime Stoppers, Durham Lions Club Day, Older Americans Month, and the Durham Police Memorial Service. Council pulled Item 7 (FY 2012-13 CDBG/HOME/ESG Annual Action Plan) from the Consent Agenda, adopted the remaining Consent Agenda 6-0 (including FY 2012-13 water and sewer rates, Downtown Durham MSD contract, Little River watershed acquisition, PAL and HIDTA police grants, Harvard Avenue hardship criteria, and the 2012 legislative agenda), and confirmed Almond Drive and Pickwick/Pickbran Circle sewer assessments (continuing contested objections to August 6) 6-0. On pulled Item 7, Interim Community Development Director Reginald Johnson relayed the Board of County Commissioners' unanimous request to reconsider CDBG funding for Operation Breakthrough's weatherization program; after questioning the reviewer score and missing cost estimates, Council voted 6-0 to carry Item 7 over to the May 10 work session for complete scoring comparisons.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations: Drinking Water Month & Poster Awards, Crime Stoppers, Lions Club, Older Americans Month, Police Memorial
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented a Drinking Water Month proclamation to Water Lab Supervisor Jimmy Gamel, and Assistant Director Vicki Westbrook presented 'Wasting Water is Weird' poster awards (388 entries across 13 schools, including multiple state-level winners). Council also recognized Crime Stoppers, Durham Lions Club Day (May 23), Older Americans Month, and the Police Memorial Service (noting Howard Clement III's absence due to health).

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Pull Item 7; Legislative Meeting Notice)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield asked Council to pull Item 7 (FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan) for additional staff comments and reminded members of the special legislative meeting Friday morning at 8:30 AM. Council approved the priority request 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Water & Sewer Rates, Public Safety Grants, Watershed Acquisition, Legislative Agenda)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Excluding pulled Item 7 and Public Hearing Item 22, Council approved the Consent Agenda 6-0. Key actions included adopting FY 2012-13 water and sewer rates, Downtown Durham MSD services contract, Little River reservoir buffer acquisition (John T. Cox property), 2012 Police Athletic League and HIDTA grants, Harvard Avenue assessment hardship criteria, petition sidewalk assessment rates, and the 2012 Short Session Legislative Agenda.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Confirmation of Assessment Rolls for Almond Drive and Pickbran Circle
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater Manager Ed Venable recommended confirming sewer main and outfall assessment rolls for Almond Drive and Pickbran Circle while continuing objections by Curly Anderson, Deanna Shiwatka, and the Cornell Jones Revocable Trust to August 6, 2012. With no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and approved the motion 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Approval of FY 2012-13 Annual Action Plan (CDBG, HOME, ESG Funds & Operation Breakthrough Request)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Director Reginald Johnson reported that the Durham Board of County Commissioners approved the $38,395 HOME consortium allocation earlier that day while unanimously asking the City Council to reconsider not awarding $75,000 in CDBG funds to Operation Breakthrough's weatherization program. Councilmembers questioned reviewer comments (citing direct state funding, missing support letters, and lack of experienced cost estimates) and voted 6-0 to carry the item over to the May 10 work session so staff could supply full applicant scoring comparisons before the HUD deadline.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 19, 2012 Durham City Council Work Session, presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, Council unanimously approved accepting the City Manager's and City Attorney's priority items, setting the May regular meeting agenda, and entering closed session on litigation and economic development matters, with no split or contested votes taken. Council received an Environmental Affairs Board briefing and reviewed a draft resolution on hydraulic fracturing, focusing on requiring comprehensive environmental and water-treatment safeguards before state legalization, protecting residents from predatory mineral leases, and preserving local zoning control. Department of Water Management staff presented proposed FY 2012–2013 water and sewer rates reflecting a 2.6% overall rate increase—lower than an earlier 4% estimate—to support an $81.5 million utility budget while continuing tiered conservation pricing and double outside-city rates. Staff also briefed Council on five new NCDOT selective vegetation removal applications for roadside billboards under July 2011 state legislation, and reported that a proposed short-session bill on minimum pretrial bonds for firearms offenses would likely wait for the January long session as a statewide measure.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order at 1:06 p.m. and conducted roll call. The City Manager introduced three priority items—Item 14 (2012 Police Athletic League grant presentation), Item 20 (FY 2012–2013 proposed water and sewer rates presentation), and supplemental Item 25 (2012 short session legislative agenda)—while the City Attorney requested a closed session item regarding litigation against the City of Durham pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a). Council unanimously approved accepting the priority items by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Item 26 (Hydraulic Fracturing) Addition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A Council member requested adding Item 26, a presentation on hydraulic fracturing, to the agenda. The City Clerk then read through upcoming agenda items, including board/commission appointments, the March 2012 bid report, CDBG/HOME/ESG grant ordinances and FY 2012–2013 Annual Action Plan (Items 6–9), Downtown Durham Municipal Service District contract (Item 10), Little River reservoir buffer acquisition (Item 11), Police Athletic League and HIDTA grants (Items 14–15), Harvard Avenue and Green Lane Drive/Hiltberg assessments (Items 16–17), geotechnical RFQ (Item 18), sidewalk assessment rates (Item 19), Almond Drive/Circle assessment public hearing (Item 22), and citizen matters.

agenda_items.title: Hydraulic Fracturing Presentation and Draft Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: An Environmental Affairs Board presenter briefed Council on a condensed report regarding horizontal drilling and hydraulic fracturing, previously shared with the Durham Board of County Commissioners. The presentation outlined risks of predatory mineral leases, urged establishing comprehensive environmental and third-party certified water-treatment regulations before legalizing drilling, and warned that pending state legislation left local zoning authority uncertain, drawing parallels to state preemption of local billboard rules. Council discussed Attachment 26, a draft resolution urging state safeguards and preservation of local control.

agenda_items.title: Proposed FY 2012–2013 Water and Sewer Rates Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated mid-meeting discussion touching on street resurfacing and post-drought water consumption trends, Department of Water Management staff presented proposed FY 2012–2013 water and sewer rates to fund an $81.5 million budget (25% personal services, 39% O&M, pay-as-you-go CIP, debt service, and fleet/radio replacement). The proposal reduced an earlier 4% projection to a 2.6% overall increase generating roughly $1.9 million in additional revenue, raising a typical Tier 1 residential bill by $0.56 per month and an average 535-cubic-foot customer bill by 2.6% while preserving tiered rates and double outside-city rates. Staff also presented Environmental Finance Center comparisons showing Durham's bills remained competitive across North Carolina.

agenda_items.title: Selective Vegetation Removal Request for Billboards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff briefed Council on a July 2011 state law and temporary NCDOT rules effective March 1, 2012 that govern selective vegetation removal permits for billboards and roadside businesses within state rights-of-way. Staff noted five applications had been received on March 1 under the expanded clearing allowances (an extra 100 feet in back and expanded front sightlines) and offered to provide regular updates to Council as applications arrive.

agenda_items.title: 2012 Short Session Legislative Agenda and Board Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported on a meeting with Mayor Bell and a state legislative representative regarding a proposed bill to set minimum pretrial bonds for firearms offenses, noting it would likely require statewide legislation in the January long session rather than a local short-session bill and was expected to be pulled before Monday's meeting. Council also recorded six votes each for appointees to the City-County Appearance Commission and Russell Johnson to the City-County Environmental Affairs Board.

agenda_items.title: Setting the May Regular Meeting Agenda and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council set the upcoming regular meeting agenda with Consent Items 1–20 and Item 25 and General Business Public Hearing Item 22, passing the motion unanimously by voice vote. Council then voted unanimously by voice vote to enter closed session to address the City Attorney's litigation item and an economic development item.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager and City Attorney Priority Items
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote; mover and seconder were not identified by name in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted City Manager priority items (Items 14, 20, and supplemental Item 25) and City Attorney closed-session litigation item.

votes.item_title: Appointments to City-County Appearance Commission and Environmental Affairs Board
votes.notes: Passed with 6 votes; individual voter names were not read aloud in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Clerk announced six votes for the City-County Appearance Commission appointee and six votes for Russell Johnson for the City-County Environmental Affairs Board.

votes.item_title: Set May Regular City Council Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Set Consent Agenda as Items 1–20 and Item 25, and General Business Public Hearing as Item 22.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for the City Attorney's litigation item under G.S. 143-318.11(a) and an economic development item.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 16, 2012 Regular City Council Meeting, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presided in the excused absence of Mayor Bill Bell, with five members present (Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard) and all votes passing unanimously 5-0 with no split or contested votes. Council issued ceremonial proclamations for Earth Day, Durham's Partnership for Children, and Children's Mental Health awareness, and recognized the eighth graduating class of Junior Fire Marshals. Council unanimously approved the consent agenda covering board appointments, refunding limited obligation bonds Series 2012A and 2012B, HUD grant ordinances, annual preservation and appearance reports, a Triangle Expressway scenic byway resolution, and taxicab advertising rules, and confirmed the Brightwood Lane and Rogers Road water main assessment rolls while referring five property owner objections to June 4, 2012. Following a public hearing on the Designing Better Bus Service draft plan where riders and advocates urged serving Central Professional Park, improving bus shelters, and extending the Bull City Connector to Northeast Central Durham, Council discussed transit budget gaps and park-and-ride planning before voting 5-0 on Mike Woodard's motion to accept the report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excused Absence for Mayor Bell, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. and led a moment of silent meditation. Council unanimously excused Mayor Bill Bell's absence, and roll call confirmed five members present: Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations and Junior Fire Marshals Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council presented proclamations declaring April 22, 2012 as Earth Day in Durham (accepted by Parks and Recreation Director Rhonda Parker), recognizing Durham's Partnership for Children (accepted by Laura Benson), and highlighting children's mental health awareness. Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden also recognized the eighth graduating class of Junior Fire Marshals alongside newly promoted Fire Marshal Edward Reed.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1–14, 17–18)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager and City Attorney reported no priority items, and Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden read the consent agenda items, including board/commission appointments (CAC, EBO Advisory Committee, Human Relations Commission), Community Development loan portfolio report, refunding limited obligation bonds Series 2012A and 2012B (Item 7), FY 2011–2012 CIP budget amendment (Item 8), HUD grant project ordinance (Item 9), 2011 Appearance Commission, Design District Review Team, and Historic Preservation annual reports (Items 10–12), Triangle Expressway scenic byway resolution (Item 13), NC State University downspout contract (Item 14), and taxicab advertising ordinance amendment (Item 17). Council passed the consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Confirmation of Brightwood Lane and Rogers Road Assessment Rolls
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater Manager Ed Venable presented the water main assessment rolls for Brightwood Lane and Rogers Road, reporting written objections from five property owners (Sydney L. and Ruby F. Edwards, Susan N. Gillespie, Carol A. Merritt, Patty O. Harper, and Vance S. Phillips). Staff recommended confirming the remaining assessment rolls and continuing the public hearing on the objected properties to the June 4, 2012 Council meeting. With no public speakers, Council approved staff's recommendation 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Sewer Assessment Rolls and Designing Better Bus Service Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff introduced Item 20 regarding sewer main and outfall assessment rolls before a truncated middle portion of the transcript. Resuming at the Designing Better Bus Service public hearing, transit staff outlined next steps toward a final plan in mid-May and Council action in June pending Orange and Wake County revenue decisions; public speakers advocated modifying Route 1 to serve Central Professional Park (noting $18,000 in annual paratransit costs), adding bus shelters and sidewalks on Cook Road, improving ACCESS/paratransit service, and extending the free Bull City Connector to Northeast Central Durham. Council Members Catotti, Woodard, and Schewel questioned staff and the City Manager on on-time performance, public outreach, delegated route-adjustment flexibility, closing the transit budget gap by May 21, and park-and-ride lot funding before voting 5-0 on Woodard's motion to accept the report.

votes.item_title: Excuse Absence of Mayor Bill Bell
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote of the five members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden noted Mayor Bill Bell requested an excused absence.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Confirmation of Brightwood Lane and Rogers Road Water Main Assessment Rolls (Excluding Objections)
votes.notes: Passed 5-0 after closed public hearing with no speakers.
votes.discussion_detail: Confirmed assessment rolls except for five objecting properties and referred those objections to the June 4, 2012 Council meeting.

votes.item_title: Accept Report on Designing Better Bus Service Draft Plan
votes.notes: Passed 5-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the public hearing and Council questioning on transit budget gaps, route flexibility, and park-and-ride capital plans, Mike Woodard moved to accept the report.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 5, 2012 Durham City Council Work Session, presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, Council acted unanimously on all procedural motions—accepting the City Manager's priority items, setting the upcoming regular meeting agenda, and entering closed session—with no split or contested votes taken. During agenda review, Council members raised questions about whether supporting the NC Turnpike Authority's scenic byway application for the Triangle Expressway could preempt future local sign or billboard ordinances, and discussed adding plastic-bag landfill restrictions to the legislative agenda. Following a briefing on the Designing Better Bus Service draft plan and a truncated middle segment, Council held an extended review of the Southside revitalization project and Item 6, the Master Development Agreement with McCormick Baron Salazar Development Inc. After Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and developer representatives discussed a potential $673,000–$675,000 budget gap tied to NC Housing Finance Agency reserve cuts and pending contractor and equity pricing, Council Member Diane Catotti advocated waiting until firm numbers arrived in one to three weeks, and Item 6 was referred back to the administration alongside Items 15 and 16.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and City Manager Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order at 1:06 p.m. The City Manager presented priority items: holding Item 6 (McCormick Baron Salazar Master Development Agreement) until after the 2:30 p.m. Item 18 Southside update, referring Items 15 and 16 (2010 repaving project amendments lacking backup materials) back to the administration, and scheduling Item 26 (Designing Better Bus Service) at 1:00 p.m. Council approved the priority items unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Scenic Byway / Plastic Bag Discussions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk read consent and public hearing items (Items 1–25), including refunding limited obligation bonds Series 2012A/2012B, HUD grants, historic and appearance annual reports, taxicab advertising, assessment rolls, GO refunding bonds, voluntary annexation, the FY 2012–2013 Annual Action Plan, and the Durham Comprehensive Plan update. Council members discussed requesting state delegation action on plastic bags in landfills and questioned whether supporting the Triangle Expressway scenic byway designation (Item 13) would allow state rules to override local Durham County sign regulations.

agenda_items.title: Designing Better Bus Service Draft Plan Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Triangle Transit staff presented a briefing on the Designing Better Bus Service draft plan currently out for public comment, ahead of the scheduled Council public hearing. No formal vote was taken.

agenda_items.title: Southside Redevelopment Update and McCormick Baron Salazar Master Development Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, Council reviewed Phase 1 financing risks, capital market assumptions, and Exhibit C budget subtotals ($15.67 million and $796,000) with Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and McCormick Baron Salazar representatives. Staff detailed a potential $673,000–$675,000 budget gap resulting from NC Housing Finance Agency reductions to lease-up reserves and attorney fees, noting contractor pricing was expected within 10 days and equity pricing within three weeks. meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 2, 2012 Regular City Council Meeting, presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with six members present and Howard Clement III excused 6-0, Council approved the consent agenda (excluding Items 13, 14, and 15) and three pulled consent items by unanimous 6-0 votes, while splitting 5-1 on Item 25 (an economic development incentive agreement). On Item 25, following City Attorney advice that the agreement would withstand legal challenge under North Carolina economic development statutes, Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Mike Woodard voted Aye, while Council Member Steve Schewel cast the lone Nay vote. Council also issued proclamations for National Public Safety 911 Communications Officers Week and Fair Housing Month, and held a public hearing on Harvard Avenue assessment rolls (Item 19). On the pulled consent items, Council unanimously approved amending City Code Section 38-21 regarding alcohol in city parks and buildings (Item 13), approved the ~$9.2 million American Tobacco Trail construction award while directing staff to review ex-offender hiring requests (Item 15), and received the Dunwitty subdivision street repair report (Item 14) while asking staff to evaluate residents' claims against the City's broader 60-neighborhood failed-subdivision policy.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excused Absence, and Ceremonial Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:04 p.m. and Eugene Brown led the pledge. Mayor Bell presented proclamations for National Public Safety 911 Communications Officers Week (accepted by David Gay and Emergency Communications Director James Soukup) and Fair Housing Month (accepted by Human Relations Manager Delirah Dawson).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 13, 14, and 15)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk presented no priority items. After reading the consent agenda—covering minutes, board attendance and Open Space & Trails appointments, the February 2012 bid report, street acceptances, Brightwood/Rogers assessment rolls, Designing Better Bus Service public hearing notice, leave-reporting audit, FY 2012–2013 budget development guidelines, emergency dispatch protocols, two-thirds bond findings resolution, facility roof design, solid waste disposal amendment, NCDOT transportation planning grant, and landfill gas agreement—Council pulled Items 13, 14, and 15 and approved the remaining consent agenda 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Confirmation of Harvard Avenue Assessment Rolls
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater Manager Ed Venable presented assessment rolls for curb, gutter, paving, and water/sewer laterals on Harvard Avenue, noting property owners objected in order to verify payment responsibility with their closing attorney. Staff recommended confirming the rolls except for the objecting property and continuing that hearing to a future meeting; the transcript truncates before the vote.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement (Split Vote)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, the City Attorney advised Council that the proposed agreement (identified on the April 2 agenda during the March 22 work session as the economic development incentive agreement with Self-Help Venture Fund) would hold up in court under North Carolina economic development statutes. One Council member remarked that his wife had taught in Durham Public Schools for 16 years and he might be 'sleeping on the couch' for his vote, but believed he was doing the right thing. The item passed 5-1 with Steve Schewel voting No.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: City Code Section 38-21 Amendment (Alcohol in Parks and City Buildings)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Victoria Peterson cited Durham Police Department data showing 1,294 DWI arrests and 43 liquor-law violations from 2009–2011 to oppose allowing alcohol and wine at events in city parks and buildings. Following her remarks, Council approved Item 13 by a 6-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: American Tobacco Trail Construction Award and Contract Amendments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater Manager Ed Venable confirmed the American Tobacco Trail project totaled approximately $9.2 million. Victoria Peterson urged Council to tie the City's ex-offenders program (noting roughly $70,000 in current funding) and local resident hiring to the $9.2 million contract; Mayor Bell asked staff to review the hiring request, and Council approved Item 15 by a 6-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Street Repairs on Dunwitty Subdivision
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members debated whether Dunwitty subdivision should be treated individually or under a comprehensive policy for up to 60 potentially failed or struggling developments, noting the first six developments alone would cost $345,000 at 100% city funding (potentially over $3 million across 60). Council Member Steve Schewel reported meeting with neighbors alongside Mike Woodard and forwarding a resident memo questioning whether insufficient/expired developer bonds made Dunwitty exceptional; staff agreed to review the memo and report back in two weeks. Council voted 6-0 to receive the report with the added discussion before adjourning at 10:22 p.m.

votes.notes: Passed 6-0.

votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved ordinance amendment after public comments from Victoria Peterson raising DWI and liquor-law crime statistics.

votes.item_title: Item 15: American Tobacco Trail Construction Award and Contract Amendments
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved ~$9.2 million American Tobacco Trail contract award while asking staff to review ex-offender and local hiring concerns raised by Victoria Peterson.

votes.item_title: Item 14: Receive Report on Dunwitty Subdivision Street Repairs
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 22, 2012 Durham City Council Work Session, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presided in the excused absence of Mayor Bill Bell, with all procedural motions—excusing absences, accepting the City Manager's priority item (Item 25: Self-Help Venture Fund economic development incentive agreement), and setting the April 2 regular meeting agenda—passing unanimously by voice vote with no split votes. During citizen matters, a resident criticized anti-fluoridation misinformation, while taxicab industry representatives (ABC Cab and Durham Best) urged FY 2012–2013 budget funding to enforce city ordinances against unlicensed shuttles operating as taxis without background checks; Deputy City Manager Wanda Page confirmed staff was preparing a cost-effective budget initiative. Council then spent over an hour debating Item 14 (Dunwitty subdivision street repairs) and broader failed-subdivision liability across roughly 60 neighborhoods, weighing city oversight responsibility, ongoing surety bond mediation (for Ravenstone and Stonehill), and options to accelerate contracting pending July 1 budget adoption. Council also received Open Space and Trails Commission ballot tallies before setting the April 2 agenda and adjourning at 2:31 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excused Absences, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order at 1:00 p.m. Council unanimously excused Mayor Bill Bell (attending a metro meeting) and Council Member Howard Clement III (under the standing resolution). The City Manager added supplemental Item 25 (economic development incentive agreement between the City of Durham and Self-Help Venture Fund) for the April 2 agenda, which Council accepted unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review for April 2, 2012 Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk read consent and public hearing items (Items 1–25), including Brightwood/Rogers assessment rolls, Designing Better Bus Service public hearing notice, leave audit, FY 2012–2013 budget guidelines, emergency dispatch protocols, two-thirds bond findings resolution, facility roof design, Section 38-21 ordinance, Dunwitty street repairs (Item 14, pulled), American Tobacco Trail construction award (Item 15, for which a Council member requested an email project timetable), solid waste and landfill gas amendments, Harvard Avenue assessment rolls, zoning map changes, and citizen matters.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters: Water Fluoridation and Taxicab/Shuttle Ordinance Enforcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen speaker Corey Skirmer noted anti-fluoridation websites used out-of-context 1930s AMA quotes while omitting the AMA's September 2010 endorsement of fluoridation. Representatives of ABC Cab and Durham Best urged funding to enforce the city's taxi/shuttle ordinance, reporting unregulated shuttles picking up passengers around Duke nightlife without annual background checks or inspections; Deputy City Manager Wanda Page confirmed Transportation, Police, and Fleet Maintenance were developing a FY 2012–2013 budget initiative for committee review.

agenda_items.title: Failed and Struggling Developments: Dunwitty Subdivision Street Repairs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council spent more than an hour reviewing street repair issues in Dunwitty subdivision (Clover Hill Place) alongside items 13 and 14, where residents faced seven years of raised manholes and unsatisfactory street patching after developer default and uncollected/expired bonds. Council members debated the City's oversight role versus developer culpability across approximately 60 failed developments, received an update from the City Attorney's Office on surety mediation scheduled for the 25th (for Ravenstone and Stonehill subdivisions), and asked staff to explore initiating procurement paperwork before July 1 so paving could begin in the fall.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointment Votes and Setting the April 2 Regular Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Open Space and Trails Commission appointment vote counts (five votes and four votes), Council unanimously set the April 2 regular meeting agenda (Consent: Items 1–18 and 28; General Business: Item 29; Public Hearings: Items 19–25) by voice vote. The work session adjourned at 2:31 p.m.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.

meetings.executive_summary: At the February 23, 2012 Durham City Council Work Session, presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, all procedural votes—excusing an absence under the health-related resolution, accepting two City Manager supplemental items (Items 28 and 29), referring January 19 work session minutes back to the City Clerk, and setting the March 5 regular meeting agenda—passed unanimously by voice vote with no split or contested votes. Following tributes to 26-year city employee Melinda Colvin, the City Manager added supplemental Items 28 (Durham Bulls Athletic Park seating change order #2) and 29 (Proactive Rental Inspection Program carryover), and the City Clerk referred Item 1 (January 19 work session minutes) back; both passed unanimously by voice vote.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 9, 2012 Durham City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the Council unanimously suspended its rules and voted by voice vote to support the Durham Public Schools Board of Education in opposing the state charter application for Research Triangle High School due to its ninth-grade algebra lottery prerequisite excluding roughly 19% of DPS students, including high-need, special-needs, and ESL learners. All seven formal procedural and substantive motions during the work session passed unanimously by voice vote, with no split or contested votes taken. Council also heard an extended briefing and discussion on Agenda Item 16 (an ordinance authorizing periodic inspections of rental dwellings and self-certification training, comparing peer programs in Greensboro, Asheville, and Raleigh), received updates from the Senior Assistant City Attorney on the Utilities Commission order in the Duke Energy rate case (including ordered negotiations on street-lighting rates and outages) and Ms. Bennett's small business loan restitution probation hearing, announced board and commission nomination tallies, set the upcoming regular meeting agenda, and voted to enter closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Council Member Comments (Sister City Delegation & Police Academy)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:00 p.m. and had the clerk call the roll. Council Member Mike Woodard welcomed a visiting delegation of three city council (Duma) members and a department head from Durham's sister city, Kostroma, Russia. Another council member thanked the Durham Police Department and administration for recruiting the largest and most diverse police academy class in over 30 years.

agenda_items.title: Resolution / Letter Supporting Durham Public Schools Board Opposition to Research Triangle High School Charter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A council member presented the Durham Public Schools Board of Education's request—also backed by a joint letter from Durham's four state House delegation members (Representatives Michaux, Hall, Luebke, and Wilkins)—for City Council to oppose the charter for Research Triangle High School. The speaker argued that publicly funded charters should not foster resegregation and objected to restricting the school's admission lottery to students who passed algebra by ninth grade, which excludes roughly 19% of DPS students, disproportionately high-need, special-needs, and ESL students. Council unanimously suspended the rules and adopted the motion to support the school board's opposition.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items: City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield noted there would be a public hearing presentation on Agenda Item 16 (periodic rental dwelling inspections), confirmed that the listed closed session on industry location or expansion would not be held, and reminded Council of the next day's budget retreat at Durham Technical Community College and Saturday's Coffee with Council. The City Attorney requested end-of-meeting open-session updates on the Duke Energy rate case and small business loan collections plus a closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation. The City Clerk noted Durham County Board of Elections representative Michael Perry was present for questions on Item 2 (2011 municipal elections bill).

agenda_items.title: Agenda Overview and Item 16: Ordinance Authorizing Periodic Inspections of Rental Dwellings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell walked through the upcoming agenda, including Item 1 (minutes), Item 2 (2011 elections bill), Item 13 (topographic data contract), Item 14 (Triangle J Council of Governments contract for B. Everett Jordan Reservoir Phase 2 regional water supply planning), Item 15 (paving and water/sewer lateral assessments), Item 16 (periodic rental dwelling inspections ordinance), and Item 17 (Cree Silicon Campus North zoning map change). Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, discussion on Item 16 continued through 01:24:45 covering one-year eligibility for self-certification training, handling approximately 1,600 to 1,700 annual Durham One Call complaints, avoiding assumptions that all issues stem from bad landlords, and how Greensboro (RUCO), Asheville, and Raleigh adjusted rental inspection and registration fee programs under new state legislation.

agenda_items.title: City Attorney Updates: Duke Energy Rate Case and Small Business Loan Restitution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A Senior Assistant City Attorney reported that Durham's post-hearing comments in the Duke Energy rate case—supported by 11 letters including the North Carolina League of Municipalities' first utility-rate support letter and 10 other cities—helped secure a variance from the stipulated agreement ordering Duke Energy, Durham, and Public Staff to negotiate on costly street-lighting schedules and streetlight outage billing, even as the Utilities Commission approved a 7.21% across-the-board increase (over $2.69 million annually for water and sewer electricity). She also reported that in a probation violation hearing on Ms. Bennett's small business loan restitution, the court found a willful violation and continued probation with stern warnings to increase restitution payments. Council and staff also briefly discussed landfill gas recovery and digester gas energy generation.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Nominations, Agenda Setting, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ballot tallies were read for appointments to the Citizens Advisory Committee (5 votes), Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission (6 votes), Human Relations Commission (Richard Ford, 5 votes), and Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority (6 votes). Council then voted unanimously to set the regular meeting agenda with Items 1–14 on Consent and Items 15–17 on General Business Agenda Public Hearings, and voted unanimously to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Suspension of Rules for Immediate Action on Charter School Opposition Motion
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('All in favor of the motion indicate by saying aye... those opposed, the motion passes unanimously'). Individual roll-call votes were not taken.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved and seconded following a council member's request to take action that day in support of the Durham Public Schools Board of Education.

votes.notes: Passed by unanimous voice vote ('All in favor of the motion indicate by saying aye... those opposed. Motion passes'). Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Council approved issuing a resolution/letter supporting the DPS Board of Education's opposition to chartering Research Triangle High School due to its ninth-grade algebra lottery prerequisite.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the City Manager's priority announcements regarding the Item 16 presentation, cancellation of the listed economic development closed session, and upcoming budget retreat.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 6, 2012 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell (with Council Member Howard Clement III absent), Mayor Bell delivered his 10th Annual State of the City Address following an 18-minute 2011 Year-in-Review video. Mayor Bell highlighted voter approval of the half-cent transit sales tax, record DATA transit ridership, emergency communications and policing technology, job announcements totaling over 4,400 positions across more than 70 companies, an $8.8 million HUD loan guarantee for the Southside and Rolling Hills redevelopment (projected to leverage nearly $49 million in public and private investment), and proposals to tighten gun-crime bond guidelines, restrict illegal firearm discharges within city limits, hold joint meetings with the Durham Housing Authority, and establish a dedicated local revenue stream for mixed-income affordable housing. The Council also held the first public hearing on the FY 2012–2013 Annual Action Plan, where 12 speakers addressed homelessness services, federal CDBG funding cuts from $4 million to $2.4 million, and housing bond and capital budget transparency, and Council Member Steve Schewel voiced support for a dedicated 'penny for housing' funding stream. No formal votes or split or contested votes were recorded in the available transcript digest (the middle segment between 00:42:34 and 01:18:17 was truncated).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Pledge of Allegiance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order and had the clerk call the roll, confirming Mayor Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, and Council Members Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard present, while noting Council Member Howard Clement III had called to advise he could not attend. Council Member Eugene Brown led the Pledge of Allegiance.

agenda_items.title: Mayor's 10th Annual State of the City Address and 2011 Year-in-Review Video
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell introduced an 18-minute 2011 Year-in-Review video spotlighting passage of the half-cent transit sales tax, record DATA ridership and the Bull City Connector, public safety initiatives (text-to-911 trial, aerial imagery, DPD firearms testing lab), recycling events, and a new performance-management website. In his address, Bell prioritized reducing gun violence—urging revised bail/bond guidelines and directing the City Attorney to draft General Assembly legislation regarding illegal firearm discharges in city limits—and outlined affordable housing goals including HUD's $8.8 million loan guarantee for Southside/Rolling Hills, 174 units across five joint Durham Housing Authority projects, regular joint Council–DHA board meetings, and a dedicated revenue stream for mixed-income affordable housing, alongside 4,400+ announced jobs.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2012–2013 Annual Action Plan (Housing & Community Development Needs)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, staff explained the Annual Action Plan timeline leading to a draft funding chart for a 30-day public comment period and a second public hearing in late April. Twelve public speakers addressed property maintenance repair costs, continued funding for Durham Interfaith Hospitality Network (IHN) and House of Hope, gun violence concerns, federal CDBG cuts reducing expected annual funds from $4 million to $2.4 million, and calls for a housing capital improvement budget, clearer HUD repayment/Southside disclosures, and a local housing bond referendum. After Mayor Bell closed the public hearing at 01:56:16, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden shared JobLink Career Center ex-offender networking details, Council Member Steve Schewel endorsed a dedicated 'penny for housing' funding stream and praised DHA's operational turnaround, and another council member also backed dedicated housing funding and management reporting before adjournment at 9:03 p.m.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 19, 2012 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden (with Mayor Bill Bell excused and Council Member Howard Clement III also absent and excused at the end of the session), the Council received briefings on NCDOT's I-40 corridor Bus-on-Shoulder pilot program and a multi-phase Main Street waterline and bridge replacement project between Buchanan Boulevard and Broad Street. Staff explained that the 240-day waterline project would reduce Main Street from four lanes to two lanes starting around February 12, followed by a bridge replacement contract that will fully close Main Street, detour transit onto Buchanan, Markham, Broad, or Ninth Street, and reopen Main Street as a three-lane section with striped bike lanes and dedicated left-turn lanes. Both formal procedural votes taken at the end of the session—accepting the City Manager's priority item/agenda and excusing Council Member Howard Clement III—passed unanimously by voice vote, with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Priority Item, and Legislative Dinner Cost-Sharing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order at 1:01 p.m. and noted Mayor Bill Bell's request for an excused absence; Council Members Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard attended. The City Manager added a priority briefing from Transportation staff (Mark Ahrendsen) on the planned partial and temporary/permanent closing of Main Street between Buchanan and Broad. Council members also informally agreed to pay only the City's portion of a joint dinner with the six-member legislative delegation and County Commissioners.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Overview and Citizen Matters
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The chair noted Item 6 (2012–2013 Annual Action Plan needs public hearing) and invited Citizen Matters speakers. Citizens spoke regarding resident access to the Recreation Advisory Committee, welfare and civil rights issues, homelessness, and historical racial discrimination by local insurance companies.

agenda_items.title: NCDOT I-40 Corridor and Bus-on-Shoulder Pilot Program Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A presenter briefed Council on NCDOT's appointment of a dedicated corridor executive for I-40 and described a proposed Bus-on-Shoulder pilot program modeled on systems in Minnesota, San Diego, Illinois, and roughly 12 states. The speaker explained that the pilot segment was chosen specifically because it offers continuous 10-foot shoulders without pinch points (avoiding locations like the Crabtree Creek Bridge) and noted discussions with law enforcement regarding patrol and safety.

agenda_items.title: Main Street Waterline Replacement, Bridge Replacement, and Three-Lane Reconfiguration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff briefed Council on Phase 2 of the waterline project replacing a 24-inch line from Rutherford Street to Peabody Street (with Phases 3 and 4 extending past Brightleaf to the eastern tank), which will narrow Main Street from four lanes to two lanes with Jersey barriers starting around February 12 for a 240-day contract (targeted for 7 months) and confine intersection crossings to nights and weekends. Staff then reviewed the follow-on bridge replacement project—opening bids in April and awarding the contract in June—that will fully close Main Street, detouring buses onto Buchanan, Markham, and Broad or Ninth Street before reopening Main Street as a three-lane cross-section with left-turn lanes/signals at Buchanan and Broad and four-foot striped bike lanes designed for roughly 12,000 vehicles per day.

agenda_items.title: Acceptance of Priority Item / Agenda and Excusal of Council Member Clement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the close of the work session, Council voted unanimously by voice vote to accept the City Manager's priority item/agenda and then voted unanimously by voice vote to excuse Council Member Howard Clement III from the session before adjourning.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Manager's Priority Item / Agenda
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('All in favor indicate by saying aye').
votes.discussion_detail: Formalized acceptance of the City Manager's priority item on the Main Street closure update.

votes.item_title: Excusal of Council Member Howard Clement III from Work Session
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('all in favor... sign aye... Opposed...').
votes.discussion_detail: Moved and seconded to excuse Council Member Howard Clement III from the January 19, 2012 work session.
