meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 17, 2012 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden—with Mayor Bill Bell (away on city business) and Council Member Howard Clement III excused by a 5-0 vote—the five present members (Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard) unanimously approved all five recorded roll-call votes, with no split or contested votes observed in the transcript digest. Council approved the Consent Agenda (5-0) excluding Item 10, heard divided public comment on General Business Agenda Item 6 regarding Old North Durham Park stormwater/drainage repairs and field specifications (with Old North Durham Neighborhood Association President Peter Katz supporting the resolution and civil rights attorney Alex Hurley urging delay on behalf of the Durham Coalition for Urban Justice; the middle portion of the transcript containing the remainder of Item 6 was truncated), and unanimously adopted (5-0) both the Unified Development Ordinance Compact Design District text amendment (TC100005, capping S2 height at 45 feet and requiring minimum residential density for projects 200,000 sq ft or greater) and the Ninth Street Compact Design District zoning map change (Z100017, expanding the S1/S2 buffer to 120 feet along Green Street). At the end of the meeting, Council also approved pulled Consent Item 10 (5-0) awarding the Andrea Avenue elevated water storage tank construction contract after addressing questions from resident Victoria Peterson.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Silent Meditation, Pledge, Roll Call, and Excused Absences
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m., reminded attendees not to block views with signs, led silent meditation, and asked Council Member Eugene Brown to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll call confirmed five members present (Cole-McFadden, Brown, Catotti, Schewel, Woodard), and Council voted 5-0 to excuse Mayor Bill Bell (away on city business) and Council Member Howard Clement III.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items, Code of Ethics Oath, and Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager and City Attorney had no priority items, and an appointee subscribed to the City of Durham Code of Ethics. Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden read the Consent Agenda—including minutes, the 300 East Main Street LLC building improvement grant amendment, vehicle bids, Church Street Parking Deck repairs, the NC Tennis Association Raise the Net grant, a Culbreth/Culp Arbor irrigation license agreement, railroad wireline agreements for W. Chapel Hill and S. Roxboro underpass lighting, and the water treatment plant residuals master plan—and Council approved the consent slate 5-0 with Item 10 pulled by Victoria Peterson.

agenda_items.title: General Business Agenda Item 6: Old North Durham Park Drainage and Field Improvements Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council granted three minutes each to one proponent and one opponent: Old North Durham Neighborhood Association President Peter Katz supported the resolution to fix seven-year-old stormwater/drainage issues and replace rocky topsoil for soccer while protecting a nearby fitness center and coordinating with the Ellerbe Creek Watershed Association, CPSC, and neighbors; civil rights attorney Alex Hurley (with a Spanish translator, representing the Durham Coalition for Urban Justice and referencing the NAACP) sought additional time and warned against private-investment displacement of low-income residents of color. Parks and Recreation Director Rhonda Parker clarified how the 2005 Resolution 9281 directives (330x180-foot field, Central Park School playground equipment, pedestrian access) differed from the new resolution addressing failing, cracking storm drainage pipes and constant flooding; the remainder of the discussion/action fell within the truncated middle portion of the transcript (with Council Member Mike Woodard later noting at 01:25:09 that Council had handled both five-year-old issues that night).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote recorded in digest (truncated)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment for Compact Design District (TC100005)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after the truncated middle section, Ninth Street merchant Carol Anderson (728 Ninth Street) and another speaker supported the staff-proposed text amendment. Planning staff clarified that the amendment establishes a 45-foot height limit in the Support 2 (S2) subdistrict per the Ninth Street planning consensus and requires projects of 200,000 square feet or greater in S2 to provide minimum residential density under UDO paragraph 6.12.4a3a. Council closed the public hearing and approved the staff recommendation 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change — Ninth Street Compact Design District (Case Z100017)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the rezoning tapering development intensity from the proposed rail transit station core toward surrounding neighborhoods and protecting historic Ninth Street. Tom Miller (Watts Hospital–Hillandale Neighborhood Association) and merchant Carol Anderson urged approval of staff's map, noting the S1/S2 boundary adjustment to a 120-foot depth at Green Street replaced 15 committed elements from the prior development plan that the City Attorney advised could not survive rezoning after talks with property owners stalled. Council Member Mike Woodard praised the hybridization of form-based and use-based zoning around transit stops while calling for future discussion on residential incentives and mixed-use definitions before Council approved the rezoning 5-0.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Victoria Peterson (P.O. Box 101, Durham) questioned the minority-business partnering arrangement on the Andrea Avenue elevated water storage tank contract, and staff (Mr. Page) responded. Council moved, seconded, and approved Item 10 by a 5-0 vote, then congratulated Finance Controller David Hickman on his Durham City-County MLK Humanitarian Award and adjourned.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 5, 2012 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, Council unanimously excused Council Member Howard Clement III due to illness and heard intense public comment demanding reaffirmation of the 2005 directive for a full 330-by-180-foot athletic field at Old North Durham Park alongside Council Member Steve Schewel's proposed resolution recommending the park not serve as a primary site for league play. Council also reviewed the City-County Electric Vehicle Charging Station Plan (discussing metering and time limits) and received a comprehensive Solid Waste Management consultant report (CHA) recommending a Phase 2 rate study and evaluation of enterprise-fee versus property-tax funding ahead of FY 2013–2014 budgeting. All seven formal voice votes—including priority items, referral of the December 19, 2011 minutes, suspension of the rules, adoption of Resolution B amending the Audit Services Oversight Committee bylaws to remove the Mayor's mandatory ex officio seat so Council Member Steve Schewel could serve, and setting the regular meeting agenda—passed unanimously with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excusal of Council Member Clement, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order and Council unanimously excused Council Member Howard Clement III due to illness. Council unanimously accepted the City Manager's priority presentations on Item 2 (City-County Electric Vehicle Charging Station Plan) and Item 6 (Old North Durham Park maintenance update), the City Attorney's priority item on Audit Services Oversight Committee (ASOC) bylaws changes, and the City Clerk's request to refer the December 19, 2011 minutes back to the Clerk's Office.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Citizen Matters, and Item 6: Old North Durham Park Update & Schewel Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell previewed the agenda—including the Water Treatment Plant Residuals Master Plan (Item 11), Solid Waste Disposal Plan report (Item 12), Guess Road Apartments plan amendment and rezoning (Items 13–14), and Compact Design District / Ninth Street rezoning items (Items 15–16). During Citizen Matters, speakers criticized six-year delays on the 2005 directive guaranteeing a 330-by-180-foot athletic field at Old North Durham Park and alleged exclusion of low-income residents of color from prior DPR and Friends of Old North Durham Park meetings. Staff reviewed plans to use Irwin Park parcel sale proceeds for soil improvement and Bermuda grass, and Council Member Steve Schewel distributed a draft resolution proposing the park not be a primary site for league play so it would not need multi-month turf-recovery closures.

agenda_items.title: Item 2: City-County Electric Vehicle Charging Station Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, Council concluded discussion on the City-County Electric Vehicle Charging Station Plan. Members discussed low initial usage expectations, limiting charging time via two- or four-hour metering to avoid restricting public parking spaces, regional sustainability director coordination, and Green Business Council recognition.

agenda_items.title: Item 12: Solid Waste Management Consultant Report on Comprehensive Disposal Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Robert Williams (standing in for Solid Waste Director Donald Long) and consultant CHA presented Phase 1 findings and a Phase 2 roadmap for Durham's solid waste system. Topics included regional landfill capacity within a 100-mile radius (three private facilities), tonnage-based comparisons with Wake County, educational diversion programs such as backyard composting, and a proposed Phase 2 rate study evaluating cost-of-service alignment across curbside, yard waste, bulky pickup, and leaf collection—including whether solid waste should move from the property-tax operating budget to a dedicated user fee—targeting Q1 RFPs and Q4 implementation.

agenda_items.title: Audit Services Oversight Committee (ASOC) Bylaws Amendment (Resolution B)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Attorney presented a memo from the Audit Services Department Director proposing to strike the bylaw provision designating the Mayor as an ex officio voting member of the Audit Services Oversight Committee, allowing any two Council members to serve. Mayor Bell noted he was stepping off the committee and Council Member Steve Schewel was ready to join. Council unanimously suspended the rules and adopted Resolution B (effective upon passage).

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously voted to set the upcoming regular meeting agenda with Items 1, 3, 4, 5, and 7–11 on Consent, Item 6 (including staff evaluation of Council Member Steve Schewel's Old North Durham Park resolution) on the General Business Agenda, and Items 13–16 on General Business Agenda Public Hearings.

votes.notes: Passed by voice vote ('all in favor... say aye').
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Bell noted Council Member Howard Clement III was not feeling well and requested to be excused.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Manager Priority Items
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Added presentations on Item 2 (electric vehicle charging station plan) and Item 6 (Old North Durham Park maintenance activities).

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Attorney Priority Item (ASOC Bylaws Memo)
votes.notes: Passed by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Added the Audit Services Department Director's memo regarding changes to the Audit Services Oversight Committee bylaws to the end of the meeting.

votes.item_title: Referral of December 19, 2011 City Council Minutes Back to City Clerk
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the City Clerk's priority request to refer the December 19, 2011 meeting minutes back to the Clerk's Office.

votes.item_title: Suspension of Rules for Immediate Vote on ASOC Bylaws Resolution
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended Council rules to act immediately on the Audit Services Oversight Committee bylaws amendment.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Resolution B Amending Audit Services Oversight Committee (ASOC) Bylaws
votes.notes: Passed by voice vote ('Motion passes').
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted Resolution B (effective upon passage) removing the requirement that the Mayor serve as an ex officio voting member of ASOC so any two Council members may serve.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Set the agenda including staff evaluation of Council Member Steve Schewel's Old North Durham Park resolution under GBA Item 6.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the brief January 3, 2012 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell—with six members present (Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard) and Howard Clement III absent—all three formal roll-call votes passed unanimously 6-0, with no split or contested votes. Council unanimously approved adding Supplemental Item 17 (6-0), passed the Consent Agenda covering minutes, board appointments, the November 2011 bid report, and an annexation consideration resolution (6-0), and following a public hearing approved a $150,000 performance-based economic development incentive contract with Moran Foods Inc., d/b/a Save-A-Lot (6-0). The incentive leverages over $1.9 million in private investment to renovate the vacant former Winn-Dixie building at 812 Liberty Street in Northeast Central Durham into a 12,202-square-foot grocery store creating 13 full-time equivalent jobs.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge, Roll Call, and Priority Item
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order, led silent meditation, and asked Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden to lead the Pledge of Allegiance; roll call recorded Bell, Cole-McFadden, Brown, Catotti, Schewel, and Woodard present, and Cole-McFadden led the chamber in singing Happy Birthday to the Mayor. The City Manager added Supplemental Item 17 (Save-A-Lot incentive contract public hearing), which Council accepted 6-0, and Mayor Bell distributed proposed City Council subcommittee assignments for member review.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the Consent Agenda items, including approval of City Council minutes (Item 1), appointments to the Durham City-County Appearance Commission (Item 2), Environmental Affairs Board (Item 4), Durham Open Space and Trails Commission (Item 5), and Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission (Item 6), the November 2011 Bid Report (Item 7), and a resolution of consideration for annexation of multiple sites surrounded by existing city limits (Item 9). meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 20, 2011 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with five members answering roll call (Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard), the Council unanimously (5-0) approved the City Manager's priority items, suspended the rules to act immediately, and approved (5-0) an assignment request from Minor League Baseball, Inc. for the Durham Athletic Park operating agreement while referring a Guess Road zoning map change (Z1100023) and a Human Relations Commission appointment (Item 3) back to staff. During Citizen Matters, residents raised concerns regarding water fluoridation dosage reductions to 0.7 ppm and urged preservation of the full-size athletic field and public input process at Old North Durham Park. The bulk of the session focused on an update on failed and struggling developments, where Engineering and Stormwater staff presented revised construction security policies negotiated with local homebuilders and funding options for unfinished neighborhood streets and stormwater infrastructure—prompting homeowners from Stonewall/Stonehill Estates to oppose special property assessments while the City Attorney noted active discovery in Stonehill and Ravenstone litigation. The Council concluded by unanimously (5-0) setting the January 3, 2012 agenda.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order following a closed session and requested roll call, confirming five members present (Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard). Mayor Bell noted he might need to depart around 2:30 p.m. for a funeral while confirming a quorum would remain. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items to vote immediately on Item 8 (Durham Athletic Park operating agreement assignment) and refer Item 11 (2125 Guess Road rezoning) back to administration.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Referral of Human Relations Commission Appointment (Item 3)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent and departmental items, including Item 3 (Human Relations Commission appointment, which was pulled and referred back for re-advertisement), the November 2011 Finance bid report, annexation considerations for multiple enclaves, and the Item 11 Guess Road zoning map change (Z1100023, referred back).

agenda_items.title: Item 8: Minor League Baseball, Inc. Assignment Request for Durham Athletic Park Operating Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting on the City Manager's priority request, Council first voted unanimously to suspend the rules to take immediate action at the work session. Council then unanimously approved the assignment request from Minor League Baseball, Inc. for the Durham Athletic Park operating agreement.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters: Water Fluoridation and Old North Durham Park Athletic Field
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speaker Cory Stromer addressed water fluoridation and cited IQ studies, prompting staff clarification that Durham is following updated EPA and HHS guidance reducing fluoride dosage by roughly 30% from 1.0 to 0.7 ppm. Subsequent speakers including Robin Jacobs of the Eno River Association criticized the public input process and urged the city to preserve the full-size athletic field at Old North Durham Park per a 2005 Council resolution, with staff estimating Parks and Recreation recommendations would reach Council in late January or February.

agenda_items.title: Item 10: Update on Failed and Struggling Developments and Construction Security Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Works Engineering and Stormwater staff (including Ed Menel and Robert Jordan) presented proposed construction security reforms developed with the Home Builders Association of Durham, Chatham, and Orange counties, including warranty security and lowering certain upfront sidewalk bonding requirements as lots build out. Staff also presented infrastructure completion cost scenarios—estimating $340,000 to $375,000 in city exposure—and homeowner assessment options, prompting Stonewall/Stonehill Estates resident Gary Capital to protest assessments on homeowners living with unfinished roads for four years; the City Attorney added that Stonehill and Ravenstone litigation is in early discovery with 6,000 pages served.

meetings.executive_summary: At the December 19, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with six members present, the Council first approved an excused absence for Council Member Howard Clement III on a 5-1 split vote, with Ayes from Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Diane Catotti, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard and a Nay from Eugene Brown. Following announcements noting the reopening of the ADA-accessible City Hall Plaza, Council unanimously (6-0) approved the consent agenda, the voluntary annexation of the Cree Silicon Campus North property, and four downtown GS 158-7.1 economic development building improvement grants totaling $277,000 in public investment across Hunt Street, West Parrish Street, Foster Street, and West Geer Street (prior to a mid-transcript truncation). meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 8, 2011 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with five members answering roll call (Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Steve Schewel, and Mike Woodard), Council approved an excused absence by unanimous voice vote and adopted the City Manager's priority schedule (5-0) for presentations on compact design UDO text amendments, the Bull City Connector first-year report, and the regional rail transit Locally Preferred Alternative (LPA). Before turning to the agenda, Council Member Mike Woodard flagged General Assembly House Bill 650 allowing firearms in parks and asked staff to draft a resolution protecting residents in open spaces and greenways. During Citizen Matters, speakers requested a non-binding resolution opposing the Citizens United Supreme Court decision and challenged ADA-related park construction plans at Old North Durham Park without formal public hearings. Following a truncated middle section, Council reviewed the Durham-Orange and Durham-Wake rail transit corridor LPA ahead of an August 2012 federal New Starts deadline, hearing extensive public testimony urging selection of the C2 alignment over C1 to avoid higher costs and New Hope Creek/Little Creek wetland impacts, before unanimously (5-0) setting the December 19 regular meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excused Absence, and House Bill 650 Firearms in Parks Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order with Bell, Cole-McFadden, Brown, Schewel, and Woodard present, and Council unanimously approved an excused absence motion by voice vote. Council Member Mike Woodard highlighted recent meetings with the City Manager, City Attorney, and Mayor regarding House Bill 650 (firearms in parks and facilities) and requested an expeditious staff recommendation on a protective resolution for city open spaces and greenways.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items and December 19 Draft Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously (5-0) approved the City Manager's priority items scheduling Item 12 (Compact Design District UDO amendment TC1000005), Item 13 (Bull City Connector first-year report), and Item 14 (rail transit Locally Preferred Alternative), while noting Item 26 (Nia Wilson citizen appearance) was cancelled. Staff then read through Items 1–27, spanning grants, Minor DPA naming rights, Cree annexation, downtown economic development incentives, Trinity Academy special use permit and site plan, and the C-Hawk Trail rezoning.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters: Citizens United Resolution Request and Old North Durham Park ADA Compliance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A Durham voter presented a grassroots request for a non-binding resolution supporting a U.S. Constitutional amendment to overturn the Citizens United Supreme Court ruling, citing corporate lobbying and tax figures including Duke Energy. Speaker Fernando LeGros raised concerns over ADA compliance and planned spring construction at Old North Durham Park without adequate public hearings or adherence to Resolution 9281.

agenda_items.title: Item 14: Locally Preferred Alternative (LPA) for Durham-Orange and Durham-Wake Rail Transit Corridor
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle section truncated in the transcript, transit staff presented station-area opportunities (including NC Central University and the VA corridor) and the MPO/TAC decision schedule aiming for a February 8 TAC decision and August 2012 federal New Starts application. Multiple speakers strongly urged Council to favor the C2 alignment over C1, arguing C1 costs $30–$60 million ($44 million midpoint) more, projects lower ridership, creates four times the wetland impact through New Hope Creek/Little Creek bottomlands, and lacks Hillmont's 200 dedicated parking spaces; Council questioned the downside of advancing both C1 and C2 into environmental scoping versus selecting one.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved setting the December 19 regular meeting agenda with consent items 1–11 and 21, no general business action items, and public hearings for Items 15–20 and 22.

meetings.executive_summary: At the December 5, 2011 Organizational and Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the Council opened with six members present (including outgoing Council Member Farad Ali) and unanimously (6-0) approved an excused absence for Howard Clement III. Following certification of the November 2011 municipal election results and farewell remarks from Farad Ali, re-elected Council Member Diane Catotti and newly elected Council Member Steve Schewel were sworn in, after which the newly seated six-member Council unanimously (6-0) confirmed Cora Cole-McFadden as Mayor Pro Tempore and proclaimed December 15, 2011 as Human Rights and Bill of Rights Day. After reading the consent agenda and a mid-transcript truncation, Council heard a police briefing covering firearms availability, concerns about recent General Assembly legislation permitting guns in city parks, and the RAP program. Council then held public hearings and voted unanimously (6-0) to approve both the Wilco Hess rezoning on NC 55 (Z110015) and the 2011 Durham Trails and Greenways Master Plan Update before requesting committee assignment preferences.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the organizational meeting to order with six members present: Bell, Cole-McFadden, Brown, outgoing Council Member Farad Ali, Catotti, and Woodard. Council unanimously (6-0) approved an excused absence for Howard Clement III.

agenda_items.title: 2011 Election Certification, Farewell to Farad Ali, Swearing-In of Diane Catotti and Steve Schewel, and Mayor Pro Tempore Selection
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Elections Director Michael Perry presented the certified November 2011 municipal election abstract, and outgoing Council Member Farad Ali delivered farewell remarks. Re-elected Council Member Diane Catotti and newly elected Council Member Steve Schewel took their oaths of office, Mayor Bell highlighted nearly $500,000 in federal CDBG and HOME housing fund cuts facing the new Council, and the body unanimously (6-0) elected Cora Cole-McFadden as Mayor Pro Tempore.

agenda_items.title: Human Rights and Bill of Rights Day Proclamation and Consent Agenda Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell proclaimed December 15, 2011 as Human Rights and Bill of Rights Day in Durham, marking the ninth year since the city's 2003 Bill of Rights Defense Resolution and Resolution 9046 supporting residents regardless of immigration status. After confirming no priority items from the City Attorney or Clerk, Mayor Bell read the headings of Consent Agenda Items 1–23.

agenda_items.title: Police Briefing on Firearms Availability, State Park-Carry Legislation, and RAP Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion, the Police Chief discussed firearm availability, criticized recent General Assembly legislation permitting guns in city parks even as Durham debates tobacco-free zones, and emphasized the need for informants. Council Member Mike Woodard also asked for details on criteria for the RAP program referenced in an email to the five PAC listservs.

members present (including outgoing council member farad ali) and unanimously (6-0) approved an excused absence for howard clement iii. following certification of the november 2011 municipal election results and farewell remarks from farad ali, re-elected council member diane catotti and newly elected council member steve schewel were sworn in, after which the newly seated six-member council unanimously (6-0) confirmed cora cole-mcfadden as mayor pro tempore and proclaimed december 15, 2011 as human rights and bill of rights day. after reading the consent agenda and a mid-transcript
